We are driving forward the decarbonization of processes by removing barriers to green self-supply of electricity and increasing the use of green hydrogen.
Climate contracts (carbon contracts for difference), which finance the difference between the current CO2 price and the actual CO2 avoidance costs, ensure investment security.
And with quotas for the proportion of CO2-neutral raw materials, we are creating lead markets for CO2-free products.
We particularly want to promote pilot plants for low-emission technologies that are not yet ready for the market.
And where possible, the aim should be for new industrial plants to be built or exported with zero emissions.

In the transformation of the chemical industry, we are focusing on new innovative products, processes and procedures which, in addition to greenhouse gas neutrality, also promote the circular economy, increase efficiency, avoid emissions and waste from the outset and make us independent of fossil raw materials such as crude oil or natural gas.
Sustainable automotive industry
The automotive industry is facing huge upheavals.
The competition for the zero-emission and digital car of the future is ongoing worldwide.
After years of stagnation, the industry in Germany has finally started to move forward.
We now need determination and cooperation to create sustainable jobs and climate-friendly added value in the automotive industry.
The transformation of the automotive industry into an important player for sustainable mobility is necessary.
Politicians have a central role to play here; they must set the framework and shape the transformation process.
One thing is clear: the combustion engine has no future.
We only want to register new zero-emission cars from 2030.

We also want to set standards in the automotive industry for a circular economy and climate-neutral production as well as decarbonization in the steel sector so that the ecological footprint of vehicles becomes ever smaller.

We are supporting this transformation with research and innovation funding for all technology options and want to promote the rapid development of the charging station infrastructure and the market ramp-up of zero-emission vehicles as part of a cost-neutral bonus-malus system.
We want to leverage the potential of new mobility services and autonomous driving for the industrial location and also for climate protection and road safety.
It is also important to look at the opportunities for value creation and jobs in the mobility transition: from new jobs in public transport to vehicle production.
It is also important that Germany and Europe quickly catch up in battery cell production.

For the next generation of batteries in particular, which are cheaper and use fewer resources, we want to create our own sustainable battery cell production in Europe, which includes an effective recycling system as well as research and development for the next generation of batteries.
To this end, we rely on clear guidelines for ecological standards and a comprehensive research and funding program.
We want to support the particularly affected car regions with regional transformation dialogs and funds.
In this way, we maintain the value chain in the SME sector and secure local jobs.
We want to support employees in the automotive industry and its suppliers with training opportunities and further education.
Strengthening the European semiconductor industry
A successful and far-sighted industrial policy will only work if a pan-European approach is taken.

A European focus is crucial, particularly with regard to the necessary sectoral structural support, such as the development of a hydrogen infrastructure, solar module and battery cell production or the promotion of the semiconductor industry.
To reduce critical dependencies, we rely on European cooperation with open standards.
EU capacity in the field of semiconductor technology is to be expanded to 20 percent of global production, as proposed by the EU Commission.

This applies above all to those areas in which we already have a strong European position in semiconductor technology for industrial applications or in which particularly dynamic future development is expected, such as renewable energies.
To achieve this, investments along the semiconductor value chain must be increased.
More specialists in daycare centers, after-school care and schools

Educational professionals in daycare centers, after-school care centers and schools bear a great deal of responsibility, as they play a decisive role in shaping children's lives from a very early age.
However, this responsibility is not yet sufficiently reflected in the pay of skilled workers.
For the important work that childcare workers, teachers and other educators do in the education system and in youth welfare, they need a good wage and good working conditions.

We also want to ensure fair training salaries, opportunities for further development and good working conditions with an effective campaign for skilled workers, and training to become a nursery teacher must not be allowed to fail due to school fees.

In order to be able to sustainably overcome the shortage of pedagogical specialists and teachers with well-qualified staff, we want to promote high-quality lateral entry training with a federal-state program, strengthen existing further training and qualification offers and ensure common quality standards.
Right to an all-day place for every primary school child and good learning conditions at secondary schools
Schools should be strong places of education, encounter and inspiration.
To do this, they need motivated specialists, well-equipped, barrier-free rooms and time.
Time for learning and playing together, research and discovery, shared cultural, social and democratic experiences, language and movement development, individual support and supervision.
All-day places in an elementary school or an after-school care center and good learning conditions at secondary schools are important for this.

Our aim is to implement an individual legal entitlement for every primary school child to all-day education and care with quality standards - with sufficient specialist staff in multi-professional teams, stimulating rooms and schoolyards, a healthy lunch and broad-based cooperation with local clubs, music schools and other stakeholders.
We want to support such collaborations financially.
Youth welfare services are an important partner for schools in the organization of all-day schooling, as informal education is essential in addition to school-based learning.
The guiding principle is integrated all-day concepts for comprehensive personal development.
All-day schooling and good secondary schools must be made possible for all children, whether they have disabilities or not.
We are committed to the WHO's physical activity target of reducing physical inactivity among children, young people and adults by 15 percent by 2030.
There should be at least one exercise program to choose from every full day.

The right to integration assistance must apply everywhere - via individual assistance or via a pool solution, whether in all-day schools or in after-school care services provided by youth welfare services.
The working conditions and remuneration of integration assistants should reflect their demanding and responsible work.
Parents of children and young people with disabilities must not incur any additional costs.
The implementation of the legal entitlement will be a tour de force throughout Germany.
This must be reflected in the federal government's contribution to the costs.

In order to support all elementary school on their way to becoming inclusive places of all-day education, we will launch an accompanying program to promote integrated, cross-professional school development and thus support coordination offices.
In the long term, we want to expand school social work and make it an integral part of all-day schooling across the board.
Bringing education up to date
Education in the digital world is much more than imparting knowledge; it is a key to future skills.
Digitalization has changed the way we live, so our way of thinking about school must also change.
Of course, this also includes vocational schools and colleges.

With teachers who place competence orientation at the center of learning, students who learn new content in a playful way, for example through game-based learning, and schools that are optimally equipped for this in terms of technology.
Both the basic technical understanding and the social dimension of digital development must be addressed.
However, the pandemic has shown that the basics are already lacking, even in comparison with other countries.

We want to change this: with modern, data protection-friendly digital equipment and with structures that effectively support schools in digital teaching and learning - with continuous training and further education opportunities for teaching staff and a central place for advice and exchange on education in a digital world.
Full-time administrators are needed to set up and maintain the technical infrastructure at schools.
We want to promote this within the scope of the powers of the federal government.
Together with the federal states, we want to improve the digital training of teachers.
We want tablets and laptops to be a natural learning tool.
Our aim is to enable all pupils to learn in new ways and to prepare them for self-determined and healthy participation in a digitalized world.

To this end, we want to comprehensively promote applications such as open-source and secure learning platforms or video conferencing systems and are committed to implementing the right to erasure of personal data for children.
Future skills such as cooperation, communication, creativity and critical thinking are becoming increasingly relevant.
We want to promote these future skills in the way that makes the most educational sense, whether digital or analog.
This also includes the promotion of STEM subjects in schools.
Digitalization means that education is less location-bound: New scope for supra-regional and international cooperation with educational and cultural institutions is emerging.

In order to implement all of this, we also want to develop the Digital Pact into a genuine joint project on a sustainable and permanent basis - with clear goals and time horizons that are to be achieved jointly within the scope of the respective responsibilities of the federal, state and local governments.
Strengthening education for sustainable development (ESD)
We support the implementation of the UNESCO Education for Sustainable Development program, which aims to promote the integration of ESD in all education networks and at local level worldwide.
ESD must therefore be anchored in all phases and areas of education in accordance with the national ESD action plan.
In order to create incentives for local authorities, local and regional education networks are initiated and supported in cooperation with the federal states.
The federally funded ESD Competence Center is already supporting around 50 of the more than 10,000 municipalities in Germany.
It must be strengthened in order to be able to make offers to more municipalities.
Facilitate naturalization
Nationality ensures a permanent bond of legal equality, participation and belonging.
Anyone born in Germany should receive German citizenship if one of their parents is legally resident in Germany.
Citizenship must not be withdrawn, also as a lesson from the injustice of National Socialism.
For people who have lived here for years and have become part of this society, naturalization should be possible earlier.
After five years of residence in Germany, everyone should be able to apply for naturalization, and an accelerated and simplified naturalization procedure also applies to recognized refugees.
We want to abolish the compulsory option in citizenship law and recognize multiple nationalities.
We want to reverse the erosion of citizenship law and reduce bureaucracy in naturalization procedures.
Obstacles in the clarification of identity that are not in the hands of the naturalized person must not be blamed on them.
We want to make entry unbureaucratic and fair for binational families and couples, regardless of whether they have a marriage certificate or not.
To build a life in Germany, you need long-term prospects.
A modern immigration law for a diverse immigration society
Germany is a country of immigration, but it still lacks an active immigration policy and immigration law that actually promotes immigration and does not make it more complicated.

We want to adopt a modern immigration law that creates new access routes for educational and labour migration - including for people who cannot prove their talents and skills through formal or recognized educational qualifications - that offers transparent, unbureaucratic and fair procedures and takes global and regional necessities into account.
To this end, a points-based talent card is to be introduced on the basis of annual labor requirements.

We facilitate educational migration through scholarships and training visas, as well as the requirements for a permanent residence permit and the recognition of professional qualifications acquired abroad.
We are also ending the automatic loss of residence permits after a six-month stay abroad.

For people who are in Germany without a secure residence permit but who are integrated into the labor market or whose qualifications match the labor demand, there should be the possibility of a genuine lane change.
We are expanding and consolidating well-functioning concepts for labor migration, such as the Western Balkans regulation.
Integration only works in the middle - language, access, participation right from the start
Arriving in a diverse immigration society is a two-way process with the aim of creating equal access and opportunities for participation in all areas of life.
It places demands both on those who come to us and on all those who have lived here for a long time, and can only succeed if everyone comes together and embarks on a common path.
The values of the Basic Law are the basis for living together.

Access to and participation in language courses is essential, which is why we advocate that all newly arrived migrants and refugees have the right to free access to tailored, easily accessible and federally funded language and integration courses right from the start.
In particular, we want to ensure the accessibility of courses for women and also develop courses for people with learning difficulties.
For many people, such as family members or EU citizens, this is currently only possible with difficulty and at a cost.
We also want to maintain the range of advanced language courses that have been expanded since 2015.

Just as important for successful integration are decentralized accommodation and a self-determined life in one's own home, a wide range of advisory services, especially for families, as well as indiscriminate access to health and social services, daycare, educational institutions, training and work, i.e. participation in cultural and social life.
In this way, targeted support strengthens social cohesion as a whole.
We want to set up a municipal integration fund at European level to provide direct support for arrivals in municipalities across the EU.

Among other things, this is intended to strengthen and establish migration advice centers, finance interpreting services in the community, promote civil society support structures and secure structural relief for municipalities that agree to take in refugees in the EU.
Companies that give refugees an opportunity for training or employment need appropriate support and funding.
We want to lower the barriers to freedom of movement within the European Union for recognized refugees.
Fair and transparent asylum procedures
We want asylum procedures in Germany to be legally secure, fair and transparent and for a decision to be made within a reasonable period of time.
To this end, special protection needs must be identified prior to the hearing.
In particular, the consideration of gender-specific persecution suffered and the associated counseling in the asylum procedure must be guaranteed.
We want to ensure that a decision on the residence permit is made quickly so that people have binding certainty at an early stage.
This includes adequate staffing at the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) and a functioning quality management system.

We want to ensure non-governmental, independent asylum procedure counseling for all asylum seekers, from their arrival to the conclusion of the asylum procedure, and we want to reverse the possible 18-month extension of the length of stay for refugees in initial reception facilities to a maximum of three months.
We reject AnkER centers in their current form.
Accordingly, decentralized living should always have priority.
We want to guarantee the right of children to access daycare centers, schools and other educational opportunities, regardless of their prospects of remaining in the country.
We will end the BAMF's blanket revocation checks without cause and optimize the asylum process law.
Applications for family reunification under the Dublin Regulation must be approved quickly.
We want to abolish the Asylum Seekers' Benefits Act - and with it a constitutionally unjustified unequal treatment of refugees that makes it difficult for them to truly arrive and participate.
We want to abolish anti-integration legislation such as work bans and blanket residence requirements as well as benefit cuts.
We want to reverse the erosion of the right of residence and asylum that has taken place in recent years.
In particular, we want to guarantee the protection of refugees who have experienced human rights violations or are seriously ill.
We reject the declaration of "safe" countries of origin or third countries - also at European level.
We want to abolish airport procedures and immediate refoulement at Germany's internal borders.
Raise the minimum wage
Work must be paid fairly.
And people need good working conditions.
But in our rich country, millions of people are still working in the low-wage sector with poor wages and in insecure employment.
Women and people with a history of migration are particularly often affected.
We want to change that.
We will immediately raise the statutory minimum wage to 12 euros.
The minimum wage must then continue to rise in order to provide effective protection against poverty and at least match the development of collectively agreed wages.
We want to reform the Minimum Wage Commission and equip it with this mandate.
We will abolish the existing exemptions for under-18s and the long-term unemployed.
Temporary workers should receive the same pay for the same work as permanent employees from day one - plus a flexibility bonus.
Fair-paying entrepreneurs must not suffer any competitive disadvantages.
In times of Corona, it is particularly evident that the short-time working allowance is too low for employees with low wages.
This is why a sector-independent minimum short-time working allowance is needed.
Employment contracts may no longer be limited in time without an objective reason.
We are taking regulatory action against the widespread abuse of work contracts and the shifting of corporate responsibility through subcontractor chains.
We want to strengthen occupational health and safety so that it provides effective protection against stress, burnout and the dissolution of boundaries at work.
We take bullying and discrimination in the workplace seriously and want to provide better protection against this through clear sanctions and mandatory contact points.
Creating full employment
We want to enable everyone to participate in working life, because a good job is an important source of income, recognition and self-fulfilment.
To achieve this, we need to create good and secure jobs.
We want to further increase employment and thus also prevent corona from leaving a long-term mark on the labor market.
We want to create an environment for many new jobs with permanently higher public investment, more entrepreneurial spirit, research and innovation.

The German labor market has been divided in recent years: Skills shortages and significant wage increases for highly skilled workers in some sectors, precarious employment, involuntary part-time work and stagnating real wages in others.
We want to counter this with a socially just labor policy.
This will ensure good wages and dry up the low-wage sector in the medium term.
Self-employed people need good framework conditions and better social security.
We want to combat the structural causes of long-term unemployment.
For people who have been unemployed for a long time, we are creating a permanent social labor market that provides meaningful activities.
Strengthen social partnership, increase collective bargaining coverage
Social partnership, collective agreements and co-determination are cornerstones of the social market economy.
They have made our country strong.
Where they apply, they usually ensure decent wages and good working conditions.
We want collective agreements and strong co-determination to once again apply to more employees and companies instead of fewer and fewer.
In accordance with European law, public procurement should be awarded to companies that are bound by collective agreements or at least pay collectively agreed wages.
To this end, we are backing a federal law on collective bargaining.
We also want to make it easier to declare collective agreements generally binding so that they apply to everyone in an industry.
It must not be worthwhile for companies to escape from collective bargaining.
We want to oblige companies to publish whether they are party to a collective agreement.
In the event of restructuring, the previous collective agreement regulations should apply until a new collective agreement has been concluded.

In future, companies with more than 1,000 employees should already have equal co-determination and we want to introduce an arbitration procedure if decisions have a particularly strong impact on employees.
Works councils that stand up for employees also need more protection themselves.
The same applies to employees who want to set up a works council for the first time.

We want to expand and modernize the co-determination rights of works councils, staff councils and also youth and trainee representatives, including when it comes to personnel development, further training, relocations abroad, empowering women, promoting diversity or improving the company's carbon footprint.
Greater financial participation of employees in the company, in addition to wages and salaries, can bring about more co-determination.
The changes in the world of work brought about by digitalization and ecological transformation must be shaped together with the employees in the company.
Migration, asylum and integration: Acting humanely and rationally - protecting Germany
The refugee movements of the 21st century
The challenges of the 21st century cannot be overcome by taking in migrants in Europe and Germany.
There have never been more refugees globally than in recent years.
In addition to armed conflicts and government persecution, the enormous population growth on the African continent plays a particularly important role.
As this is associated with poverty and the struggle for daily survival, the pressure to migrate to Europe is growing in a special way.
Contrary to the intention of the UN migration pact, this global problem cannot be solved through migration.
Even smaller parts of this development, which can be expressed in millions of people, cannot be absorbed in Europe, neither economically nor in terms of social and integration policy.
Germany and the other European countries would be destabilized without making an effective contribution to solving the global problem.
End asylum abuse
The current asylum system is dysfunctional and resembles a lottery.
Financial disincentives and failure to deport people lead to illegal migration, smuggling and numerous deaths in the Mediterranean.
Most of these migrants make their way to Europe in the hope of a better life.

However, aid for people in need must be decoupled from reception in Germany and provided in the crisis regions themselves, where it is far more effective and reaches many more people who really need help.
The unsolvable follow-up problems

The disastrous consequences of unregulated mass immigration since 2015 are unmistakable and continue to worsen: disproportionately high levels of immigrant crime, terrorist attacks and Islamic separatism are evidence of this, as are costs in the triple-digit billions, housing shortages and high unemployment among immigrants.
Successful integration cannot and will not succeed in this way.
Deportation and return
The failure to terminate the stay of rejected asylum seekers who are obliged to leave the country is the opposite of the rule of law: it is an expression of the continued failure of the state.

The number of people required to leave the country has risen continuously and reached around 300,000 in the second quarter of 2021 - while the number of voluntary departures and successful deportations is falling steadily.
Politicians have capitulated to the task of resolving this contradiction - driven by a powerful anti-deportation industry.
It is cynical and inhumane to lure people with the de facto guarantee of permanent residence in "rich" Germany while accepting their possible death in the Mediterranean.

Voluntary return is always preferable to deportation for financial, organizational and humanitarian reasons, which is why willingness to return must be encouraged much more than it has been in the past.
Saving lives and creating social justice
Germany's benefits for asylum seekers are very high by international standards.
Recognized persons can expect lifelong material security.
The funds for this are raised by taxpayers who have to work hard for it, but have not invited economic refugees.
The generosity of the German state causes a considerable pull effect, which leads to the death of many people.
In doing so, the German government is burdening itself with grave moral guilt.
Recognition of asylum leads to immediate equality in all social security systems, without any previous participation in the solidarity system.
That is socially unjust.
Help on the ground instead of death on the way to Europe
Help on the ground is a top priority for the AfD.
It must be given absolute priority over accepting asylum seekers in Germany.
At the same time, this reduces important reasons for flight.
Some of the tens of billions of euros invested in asylum policy can have a multiple impact close to home and thus help to reduce migration pressure in the long term.
Regulate immigration nationally again
Germany no longer has sovereignty over immigration policy.
The main reason for this is a far-reaching transfer of sovereign rights to the EU and accession to international agreements, all of which pursue an extreme left-wing "one-world utopia".
Qualified immigration
The current immigration system is damaging Germany both culturally and economically and is in urgent need of reform.
The AfD is committed to preserving Germany's cultural identity.

The model for an identity-preserving migration policy for Germany cannot be classic immigration countries the size of Canada or Australia, but rather countries such as Japan, which limit and control migration in accordance with their national structure.
Due to the lockdown crisis, automation and digitalization, the times of record-high employment are foreseeably over.
Mass migration creates wage pressure right down to the middle class and leads to competition for social benefits.

We call for the development of a comprehensive migration policy approach based on the Japanese model with the primary goal of safeguarding the interests of Germans and citizens who have already immigrated and are committed to Germany's cultural identity.

The claim by some business associations and lobbyists that there is a shortage of skilled workers in Germany and therefore a need for qualified immigration only superficially serves the common good and must therefore not be relevant.
The harmful influence of particular economic interests or even anti-German resentment concealed by them must be ended.
Integration
We consider immigrants and people to whom we grant temporary protection to be responsible for integration.
Integration can only succeed if the rules, traditions and values of our society are accepted.
The acquisition of the German language is essential.
Fighting left-wing violence decisively
Left-wing extremism is increasingly crossing the threshold to left-wing terrorism.
We are therefore calling for increased efforts in the fight against left-wing extremism.
The granting of state funding must once again be linked to a declaration of commitment not to support extremist structures.
We are therefore calling for the reintroduction of a binding extremism clause.
We are also calling for the left-wing extremist platform "Indymedia" to be banned.
Violent and supportive left-wing extremist and autonomous groups belonging to the so-called Antifa are to be classified as terrorist organizations.
The privileged treatment of "antifa research" intended by the federal government must be prevented and, if necessary, abolished immediately.
Effectively combating crime against foreigners
The considerable proportion of foreigners, especially in violent and drug-related crime, but also in public unrest, currently leads far too rarely to measures under immigration law.
Foreign criminals can very often invoke obstacles to deportation and are thus spared deportation.

We therefore call for (a) the facilitation of deportation, in particular the reintroduction of mandatory deportation even for minor crimes, (b) deportation by the criminal courts, (c) the possibility of accommodating criminals who have not been deported abroad, (d) the creation of the possibility of detaining dangerous persons, especially terrorists, for as long as they are in Germany and pose a significant danger to the general public.
The naturalization of criminals can be reliably prevented by rejecting the acquisition of German citizenship by birth in Germany because, among other things

members of criminal clans can automatically become German citizens, the abolition of the enforceable right to naturalization and the tightening of the grounds for exclusion from naturalization in the case of criminality.
In the event of serious crime within ten years of naturalization (involvement in terrorist organizations, membership of criminal clans), naturalization must be revoked.
Police reform
Police officers at federal and state level ensure
public safety with great personal commitment.
They are often let down by the state: Lack of personnel, structural inadequacies, inadequate equipment and weaponry with poor pay and miserable social security.
These conditions are outrageous.
This must finally come to an end.

The AfD is calling for standardized national salaries for police, soldiers and emergency services, as well as appropriate remuneration with risk allowances and additional allowances for overtime and special assignments.
We also demand adequate armament and equipment, including
Body cameras.

The employer must take out disability and public liability insurance and ensure that the survivor's pension is adjusted to the amount of the pension entitlements of the last office in the event of death due to a qualifying industrial accident.
Improve search options
In order to improve search possibilities, the police authorities are to be able to use video surveillance with facial recognition software in places and buildings where crime is neuralgic.
When searching for unknown perpetrators, it should be permitted to use existing
DNA trace material can also be examined for biogeographical characteristics of the wanted person in order to enable targeted search measures.

Intergovernmental agreements are intended to ensure that police officers on duty are also able to determine whether and, if so, which investigations and criminal proceedings were and are pending against a person being checked abroad.
Fighting organized crime
We want to fight organized crime (OC) decisively and sustainably.
Assets acquired through criminal activities must be confiscated.
This has not yet been done satisfactorily.
The existing legal instruments for this must be better utilized and further developed.
The majority of perpetrators of organized crime are foreigners.
Their expulsion must be simplified.
For this reason, membership of an OC should be introduced as a reason for deportation for this group of people.
Improving the safety of citizens
At the proposal of the EU Commission, the EU Parliament amended the EU Firearms Directive in response to the terrorist attacks in Paris in November 2015.
This will lead to a further tightening of gun laws.
Those most affected by the tightening of the already restrictive gun laws are sport shooters, hunters and gun collectors.
Illegal weapons used for terrorist attacks are not included.
We continue to reject the implementation of the EU Firearms Directive.
Instead of criminalizing legal gun owners, a stop should be put to the illegal possession and trade of weapons.
Improving criminal justice
The AfD is committed to rapidly improving the organization of the judiciary, strengthening our legal system and ensuring effective legal protection for citizens.
Specifically, we want to speed up the procedures and (a) use the 19th-century procedures for this purpose.

(a) modernize the legal system dating back to the 19th century, (b) recruit more staff for the judiciary, (c) combat serious crime more effectively by making it easier to take people into custody, (d) suspend fewer sentences on probation and (e) increase the minimum sentence for "knife offences".
A positive approach to climate change

The German government's goal of effectively reducing CO2 emissions to zero is leading to a radical restructuring of industry and society ("The Great Transformation" / "The Great Reset") and is threatening our freedom to an ever more frightening extent.

The AfD rejects this goal and the associated social restructuring, justifying the radical restructuring of industry and society with the claim that decarbonization, i.e. the abandonment of the use of coal, oil and gas, could still prevent a man-made "climate catastrophe".
We consider this thesis and the measures derived from it to be wrong.
The trace gas CO2 is essential for all life.
The increase in the concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere has contributed to the greening of the earth in recent decades.
Nobody denies the recent global warming.
However, the AfD doubts that this will only have negative consequences.
Instead of waging a hopeless battle against climate change, we should adapt to the changing conditions, just as plants and animals do.
Human history shows that warm periods always led to a flourishing of life and cultures, while cold periods were associated with hardship, hunger and wars.
It has not yet been proven that humans, especially industry, are significantly responsible for climate change.
The recent warming is within the range of natural climate fluctuations, as we know them from the pre-industrial past.
In Germany, technological progress is increasingly no longer seen as an opportunity for our country, which is poor in raw materials, but is instead hindered or prevented due to fears.
The AfD opposes this development and tries to convey a positive expectation of the future in society and parliaments.
It is not renunciation, regression and socialism that have
environmental pollution for decades, but technological progress and a market economy based on clear rules.
Technologies must benefit citizens, the economy and also our home country, i.e. the environment.
It is the task of politicians to formulate framework conditions based on the current state of science and technology.
The safety and efficiency of any technology must be ensured by the user.
This is why the AfD is calling for the challenges of the present to be met with an open-minded approach to technology.
A secure and affordable energy supply is one of the basic prerequisites for prosperity, security and health.
Ensuring this is the core task of the state.
Energy policy means setting framework conditions in such a way that the energy supply is secure, environmentally friendly and cost-effective within the framework of the free market.
Expensive and scarce energy causes industries to move away and drastically restricts the standard of living of large sections of the population, especially the lower income groups.
Energy - No to the "Green Deal"
We reject the EU's "Green Deal" and all other forms of planned economy.
We want to abolish the EEG without replacement and end priority feed-in.
The secure energy supply of an industrialized country requires a broad energy mix.
A complete conversion of our energy supply to volatile "renewable" energy sources is unecologically unrealistic and should therefore be rejected.
The AfD rejects the new GEG (Building Energy Act) because it leads to further rent increases without appropriate ecological improvements.
No wind and solar installations may be erected in forests and protected areas.
We are committed to preserving the local landscape, our environment and wildlife.
Priority areas for wind turbines should only be designated with the broad consent of the citizens concerned.
The minimum distance between wind turbines and residential buildings must be 10 times the total height, but at least 2.5 km.
Plants that are no longer subsidized after 20 years are to participate in the market without subsidies and feed-in priority.
Wind turbines must be completely dismantled, including the concrete foundations.
We no longer want to promote so-called energy crops and instead want to use arable land for growing food again.
Alternatively, these areas can be returned to nature.
We reject the preferential treatment and promotion of a hydrogen economy as well as the one-sided promotion of electromobility.
Openness to technology also applies to the use of hydrogen and electromobility.
Both require an ecologically, energetically and economically nonsensical parallel infrastructure system.
Due to the high and low-cost availability of natural gas, there is no need for volatile
"renewable" energy sources, large-scale production of hydrogen is not yet possible.
We need more flexible gas-fired power plants to secure the energy supply.
To this end, the gas supply must be secured by completing the Nord Stream 2 project.
The landing of liquid gas must also be made possible.
The AfD is committed to the generation of electricity from lignite and hard coal as a base-load and controllable energy source.
Germany has the world's cleanest and most efficient coal-fired power plants.
We therefore reject the plans to phase out coal-fired power generation.
The service life of the six remaining active nuclear power plants in Germany must be based on their technical service life and economic criteria.
We reject a shutdown for other reasons.
German nuclear power plants are among the safest in the world.
Recyclable nuclear power plant residues should be stored in a retrievable form for future use ("closed fuel cycle").
Since Gorleben is a fully researched and fully suitable repository, the search for another geological repository must be discontinued.
Instead, the research and utilization of technologies that no longer require the storage of highly radioactive waste in geological time frames should be accelerated.

The AfD calls for the re-establishment of nuclear research centers and extensive participation in international nuclear research projects to secure the necessary knowledge for the operation and construction of nuclear reactors, for research into advanced reactor concepts of Generation III+ and IV as well as breeder reactors and fusion energy.
The AfD advocates the construction of new safe nuclear power plants in order to avoid energy shortages for Germany as an industrial location and its citizens.
New prosperity - sustainable growth to become a climate-neutral industrialized country
Our Union promise: We will get our economy moving again and provide secure and sustainable jobs.
In doing so, we combine sustainable growth, climate protection and social security.
We want to bring interests together and not play them off against each other.
More than ever, this principle will guide our policies, actions and decisions.
The coronavirus pandemic has also led to a massive economic slump in Germany.
We were able to stabilize the economy and secure jobs because we acted quickly and decisively in a major joint effort.
At the same time, the pandemic has shown that our country is not fast, agile or courageous enough in some areas.

All too often, we place unnecessary obstacles in the way of the hard-working, the capable and the courageous - in the skilled trades, in SMEs and in the freelance professions as well as in the cultural and creative scene - instead of clearing the way for them and trusting their skills and ideas.
The path from problem to solution leads too often and for too long through a thicket of regulations and concerns.
It is not enough to just tweak a few screws.
We need a decade of modernization in Germany.
We need to set a new course.
In doing so, we will focus even more strongly on the principles of the social market economy.
It combines freedom with security, personal responsibility with the common good, economic dynamism with social balance.
It focuses on doing instead of complaining, on openness instead of isolation, on generating instead of distributing, on ideas instead of prohibitions.
We also rely on these principles in the fight against climate change.
We want to take the decisive steps now, in this decade, to ensure that Germany becomes a climate-neutral industrialized country by 2045.
Our Christian view of humanity obliges us to preserve creation and to act responsibly towards our fellow human beings, the environment and future generations.
We want to remain an industrialized country and maintain highly qualified industrial jobs - together with industry and the social partners and without overburdening consumers.
Continuing the social market economy as a successful model
The social market economy is the economic order of our liberal democracy.
It is the foundation of our success as an innovative, efficient and sustainable economy.
It combines opportunities for the individual with social security in our society.
It is the order that harmonizes economy, ecology and social issues like no other.

On this basis, generations of women and men have made Germany one of the most prosperous nations in the world through education, hard work and achievement, a willingness to take responsibility and commitment; a globally admired economic and ecological role model; the home of hundreds of thousands of companies that contribute to social prosperity and social security with their competitiveness and innovative strength.
We want to continue this success story and renew the guard rails of the social market economy.
We will continue to combine economic expertise with practiced solidarity and efficient protection of the environment and climate in the future.
The sustainable, social, ecological and digital market economy is our social market economy of the 21st century.
Century.
We rely on trust in people, on freedom instead of paternalism, on freedom instead of control.
We rely on functioning competition that gives people the chance to make the most of their abilities.
Especially in the age of globalization and digitalization, we rely on the state to regulate the market.
A strong state organizes the economy and sets the rules, but does not take part in events itself.
Our unleashing package for the economy

Regardless of whether they are self-employed and small, medium-sized or large companies: In our decade of modernization, we need to enable them to focus more on their core business and implement new ideas.
A modern Germany is also one that gives inventiveness and entrepreneurship more freedom.
We will therefore launch a comprehensive unbundling package that will relieve companies of taxes and bureaucracy and speed up planning and approval procedures.
Our aim is for the doers to use their energy first and foremost to do business successfully and not to fulfill bureaucratic obligations.
Because that will move our country forward.
Preventing new burdens
It is clear to us that in order for the economy to regain momentum and for us to create new prosperity together, no new burdens should be imposed on companies.
We want to keep non-wage labor costs at a stable level of no more than 40 percent.
We will continue to adhere to the principle of "relieving rather than burdening".
Tax increases are the wrong way to go, especially after the pandemic.
They stand in the way of the necessary upturn in our economy.
We will gradually abolish the solidarity surcharge for everyone and at the same time reduce the income tax burden on small and medium-sized incomes.
We are firmly opposed to any plans to introduce new taxes on assets such as wealth tax or an increase in inheritance tax.
Both would above all jeopardize Germany's economic substance and cost jobs.

The foundation stone
The foundations for advancement through education are laid at an early age.
We believe that people's origins should not determine their future.
Parents and children have a right to high-quality childcare that is reliable and appropriate to their needs.
We will continue to promote the expansion of daycare centers and the further development of quality beyond 2022.
In this way, we help children in their development and support parents in balancing family and career.
We will continue to develop early education facilities into high-quality places of education and thus make a key contribution to decoupling origin and educational success.
Promoting language education for all children
All children must be able to make the most of their educational opportunities right from the start.
No child must be left behind.
This is the only way we can keep our promise of "advancement through education".
We will promote the acquisition of the German language as early as possible, in particular through binding, continuous and standardized diagnostic procedures.
From the age of three, mandatory language proficiency tests with high-quality language support programs are added for all children.
Wherever a special need for language support is identified, compulsory, qualitatively effective and continuous language support must be provided in a daycare center or preschool.

An individual language support plan is to be drawn up for each of these children, which includes support goals, duration and scope of the specific measures in addition to the integrated language support.
Every primary school child must be able to speak German before starting school in order to be able to follow lessons from the first grade onwards.
We support the federal program "Sprach-Kitas: Because language is the key to the world" and want to further promote language education in this area.
It is important to us that we focus even more on children with language support needs.
Strengthening schools in socially difficult locations in particular
To ensure that every child can make the most of their opportunities, we want to further strengthen schools, especially in socially disadvantaged areas.
The federal-state initiative "Schule macht stark" (School makes you strong) promotes the best educational opportunities for socially disadvantaged pupils.
We want to strengthen this initiative and develop it further so that schools can offer the best possible individual support.
Strengthening digital education
It is the task of our educational institutions to educate children and young people to become self-determined and responsible personalities.
To do this, they need specialist knowledge and skills as well as a sense of values and judgment.
In addition, there are teamwork and collaboration skills, resilience, creativity, a spirit of research and entrepreneurship as well as problem-solving and critical thinking.
We want students to see lifelong learning, in particular further education and training, as a permanent task that they are responsible for.
This includes a learning environment that promotes their skills.
We want pedagogical concepts and teacher training to be developed further.
Digital skills must be comprehensively integrated into lessons.

We want to establish nationwide educational competence centers with the aim of networking teacher training universities, research institutes and teacher training institutions in the federal states and making educational research findings directly usable for teacher training.
The successfully established teacher training quality campaign is to be further developed in terms of content.

Living safely within your own four walls
We have enforced tougher penalties to deter burglars.
But this alone is not enough.
We must also ensure that more burglaries are solved, perpetrators are caught more easily and repeat offenders are prevented.
Serial offenses can be prevented.
We have therefore given the police additional investigative powers.
We are consistently pursuing this path.
We want software-based tools to be increasingly used in the future to help predict burglary patterns.
In this way, particularly vulnerable residential areas can be identified and specifically monitored by police patrols.
We continue to support owners and tenants in better securing their doors and windows.
To this end, we will expand state subsidies.
Show more police presence
Where boundaries are crossed, rules disregarded or laws broken, zero tolerance applies.
Safety is particularly important where we are at home, in our everyday lives and in our neighborhoods.
We want to relieve the police of bureaucratic tasks.
This will bring it even closer to the people and make it more visible.
We need more police officers on the streets and in the squares - both in the city and in rural areas.
We are also focusing on security on trains, at train stations and airports by increasing police presence.
Anyone who experiences neglect, dirty green spaces or graffiti on facades does not feel comfortable and therefore not safe.
That is why we are committed to clean towns and well-kept districts.
Expand video protection at public danger spots
Cameras with intelligent video security technology help our police officers to deter criminals and solve crimes.
The following applies: more security and targeted data protection through modern technology that is efficient and innovative.

We will have to constantly reassess the extent to which the individual's right to the protection of their personal data can be reconciled with the constitutional mandate to guarantee security for all people.

We want to further expand intelligent video protection at public danger spots such as in front of and inside soccer stadiums, at train stations and other transport hubs as well as on buses and trains.
We want to make even better use of the opportunities offered by digitalization and artificial intelligence.

In order to improve the search for serious criminals, dangerous individuals and terrorists, we want to create the conditions for automated facial recognition to be used at dangerous locations in Germany.

Consistently protecting emergency personnel Police officers, firefighters, paramedics and other emergency personnel stand up for the safety of us all every day with their work and often with their lives.
In order to better protect those who protect us, we will increase the minimum sentence for assault to six months, and for insidious attacks to one year in prison and thus classify them as a crime.
If the offender is carrying a weapon or other dangerous instrument, a sentence of up to ten years may be imposed.
Police officers must not only be well trained, but also well equipped so that they can protect us and themselves.
We therefore want to improve training and further training and ensure the best possible equipment, such as the widespread use of bodycams - including for operations in residential areas.
This means that operational situations can be recorded with certainty, attackers can be identified and criminal offenses can be prosecuted more easily.
We want those who join a violent crowd and do not leave despite police requests to do so to be held criminally liable, thereby protecting active perpetrators of violence.
In order to support police officers and other emergency services personnel as well as soldiers, we want to regulate their claims for compensation for pain and suffering.
Even if they are insulted on duty, the compensation awarded by the court should be advanced by the state.
The state then recovers the money from the offender.
We want to examine the pensionability of the police allowance.
Working together more closely across regions and authorities
Criminals today are often highly mobile, and gangs have long been operating across borders in areas such as burglaries, human trafficking, drug trafficking and arms dealing.
We are responding to this in the fight against crime.
We want police and investigative authorities in Germany to work together even more closely on a supra-regional and inter-agency basis.
We will also counter organized crime, the mafia and criminal clans at European level through more effective cooperation - also with regard to EUROPOL and the perpetrators' countries of origin.
We will continue to expand the already improved cross-border police cooperation.
In order to further strengthen border searches in particularly dangerous situations, we have enabled the Federal Police to record car license plates with automatic readers.
We want checks to be carried out everywhere in Germany with the help of an image-based dragnet.
This is not only important in border regions, but also on internationally important transport routes and in the vicinity of railroad stations and airports.
To this end, we want to extend the border corridor currently used by the federal police.
Education of the future - opportunities for advancement and self-determination
Education is the elementary prerequisite for individual progress and a self-determined life.
Today more than ever, the chance of social advancement depends on education.
We Free Democrats want everyone to be able to realize their full potential - throughout their lives.
That is why we are working to ensure that state-of-the-art education becomes the standard in Germany.
We Free Democrats are calling for an additional percentage point of the existing VAT revenue to be invested in education.
The federal and state governments, with the involvement of the municipalities, are to commit to this in a state treaty.
This will enable additional investment of around 2.5 billion euros in the education sector, which is urgently needed for the comprehensive modernization of our education system.
In this way, we can bring Germany into the top 5 OECD countries.
Sustainable education federalism
We Free Democrats demand nationwide final examinations for the intermediate school-leaving certificate and the Abitur as well as high-quality educational standards.
We need more innovation and quality assurance through comparability in education.

We are calling for a reform of education federalism and an amendment to the Basic Law so that the federal and state governments can work together to ensure the quality, performance and further development of the education system.
We can afford 16 different school systems, curricula and examination regulations, but we do not ensure that school education is of the highest quality throughout Germany.
We want future-proof schools in which the best work opportunities for teaching and learning are available.
Strengthening the autonomy of schools
We Free Democrats want to strengthen the autonomy of schools and give schools more pedagogical, personnel and financial freedom.
Each school should receive its own budget, the use of which it decides autonomously.
Within the framework of school autonomy, lessons can be organized in a modular system, for example, and thus tailored to the individual pupil.
At the same time, this gives pupils greater freedom of choice and allows the school to cater to the different performance levels of pupils more individually.
This should also make it easier to teach interdisciplinary projects.
Staffing decisions and the selection of teaching materials are also made locally by the school.
We demand equal support for independent schools.
We are campaigning for school freedom laws in the federal states to give schools more opportunities to develop their profiles.
Uniform educational standards set the goal of aligning with the level of the best educational institutions in the world.
In order to achieve the standards, schools must be supported with excellent further training in school and teaching development.
The PISA study shows that children achieve significantly better results in schools with greater freedom of design and decision-making.
Strengthening schools and daycare centers financially

We Free Democrats want to strengthen schools and daycare centers financially by placing their funding on three pillars: a basic amount according to the size of the institution, education vouchers that grant a subsidy per child, and a "German Dream" subsidy for children with low socio-economic status.

The fixed basic amount guarantees the viability of smaller schools in rural areas in particular and funding via the education voucher model guarantees needs-based funding for educational institutions.
At the same time, healthy competition is promoted and the freedom of choice of parents and children is strengthened.
Finally, thanks to the "German Dream" grant, educational institutions can offer individual support concepts for children and young people with more support needs on their own responsibility.
At the same time, we are preventing the quality of schools from drifting apart.
Strengthening STEM education at an early stage - targeted support for girls and women
We Free Democrats are calling for an offensive for education in mathematics, information technology, natural sciences and technology (STEM).
Children must receive STEM education at an early age, which is why we are calling for mandatory, high-quality and nationwide quality and educational standards in early childhood STEM education.
Teachers must be trained for experimental and research-based learning in all daycare centers.
We are calling for a targeted package of measures to promote girls and women in STEM fields.
We want to further strengthen extracurricular initiatives such as the "Little Scientists' House".
