Chemists have elucidated the formation stages of the components that would have given rise to life
Researchers may have discovered the recipe that led to the formation of the components of genetic material, which could be a major step forward in understanding the origins of life.
How did life originate?
And how was the genetic information enabling the creation of the first organisms stored?
These are multi-million dollar questions... literally.
Finding these answers would be a guaranteed nomination for the Nobel Prize.

For the moment, many scientists accept the theory that the first molecule to carry genetic information was RNA, which later evolved into DNA, a much more stable molecule and therefore less prone to mutation.
However, the origins of RNA are still a mystery.
But a team of researchers has demonstrated that simple molecules, presumed to have existed during the Earth's primitive era, could have formed the materials necessary for the formation of RNA.
These materials, the nucleic bases, are four in number, and are divided into two groups according to their molecular structure: pyrimidines (uracil and cytosine), and purines (adenine and guanine).

You'll also like: In 2009, scientists at Cambridge University had already succeeded in synthesizing pyrimidines in the laboratory, from five compounds thought to have been present in the early days of the Earth.
And only two years later, it was the turn of the two purines, synthesized at Munich's Ludwig Maximilian University.
However, the chemical reactions required to synthesize the two groups of nucleic bases are not identical.
What were the conditions that allowed them to form at the same time and in the same place?

Thomas Carrell, who was involved in the development of purines in Munich, may have found the answer to this question, having identified a series of reactions that would have led to the creation of the four RNA bases.
He and his colleagues worked on six molecules that would have been present during the primitive era: nitrogen, oxygen, ammonia, methane, hydrogen cyanide and, of course, water.
To form pyrimidines, his group started with two compounds formed from the following molecules: cyanoethyne and hydroxylamine, which react to form aminoisoxazoles.
These are then mixed with the urea molecule to form another compound which again reacts with a sugar, ribose.

The molecule obtained from these reactions is further mixed with a small amount of iron, nickel salt and thiols (sulfurized compounds), eventually forming the two pyrimidine bases, uracil and cytosine.

Another interesting fact is that this last reaction only occurs when the salts in the mixture carry more positive charges, a criterion also required in the final stage of purine base synthesis (adenine and guanine), showing that nucleic bases can be formed in the same place.

Steven Benner, a chemist at the Foundation for Applied Molecular Evolution in Florida, says that the process employed produced the four bases under conditions believed to be similar to those of the primitive era.
Nevertheless, there are still many obscure points in RNA assembly, such as the steps involved in linking the four nucleic bases, and determining which molecules are involved.
But their research represents an important advance in our understanding of how genetic material was synthesized when the Earth was still a primitive planet.

One of the most puzzling questions is how the structures are so perfectly aligned.

Although slightly unbalanced, overall, the sides of the Great Pyramid of Giza (which stands 138 metres high - also known as the Pyramid of Cheops) are very straight and almost perfectly aligned along the four cardinal points. "The builders of the Great Pyramid of Giza aligned the monument to the cardinal points with a precision greater than four minutes of arc, or one fifteenth of a degree," writes archaeologist and engineer Glen Dash, in an article published in The Journal of Ancient Egyptian Architecture.
In fact, Egypt's three largest pyramids (two at Giza and one at Dahshur) are remarkably aligned.

This precision is very surprising, given the era in which they were built. "All three pyramids have the same type of error: they are turned slightly counter-clockwise from the cardinal points," explains Dash.
Today, there are many hypotheses as to how the pyramids were aligned in this way: using the North Star to align them, or the shadow of the sun.
However, no one has yet been able to define exactly what techniques the ancient Egyptians used.
But Dash has another, simpler idea.
His latest research suggests that the Egyptians, some 4,500 years ago, may have used the autumnal equinox to achieve perfect alignment.
The equinox is considered to be the moment when, twice a year, the plane of the Earth's equator passes through the center of the Sun's disk, and the duration of day and night are roughly equal.
Previously, equinox measurements had been overlooked as a possible alignment method, as it was assumed that they would not provide sufficient accuracy.

The brain has a particular structural organization, divided into areas and segments, where each zone fulfills a precise function.
For example, there are brain regions linked to language, smell, sight, limbs and so on.
This organization is called a "brain map".

These results confirm the brain's exceptional ability to adapt to change.
Loss of a limb: the brain reorganizes itself to compensate for the amputation.
Researchers used functional MRI (fMRI) at the MU Brain Imaging Center to scan the brains of 48 people, 19 of whom had lost a hand.
They created a computer-controlled system to deliver a light sensation of touch to the hands and face.
Functional MRIs are similar to conventional MRIs, but are sensitive to minute changes in blood oxygenation levels in the brain, which occur as areas of the brain process information.
The researchers observed in the scans that, when the brain is deprived of information from a lost hand, it reorganizes its neural map and redirects these functions to the remaining hand.

This discovery could help neurologists and healthcare professionals better understand the mechanisms underlying brain plasticity when physical trauma occurs, for example when wounded veterans return from the battlefield.

Increasingly expensive journeys.

Combine the benefits.

The United Kingdom is a parliamentary monarchy.
Most power comes from Parliament and the government, which is accountable to it.

The fact that the monarch is not appointed directly by an electoral procedure, as in France, or indirectly, as in Germany, prevents a purely political decision that would threaten the stability of the institutions.
A politically independent safeguard that prevents the executive from concentrating too much power.
This situation contrasts with republics with a strong presidency, such as France or the United States, where the president practically has sole decision-making power.
A symbol for the UK, the Commonwealth and the rest of the world.
If the monarch's real role is limited, his symbolic role is powerful.
The Queen united the country around her.
As leader of the Commonwealth, she had influence all over the world, including India.
In this way, it retained a real symbolism in the world.
An aura that extends to the royal family.

War in Ukraine: the commercial implications of cutting Russia off from the world
As a principle of public international law, the MFN statute establishes the sovereign equality of states in matters of trade policy.
It implies that each WTO member must guarantee equal treatment for other members, and that each member must treat all others equally as trading partners.
If a state increases the benefits it grants to a trading partner, it must grant the same "better" treatment to all other WTO members, so that they all remain "most favored".
An exception to the favourable principle of the multilateral trading system.
The principle of MFN treatment dates back to 1947.

It appears in Article I of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), governing the treatment of goods, in Article II of the General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS) and in Article IV of the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS), governing relations within the WTO.
On reading the WTO rules, we can see that they provide specific means for members of this international organization to impose special trade barriers on other members.
The relevant one in this case is the safety exception.

Article XXI of the 1994 WTO treaty allows 164 member states to refuse to apply MFN status to another member if this is "necessary for the protection of its essential security interests", in particular "in the event of war or other emergency in international relations".
With armed aggression underway, the security provision is the main legal justification for the sanctions imposed on Russia.
It is therefore an exception to the favourable principle of the multilateral trading system.
The removal of Russia's trade privileges at the WTO will have several consequences.

As the European Commission stated on March 15, 2022: withdrawal from MFN status means the end of the advantages of WTO membership, specifically the advantage of not being discriminated against by other members.
Withdrawal of MFN treatment means that the member concerned - in this case Russia - may be subject to higher tariffs and import bans.
This is not compulsory, but if a trading partner wants to exert pressure on the Kremlin to reconsider its ambitions, international law does not prevent it from doing so.
Faster, more effective sanctions than higher import duties.
In this context, the EU has decided to act not by raising import duties, but by imposing a range of sanctions, including bans on the import or export of goods.
This method is faster and more effective than preparing a completely new pricing program.
In practice, the Russian Federation has already lost several commercial advantages.
In particular, the suspension of the supply of SWIFT financial services to certain Russian banks constitutes a non-application of the MFN clause vis-à-vis Russia under the GATS.
The suspension of MFN status undoubtedly lends further meaning to these unprecedented sanctions.
As European Commission Executive Vice-President Valdis Dombrovskis has said, the EU is united in holding President Putin and his regime accountable for their crimes.
The only way for Russia to avoid commercial, financial, economic and reputational disaster is to end the invasion of Ukraine immediately.
The PFUE and the Commission are therefore adopting a very clear geopolitical commitment.

This decision to make an exception to the MFN principle of international law must be seen as a clear response by the EU to Russia's failure to respect another founding principle of public international law, the non-use of armed force enshrined in the 1946 UN Charter.

This is a very significant challenge especially when the enemy specializes in deception and does everything to hide the balance-breaking weapon in his possession.

Exactly one week ago, registration for the secondary education institutions in Hamad opened, and many parents are debating how to choose the best place for their children.

"After I listen to the parents, their values ​​and what is important to them, it is very important to listen to the child.
I meet with the child and the parents, then with the parents separately and then with the child separately.
You need to hear from him what is important to him."
Usually children are attracted to friends and want to go where the "guys" are "There is no doubt that friends are something very important and we all know it because we were teenagers.

How can you understand if this is the right step or not?
This is done while reflecting the academic and social situation.
For example, if it is about going to a far away place together with friends, we ask if it is built for leaving the house?
How did she feel about the annual trips or Bnei Akiva's trips from a social point of view?
If it's a girl whose friends all go to her boarding school, but she's better suited closer to home, she needs to be brought to this understanding."

"My understanding is that the answers to every question are at home - the parents and the children know what is good for them - and you just have to stop and ask and not get carried away with the flow.
Not to think, if everyone registers in one place, I'm after them, but to think what is right and good for the child at this point in time."
It happens that at first glance the child seems very suitable for institution X, but after a few meetings you realize that it is something completely different?

The most important thing is that a child does not experience the experience of not being accepted into an educational institution."
"A boy came to me with a painted blue shirt, torn jeans, and the parents wanted a place with a Gemara reinforcement.

Show us what you're really worth: the known assets of party leaders
Ahead of the establishment of the 21st Knesset after the upcoming elections, "Calcalist" asked to map the personal capital of the party leaders.

We approached them for this purpose, but only four responded to our request: Avigdor Lieberman from Yisrael Beitenu, Tamar Zandberg from Meretz, Aryeh Deri from Shas and Yaakov Litzman from Torah Judaism.
The other party leaders refused.
In the case of the party leaders, the only way to estimate their wealth is through the real estate they own.
Beyond that, the public relies on their willingness to give statements.
Accordingly, Calcalist's attempt to evaluate their wealth is based on their real estate.
For this purpose, we were assisted by the appraisers offices Kamil-Tarshansky-Raphael Vidid-Byrne & Co.
In order for the public to be able to get a more complete picture, legislation is required that would oblige elected officials to reveal more details.
At the very least, they should be required to disclose a list of conflicts of interest.
In Israel, the prime minister and ministers are required to submit capital statements to the state auditor at the beginning of each term, each year of office and after retirement.
These statements are confidential and the auditor has no authority to publish them.
MKs are required to submit capital declarations within 60 days of their election or any significant change to their capital, as well as 60 days after the end of their term of office.
These statements are delivered to the Speaker of the Knesset and are kept secretly in safes.
For all elected officials, the report must include details of their own and their family members' capital, assets, rights and obligations.
Elected officials are required to list all types of assets, their value on the day of their purchase and their additional sources of income and their amount.
In recent terms, several different bills have come up that sought to reveal the declarations of capital or conflicts of interest of elected officials.
Among others, such proposals were submitted by MK Sheli Yachimovich and Miki Rosenthal from Labor, by the Israel Beitenu faction and by former MK Zehava Galon from Meretz.
All the proposals fell in the plenary.

If the bill submitted in 2016 by MK Robert Ilatov of Israel Beytenu was accepted, the MKs would be required to disclose a statement that includes all their capital, assets, rights and obligations - as well as those of their family members.

The reasons for the bill state that it will "disclose to the public the capital statements of its senior elected officials in order to deal with existing conflicts of interest that may arise from them, as well as encourage transparency, due disclosure and strengthen the public's trust in the state and its elected officials and as a result in their decisions."
In many countries around the world, members of the various parliaments are required to submit capital statements - and in some of them there is even an obligation to disclose them to the public.
For example, the capital statements of members of parliament in France will be disclosed if they are required for legal proceedings.
EU MEPs' capital statements appear in a public register.

In a review on the subject conducted by Dina Zadok from the Knesset Research and Information Center, it is stated that "in most of the countries surveyed, there is an obligation for members of parliament to report on private interests, but the extent of the obligation is different in each country.
The differences between the countries are influenced, among other things, by the conflict of interest rules that apply to members of parliament in each country."

It may sound like something that happens mostly in far away and exotic places in the world, but it turns out that illegal hunting and trade in wild animals is a problem that has not escaped Israel.

According to Shoki Donitza, Director of the Inspection and Enforcement Division at the Nature and Parks Authority, animal trafficking is the fourth most economic crime after arms, drug and human trafficking, and dozens of such cases are also detected in Israel every year.
These two issues are on the regular agenda of the Authority, which is the political body responsible for preserving nature, a heritage landscape.

Thus, in 2018, 71 cases of illegal hunting were opened in Israel, 32 incidents were recorded in which illegal trade in wild animals was enforced and 231 animals and products derived from wild animals and protected natural values ​​were seized.
It's happening off our radar, the media's, and unfortunately the authorities too, but a new collaboration that has recently been officially launched gives hope that all of this can change.

Two weeks ago, on December 25, a treaty was signed to strengthen the cooperation between the Nature and Parks Authority and the Border Guard of the Israel Police, and thus they actually officially established a joint special force intelligence unit in the MGB, within the framework of which the bodies will exchange intelligence information in a regular and organized manner, with the aim of significantly reducing the extent of illegal hunting and damage to nature.

"This idea has been accompanying the Nature and Parks Authority for several years, and a long staff work was carried out until the decision was made on the joint establishment of an intelligence system," says Donitza, "This cooperation began a few years ago in an unorganized manner, and to this day the Nature and Parks Authority has operated Modiin in a self-directed way according to the extent of her understanding and abilities.

But intelligence is a professional field that is made up of different aspects, and includes people, open sources and a whole spectrum of confidential sources such as the Internet and other technological means from which information can be obtained that can be used to uncover capitals and criminals.
The basic understanding is that every enforcement body works more effectively and better when it has intelligence."
Snakes, spiders and parrots worth hundreds of thousands.

According to Donitsa, from the moment the agreement is signed, the intelligence coordinators of the Mageb will work with the intelligence tools at their disposal to gather intelligence that will allow the Nature and Parks Authority to uncover crimes of hunting wild animals and crimes of keeping or trading wild animals and protected natural values.
"The purpose of the intelligence is to help detect disclosure offenses.

These are crimes that are often committed in an open area, and if they are not randomly identified by law-abiding citizens who can report them or our inspectors who locate them, then they need to be exposed, and one of the tools for this is intelligence."
What animals are we talking about?
"The preferred wild animals for illegal hunting are deer and porcupines, mainly for food.

It is customary to smuggle and trade a lot, for example, in songbirds such as finches or rare parrots that are forbidden to import into Israel without a permit, or to take species out of the country, whether those that are unique to Israel or those that have already arrived here and want to continue transporting them to other parts of the world.

People trade and smuggle wild animals for all kinds of reasons because they want to keep a wild animal or trade it for financial reasons, believing that an animal's horn can be used for healing purposes, and even for collections of snakes, spiders or insects, which people travel around the world to import.
Everything is smuggled, and this is a very common offense that is dealt with all over the world."
Why is the cooperation carried out specifically with the Ministry of Defense?

"The working environment of the Israel Police is the cities, while the MGB operate in a rural, agricultural environment, in open areas, so naturally our areas of operation are much more tangential to the MGB than to the Israel Police.

Meanwhile, the cooperation between the two bodies is already recording successes.

"In one case we found in the yard of a private house in the center of the country a cage with rare parrots worth hundreds of thousands of shekels," says Donitsa, "in another case there was smuggling of rare parrots through Ramon Airport."
According to him, these join many other cases, where protected animals that were hunted for food were found in private homes.
"There is more intelligence information that is already being processed, and the results will not be late in arriving," he says.
Do you expect that this cooperation will reduce the amount of crimes?

"You always have to remember that what we see can only be the tip of the iceberg, and just as I don't know how many cases we haven't detected, I can't know how many cases we have prevented, but I really hope that it will indeed happen.
In a game between cops and thieves, or in this case inspectors and hunters, even the criminals will know very quickly that we double our strength.

It's a collaboration that should streamline and improve our work, and I want to believe that a certain percentage of criminals will tell themselves that maybe now it's not worth hunting for them anymore, because the risk of them being caught increases.

The route to rescue El Al runs between Washington and Berlin: here is the recommended outline for the Israeli version
, who since the outbreak of the crisis has been crying out for help from the government.
In order to adapt the aid package to society in a way that maximizes the benefit to the public, the Treasury needs to answer a number of basic questions.
The first question - is there room to provide dedicated aid to the airlines beyond the aid programs offered to the entire business sector?
If so, how should the assistance be provided?
Finally, the third question is, what should the government demand in return.
The answer to the first question is simple and is probably positive.
The aviation industry provides essential transportation infrastructure whose regular supply is important for the proper functioning of the economy.
The expression of this can be seen in the dedicated aid programs offered to the airlines by different countries.
For example, in the US, a $25 billion aid program was launched for the airlines, which aims to finance the salaries of the companies' employees during the crisis.
The European airlines requested support from the governments in the amount of about 30 billion euros, of which aid of about 13 billion euros was approved and the rest is in discussions.
Israel is no different in its dependence on civil aviation.
It can be argued that the dependence is even greater in the absence of land connection with the world.
The question of how to grant aid is more complex.
The government has several options: loans, guarantees, grants and capital investments.
For example, the American government provided aid in the form of a mix of loans and grants, with 70% of the $25 billion in aid given as grants and the rest as ten-year loans.
In Europe, in most cases, the aid is given as loans or guarantees from the countries to the airlines.
In two notable cases, the governments injected capital into companies in return for partial (Italian) control of the companies' share capital.

In the case of the outline that is on the agenda, it includes a bank loan of about 400 million dollars with a state guarantee of about 80%, subject to a capital injection of 100 million shekels by the shareholders as well as efficiency measures in the company.
This outline can suit companies with reasonable financial leverage, seeking to bridge the cash flow deficit during the crisis, but this is not the case in the case of El Al.
Even before the current crisis, El Al was one of the most leveraged airlines in the world, with a leverage ratio of more than 90%, while the global average was about 52%.
The current aid outline not only does not ease its debt burden but exacerbates it and increases the abnormal level of leverage.
Therefore, in my opinion, this is a wrong move by the Treasury, which will make it difficult for the company to exit the crisis and endanger the public funds used as a guarantee for the debt.
Another alternative is a direct grant to the company.
This solution will not serve the public's goals, because then it is a subsidy of the company's shareholders and debtors at the expense of the public.
Grants of this type are used in the world mainly in situations where the government subsidizes personnel costs in order to reduce unemployment during a crisis.
For example, in the American aid program, the airlines were required to commit not to lay off workers until September.
The Israeli government has already provided significant assistance to reduce unemployment in the form of a broad unemployment benefit program and incentives for employers to return workers to work.
If so, the only reasonable option is to inject capital into the company in exchange for shares.
Because of the company's low value, it is actually about taking over a significant part of its share capital.
This is a relatively unusual move that governments take from time to time.
Prominent examples are the bailout of the automobile industry and the bailout of the insurance company AIG by the US government in the 2008 crisis.
As part of the bailout, the government received ownership in the companies in exchange for an injection of capital.
The most current example was reported last week by the German airline Lufthansa.
According to the report, the company was given an aid package in the amount of 9 billion euros, for which the German government will receive a 20%-25% ownership of the company.
An argument that many raise against this move is the inefficiency of state ownership of business companies.
In order to reduce this inefficiency, the holding of shares can be held for a limited period and sold later to investors.
For example, this is how Israel behaved after the nationalization of the banks in the 1980s, and so did the US government when it realized its holdings in the companies it bailed out in 2008.
Finally, the third question is what the treasury should demand in exchange for the grant of aid.
The current outline emphasizes the demand for efficiency, reducing personnel, reducing lines and lowering costs.
This requirement is understandable due to the relatively low efficiency of the company even before the current crisis.
El Al is one of the international airlines with the lowest operating profitability in the world.
While the operating profit rate (excluding depreciation and amortization) of the company was about 11%, the global average in the industry was about 20%.

Therefore, the demands for efficiency seem reasonable, although as far as personnel cuts are concerned, this is a contradictory policy of the treasury, which invests billions in returning workers to the workplace.

It may be time to adopt a different policy: implement efficiency measures, but at the same time make significant capital investments in the company, to make it more competitive at the international level.
By increasing the capital, it is possible to expand the activity and optimize it based on the existing personnel, thus generating value without laying off workers.
Besides the concern for the efficiency of the company, there is room to take advantage of the opportunity to make structural changes in the Israeli aviation market.

For example, if we return to the example of the aid to Lufthansa, as part of the conditions of the aid, Lufthansa agreed to give up landing and takeoff rights at central airports in Frankfurt and Munich, as well as aircraft rights in favor of its competitors.
These requirements of the state arose from the desire to encourage competition on certain lines in Europe.
In my opinion, the government's adoption of the outline detailed here towards the local airlines may lead to a better economic result for the public as well.
Asher Shekler, CPA, is a managing partner in the Varians School of Economic and Financial Consulting.

On what has already been called "the night of the elimination of the accounts", several platforms went out during an extensive purge that cleaned some of the most dangerous accounts and users from the network: Reddit closed the wild subreddit of Trump supporters The_Donald (and another 2,000 other subreddits), YouTube removed the accounts of some users who support white supremacy (and Trump) prominent, and Twitch helped bravely suspend (temporarily) Trump's account.

These came after the moves of Twitter and Facebook to mark, in a small way and with great fear, Trump's tweets as false or inciting violence.
All excellent and worthy moves, even with too late and not comprehensive enough.

But, as Dr. Joan Donovan, research director of the Center for the Study of Media, Politics and Public Policy at the Kennedy School of Government at Harvard University, argues, when it comes to steps that can be taken to deal with problems such as the spread of misinformation, inflammatory and divisive discourse and users who take advantage of the platform given to them in order to promote racism, violence and just hatred of people in general, moves such as blocking accounts and deleting or flagging content are only one half of the methods of action that can be taken to improve the discourse on social media.
And not even necessarily the most important half.
Because alongside a direct fight against negative content, it is necessary to take active action in order to improve the visibility of positive content.

The question of how social networks deal with harmful content is almost as long as the history of the newsfeed on Facebook - the tool that significantly increased exposure to content created by surfers and rescued them from the relative ghetto of their profile page.

At the beginning, a significant part of the discussion focused on Facebook's own content removal policy, and especially on its fierce and delusional fight against bare nipples and breastfeeding women.

Essential questions, such as dealing with fake news or content that encourages violence, have been at the center of the conversation in recent years, following the 2016 US presidential elections and the massacre of the Rohingya minority in Myanmar.

Facebook had already operated human content filters for several years before, but in 2018 made content filtering its main strategy in dealing with problematic content, when founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg testified before Congress in April of that year that the company is on record as hiring 20,000 people for its content filtering system (Hire is a misleading word, since the content filters are employed through contractor companies and are not Facebook employees).
Since then, the content filtering policy of Facebook and other social networks has been in focus whenever it comes to fake news or inflammatory and divisive content.

This policy is also the main reason for the extensive boycott campaign against Facebook, which has already succeeded in sweeping away hundreds of advertisers, including quite a few prominent companies and brands.
And there is room to discuss the principles that guide social networks regarding which content they allow and which content they prohibit on their platforms.

But as Donovan writes in an article she published on Wired, as long as the discussion and activism focus only on what content to keep and what content to remove, the battle against incitement, racism, hate and fake news will remain a losing battle.
Because at the same time as the policy of removing negative content, the social networks also need a policy of promoting the promotion of positive content, what Donovan calls "retention".
"Without a strategy for how to curate content, technology companies will always be one step behind the manipulators, the disseminators of false information and the promoters of hate and fear."

While content filtering focuses on removing harmful things, Donovan emphasizes the importance of curation as a means of finding content that can help the user, put what is happening around him in an appropriate context and above all promote accuracy and truth.

"The truth needs an advocate, and it needs to come in the form of a huge horde of librarians who will storm Silicon Valley and create the Internet we deserve, an ecosystem of information that serves the people," she explained.
"The blessing and curse of social media is that it must remain open for us to enjoy its benefits.
Platform companies have an obligation to curate content on controversial topics so that their systems do not increase hatred or make it profitable.
Technology companies that refuse to adapt to the culture will become obsolete."

"There are a lot of failures and fickle statements that make our work difficult," said a high school teacher from the center of the country, "Nothing is clear, the Ministry of Education said that coming to school is not mandatory - so how am I supposed to prepare the students for matriculation, how can I take responsibility for them? ".

The confusion among the teachers comes against the background of the instructions published yesterday by Prof. Sigal Sadatsky, head of public health services at the Ministry of Health, according to which "if there are more than 3 patients in the institution (even if they are all from the same class) the closure of the entire institution should be preferred."

It is also written that "if there are 3 or less patients, but they are spread over several classes or alternatively in the case of a teacher who teaches in several classes, the closure of the institution or an entire age group should be preferred."
On the other hand, the Minister of Education Yoav Galant ordered that a school where one patient is found - will be closed.
However, Gallant emphasized that in schools where study routines are held in separate complexes - partial activation will be considered.

Ynet has learned that one of the measures being considered by the Ministry of Health is the closure of the education system in the authorities where infections were detected in several schools in the same city at the same time.
"The conflicting instructions of the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Health are very confusing," noted a high school teacher from the center of the country.
"The unqualified statement between one and the other makes us stand in front of parents and students in an unclear way.

The Ministry of Education said that coming to school is voluntary, i.e. not mandatory, so how am I supposed to prepare the students for matriculation and how am I supposed to take responsibility for them?
"There are a lot of failures and fickle statements that make our work difficult, nothing here is clear," added the teacher.
"Everyone wants to show that they have the upper hand and maximize their political status.
It turns out that they confuse us and make it difficult for us."
Hila, a mother of a student and a high school student from the central region, said: "I don't need anyone to tell me what to do, I decide whether to send the children or not.
If I see that there is a patient at school, I will unequivocally not send.
If I had followed the instructions of the Ministry of Health, my situation would have been very bad.
Many teachers and parents are of the opinion that this is a very irresponsible repetition of the students.
There is a possibility that the 4th-10th grades will be allowed to return to studying at home until the end of the year to thin out the crowds at the schools.
Especially the students of the division."

Last night, Health Minister Yuli Edelstein announced the expansion of the corona testing policy, contrary to the position of his office's senior officials as presented so far, so that even people without symptoms can be tested, and this at the discretion of the attending physician.

Edelstein referred to the parameters presented regarding the possibility of canceling the reliefs which included 100 patients per day who are not affected by the outbreak, 250 patients in serious condition and a doubling rate of 10 days in the number of patients: "Thank God we are not there, we do not want to be there, so I repeat the importance of the public's cooperation.
You all saw what happened last weekend and I don't think anyone would argue that the rules were followed.
Therefore, if we don't want to cross the lines and reach a situation of closures once again, then it is very important for us to expand the tests and for the public to cooperate."
The vast majority of the patients diagnosed in recent days are from Jerusalem, and as of yesterday 129 of the city's residents were diagnosed with the virus.
Most of them are students and teachers at the Jerusalem Hebrew High School, where according to the updated data, 141 high school students and staff members have already been infected with Corona.
In second place is Tel Aviv, where seven new patients were diagnosed.
Earlier, two students at the Paula Ben Gurion School, in grades 3 and 5, were diagnosed with the virus.
The school was closed until June 10, and its 472 students went into home isolation.

The municipality of Bnei Brak, where, according to the latest data, one person has been infected in the last three days, announced increased enforcement after, according to it, a loosening of the guidelines in the synagogues and in the public space was detected.

The municipality's announcement states that "Along with the great joy and excitement of our return to the synagogues, in light of the tangible fear of an outbreak of another illness in the city and a feeling of laxity in maintaining the procedures, it was decided in an emergency meeting on enforcement measures.
The collectors will be fined heavily.
In the first step, warning reports will be given and in addition, an immediate enforcement operation will be launched throughout the city for not wearing a mask in the public space."
"I don't think you can leave a conference call on bank profitability and feel that the worst is already behind us"
The big banks estimate that the recession created by the corona epidemic will leave scorched earth in large parts of corporate America.
When they reported their second quarter results last week, major American banks said they do not expect the US economy to soon emerge from the slowdown it has entered.
A prolonged slowdown, they said, bodes ill for all types of businesses, even those not directly affected by the travel bans and social distancing regulations imposed to curb the virus.
Between the first quarter and the second, the four largest banks in the US almost doubled the amount of money they set aside to cover unpaid business loans.
In the first quarter, the banks mainly increased provisions to cover consumer debts.
Even what seemed like good news was not really so.

Investment banking revenues rose in the second quarter, but not from advising CEOs on deals, but simply because banks charged more fees for helping companies accumulate cash to ride out the recession.
"Everybody's in trouble, really," Bill Demchek, CEO of PNC Financial Services Group, said on a conference call last Wednesday.

"The normal corporate client we talk to, who is open and doing business, is almost without exception in a decline from what he expected at the beginning of the year, and in a decline from where he was last year."
Banks have very good visibility of the health of US consumers and businesses.
They hold the deposits, engineer the mergers and lend the money.
They see what goes into the customers' deposits, what comes out of them and where the money is invested or where it is spent.
In the second quarter they saw some particularly worrying things.
One after the other, bank managers are warning that the worst part of the corona recession is yet to come.
They said they no longer foresee a quick return to healthy economic activity or high employment.

"I don't think anyone should come out of a conference call on bank profitability this quarter and feel that the worst is behind us, and that the road to recovery is paved," Citigroup CEO Michael Corbett told analysts last Tuesday.
"I don't want to be pessimistic, but I want to be realistic."
The four major banks - JP Morgan Chase, Citigroup, Bank of America and Wells Fargo - set aside $33 billion in the second quarter to cover loans that could go bad.
Loans to businesses and companies accounted for $16.8 billion of this total, up from $8.8 billion in the first quarter (Bank of America set aside less to cover loan losses than the other banks.
CEO Brian Moynahan said there are encouraging initial signs for the turnaround).
JPMorgan, the leading bank in terms of assets, allocated $4.6 billion to commercial loan losses, up from $2.4 billion in the first quarter.
The provision to cover consumer loan losses remained at $4.4 billion.
"In the first quarter, when we saw a sharp but short-term economic slowdown, we focused more on the sectors that were hit the hardest," said JPMorgan CFO Jennifer Pipshack.
"Now we see a more prolonged slowdown, and we have reserves for a wider projection across many sectors."
The customers are also digging.
Even after some signs of improvement in the economy, bankers said, companies are still deep in the phase of emergency preparedness and cash hoarding.
When America shut down in March to beat the coronavirus, companies hoarded cash by drawing on their lines of credit.
In the following months, the companies paid off the debt and replaced it with new loans, bonds or convertible bonds.
JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs have all had successful quarters for their investment banks thanks to these offerings.
"People are scared, and they're also responding by depositing cash in banks and pre-empting their borrowing needs as much as they can," said Wells Fargo analyst Mike Mayo.
Some companies have issued bonds or shares more than once.
Delta Airlines, which was hit hard by the pandemic, was among the bond market's repeat customers in the second quarter.
Companies more insulated from the crisis, such as Netflix and Slack Technologies, also raised capital.
In good times, all this borrowing was expected to encourage investment and expansion, but businesses park the money in their bank accounts.
The U.S. banking system has added $2.2 trillion in deposits so far this year, three times more than in any other six-month period on record, according to Federal Reserve data.
"We can't predict the future," JPMorgan CEO James Damon told analysts.
"We don't know anything.
The phrase 'unprecedented' is almost never used correctly.
But this time it is being used properly."
Due to the economic crisis in Lebanon, Hezbollah offers to purchase oil from Iran
The Lebanese pound has lost about 80% of its value since October, and Nasrallah said talks are underway with the government in Beirut about a deal with Tehran.

Meanwhile, a Hezbollah businessman who was jailed in the US returned to Lebanon after receiving early release, but Pompeo makes it clear that there will be no aid to Lebanon if it becomes a "puppet state"
Hezbollah proposed to the Lebanese government to purchase oil from Iran in exchange for Lebanese pounds, to ease the pressure on Beirut's currency reserves.
The country is suffering from an acute economic crisis and a liquidity problem.
The Lebanese pound has lost about 80% of its value since October, with the explosion of the crisis that had been brewing for a long time.
The Shia organization believes that Lebanon should turn east, in light of the American sanctions imposed on it due to its ties to Tehran.
In a speech he gave on Tuesday, Hezbollah Secretary General Hassan Nasrallah said that "calm talks" are underway with the government, which his organization supports, on the issue of aid from Iran.
"We started discussions, to see where we can move forward with this option," Nasrallah said.
"This track is progressing, what will be the result?
I don't know, but we have to try."
The Hezbollah leader added that Iran will deliver its official position on the issue at the appropriate time.
The close relationship between Hezbollah and Iran, its patron, keeps the United States and the Sunni Gulf states away from investing in Lebanon.

The United States defines Hezbollah as a terrorist organization, and it urges Beirut to pass economic reforms to get out of the worst crisis it has experienced since the civil war, which ended in 1990.

"Make no mistake about what the United States has done and will do to pressure Hezbollah and also to try to help the Lebanese people build a successful government," said US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo yesterday.
"Hezbollah is a terrorist organization and we support Lebanon as long as they pass the reforms and they don't become a puppet state of Iran."
Pompeo refused to address questions about the release of Lebanese businessman Kassem Taj ad-Din, who returned to Lebanon from the United States yesterday.
He was sent to five years in prison last year after being convicted of laundering millions of dollars for Hezbollah while circumventing US sanctions.

He was arrested in Morocco and extradited to the United States in 2017, and a State Department official in Washington told The Associated Press that the administration opposed his early release, but the court granted his request.
The source added that Taj al-Din, which was put on the terrorist list in 2009, will remain there even after the release and its assets will continue to be frozen.
The source, who maintained anonymity, added that his early release does not reduce the severity of the offenses.
Officials in Lebanon have not yet commented on the early release of the 64-year-old businessman, who was welcomed upon landing at Beirut airport, wearing a mask.

According to reports, the decision to release him, which was ordered by a federal judge in May, was due to his health condition and the fear of the spread of the corona virus in prisons in the United States.
As part of his guilty plea last December, the Lebanese businessman agreed to pay a fine of 50 million dollars.

It is not clear if the early release has anything to do with the decision made by a military court in Lebanon in March, which ordered the release of former SDF senior officer Amr Fakhuri, who had been held in custody for about six months.
This led to speculation that Tajuddin might be released in exchange for Fakhuri, who was granted US citizenship last year.
Another point of contention between Hezbollah and the United States concerns the words of the American ambassador in Beirut, who attacked the Shiite organization.

Nasrallah said the ambassador, Dorothy Shea, had interfered in the country's internal affairs and that Hezbollah members of parliament would submit a request to the Foreign Ministry to summon her and demand that she abide by diplomatic norms.

Despite the tensions, the commander of the United States Army Central Command, General Kenneth McKenzie, visited Lebanon yesterday and met with President Michel Aoun and senior political and military officials.
Although Hezbollah is designated a terrorist organization by the United States, it provides significant aid to the Lebanese army.

According to the American embassy, ​​the general stressed to the Lebanese president the "importance in maintaining the security, stability and sovereignty of Lebanon" and the firm cooperation between the armies of the two countries.
McKenzie even made a short stop at the memorial sites for American soldiers who were killed while serving in Lebanon.
In 1983, nearly 260 Americans and 63 other people were killed in attacks on the American embassy and the Marine headquarters in Beirut.
His visit sparked anti-American protests in Lebanon.

Dozens gathered near the airport, which was under heavy security, and some shouted "death to America" ​​and expressed support for the attacks, while waving the flags of Hezbollah and the Communist Party.
Others burned a picture of the American embassy and Israeli flags.
Accelerated changes in the labor market will hurt the weak
After Israel crossed the threshold of one million unemployed and reached 25% unemployment, the March summary report of the Employment Service provides additional reasons for concern.
The first, confirms a fear that has been floating in the air for several weeks: the main victims of the crisis are the weakest: many of them are residents of Arab and Orthodox cities.
Second, the corona crisis accelerates the transition to the new labor market.
This may result in the mass cancellation of jobs in the world and in the Israeli economy.

Already last week it became clear that the crisis mainly affects the weak, when the National Insurance Institute announced that the average wage of the newly unemployed is 28% lower than the average wage in the economy.

This fact is also true outside of crisis days: the average salary of unemployment claimants in 2019 was only NIS 7,720 compared to the average salary in the economy which was NIS 10,800 during this period.

Yesterday the employment service published the unemployment data by city and it became clear that the cities leading the list of the unemployed are Arab, ultra-Orthodox or weak cities that usually also have an Arab or ultra-Orthodox population.

For the ultra-Orthodox, the fact that many of them work in private education, which is partly supported by donations and payments from parents, contributes greatly to this, and therefore the workers were taken out of the salaried state.
Among the Arabs, the large number of workers in the tourism, restaurant and food businesses, as well as private education, contributes to this.

In the list of localities plagued by unemployment, the city of Eilat is in first place, where 70% of the workers were put on unpaid leave or fired and it has effectively become an unemployed locality.
This is of course due to the fact that most residents of Eilat make a living from working in hotels and food and leisure businesses.
Unemployment and humanitarian crisis.
Much more surprising is the fact that in second place are the ultra-Orthodox Beitar Ilit with 52%, fourth is the ultra-Orthodox Modi'in Ilit (35%) and fifth is Bnei Brak (34%).
There is no book that the ultra-orthodox are the main victims of the corona crisis, not only because of the carelessness they showed in the first week.
Another factor is, of course, the severe donation crisis born from the inability to reach the United States and the fact that the corona is hitting New York so hard as well - the seat of many donors.
The most important Arab city Nazareth is in third place with 47% unemployment.
Rahat and Umm El Fahm in the sixth and seventh places with 33%.

Yesterday at the meeting of the Knesset's special committee to deal with the corona epidemic, the ministries of health and the interior reported that at this stage there does not seem to be a significant spread of the corona in the Arab sector.
This is evident from the tests conducted in recent days and also from the proportion of Arabs among the severe cases.
In terms of health, the situation is better than with the ultra-Orthodox.
Economically, both sectors seem to be moving rapidly towards a serious crisis.
A blow to the weak workers.
One possible reason for mass job losses could be a possible continuation of the corona crisis.
"As the crisis drags on, the chance that we will experience the most severe economic recession in the last decades - will increase," states the employment service.
This means that there is a great chance that Israel is heading for a crisis the likes of which we have not encountered since the great recession of the 1960s.

The Prime Minister and the outgoing Minister of Finance, Moshe Kahlon, constantly remind us how important it is that we reached the crisis with a strong economy, low unemployment and an excellent debt-to-GDP ratio.

This is true, and despite this, the employment service makes it clear that the depth of the crisis does not depend only on us, and if the economy in the United States falls ill with Corona, our economy will also need a ventilator.
"The United States is the benchmark for global crises," they say there.
"If unemployment in the United States continues over time, the impact on us will be significant."
The most difficult statement in the report is the update in the forecasts of the International Labor Organization.

About two weeks ago, the organization issued a report in which it predicted that the corona crisis would lead to the disappearance of 25 million jobs, to a significant increase in unemployment rates in the various countries, to the expansion of the phenomenon of poor workers, and to the fact that millions of people would enter a situation of employment below their qualifications.

However, last Thursday the organization's researchers admitted that their estimates were much lower than what the global epidemic requires, and updated their forecast for the disappearance of 200 million jobs worldwide.
The economic crisis is not the only reason for the expected job loss.
Another reason is the worldwide experiment conducted last month in remote work by digital means.
It turned out that countless things that are considered to require a direct meeting, from taking out a mortgage to filing a complaint with the police, can be done by digital means.
When the jobs that are in danger are as usual those of the weak workers.
America Israel Chamber of Commerce CEO Oded Rose is the initiator of the Outsight project to advance Israel into the future world of work.
Rose says that "following the crisis, processes in the world of work that were supposed to take five to ten years will take two or three years.
There are jobs in the service industries that are going to disappear, because everything can be done remotely.
These people go home or do something else."
According to him, the fact that the crisis has paralyzed factories will encourage the owners to introduce robotics.

Another change that Rose foresees is the transition of people to work from home as well as to work in several parts of a job, for example an engineer who is also a teacher, when the payment will be made in one slip.
This is because the employers discovered that they do not need complete jobs in all cases and the young workers tend to prefer working for several employers.

Accelerating the transition to the future labor market following the corona crisis is expected to be very effective for employers, providing for skilled workers, but it will probably crush tens of thousands of weak workers.
The epidemic caused distance between Israel and the Diaspora - we must fix this

The corona epidemic caused a distance in the relations between the State of Israel and Diaspora Jewry, a distance born from the distinction between Israeli citizens and Jewish citizens of other countries.
For most Diaspora Jews, until recently, it was almost impossible to enter the Jewish state.

Besides the pain of families being separated from each other, especially at key moments in their lives, there is the emotional and spiritual trauma of Jews who were forbidden to enter the Jewish homeland for the first time since the establishment of the State of Israel.
Back in December 2020, Israel began its vaccination campaign before any other country, vaccinating almost the entire adult population.
Jews in the diaspora were proud of these achievements.
There was then an opportunity for Israel to become a vaccination center for those who are willing to come and be vaccinated and follow all the isolation protocols.
Admittedly, these are complex issues and complicated times, but Israel is not like any other country.
This is the Jewish state.
And as such, its duties go beyond its own citizens.
The matter goes to the heart of Jewish identity.
The connection to the land is more than 3,800 years old when God said to Abraham, "Go, go...to the land that I will show you".
The Jewish nation was united at Sinai when we received our divine mission, the part of which as always was that we were all "as one man with one heart".
As the Talmud says, "Worships for each other".
The modern state of Israel is the inheritor of this history; Its national vocation, the mission and purpose of the Jewish people, derives from it.
It is a state that gives meaning and expression to an idea - it is not just a political entity operating within designated borders.
The founders of the country understood this deep meaning, and expressed it through the "Law of Return", which grants the Jews of the world the right to immigrate to Israel and obtain citizenship.

From the extraordinary efforts to absorb Russian and CIS Jewry after the breakup of the Soviet Union, to the dramatic flight of Ethiopian Jews from Sudan and Ethiopia in the late 1980s and early 1990s, the message to Jews in need: We are here for you.
These feelings are mutual, and this message is always also sent back from the Diaspora to Israel.

From the beginning of the project called the State of Israel there was a full partnership with the Diaspora; A partnership in which Jews around the world invested enormous resources - money, political capital, even blood.
During the War of Independence, South African Jews volunteered for the IDF and defended the nascent country against invading armies.

South African Jews have continued to make an extraordinary contribution to the Jewish state, building schools, hospitals and other infrastructure, including the recently completed Samson Assuta Medical Center in Ashdod - the first hospital in Israel that is completely protected against missiles.
More than that, as proud Zionists, we championed Israel's position in the press and in public and international forums.
We are still at the forefront of the fight against BDS and their efforts to deny the legitimacy of the Jewish state.
We led the fight against our own government in defense of our beloved State of Israel.
Our enemies do not recognize the negligible distinction between Jews and Israelis.
Even in the last war in Gaza, anti-Semitic attacks increased all over the world.
Because we are truly one people.
This is the founding principle of the State of Israel and the great agreement between Israel and Diaspora Jewry.
During this pandemic we see that the agreement is being eroded.
Not sure there are simple solutions.
But I firmly believe that the welfare of Diaspora Jewry must be a central factor in the government's decisions.
There is a violation of the contract between Israel and Diaspora Jewry.
Fortunately, the breach is fixable.
Israel's relationship with the Diaspora is strong.
Even in these difficult times, Jewish immigrants arrived in increasing numbers and were welcomed with open arms.
This is an example of the depth of the relationship.
The fate of Israel and world Jewry are intertwined.
We share a common vocation and mission.
We are each other's guarantees.
Rabbi Dr. Ze'ev Warren Goldstein is the chief rabbi for the Jews of South Africa, a doctor of law and an expert on human rights.
After more than a year: the first group of tourists landed in Israel
The first group of foreign tourists landed today (Thursday) at Ben Gurion Airport as part of an outline initiated by the Ministry of Tourism, led by the Minister of Tourism, Orit Farkash HaCohen.
Flight UA 90 landed today at 16:11 in Tel Aviv with foreign tourists on board.
As they got off the plane, they were greeted by Tourism Minister Farkash HaCohen and the Director General of the Ministry of Tourism, Amir Halevi.
According to the conditions of the experimental phase, the group must be in isolation and social distancing until the arrival of negative results for the corona tests.
This is a group of 12 Christian pilgrims from the United States, of various ages, who are studying theology at CONCORDIA SEMINARY in the state of Missouri.
The visit is part of their curriculum, and it will count as part of their study hours.
The group will stay in Israel until June 10.
The members of the group are Protestants, for whom the tour route was adapted.
The group will visit Jerusalem, field resources in the Negev, Masada, Nazareth, and near the Golan as well as 15 national parks in addition to Christian sites.
They are accompanied by Pastor Dr. Tom Zelt, who brings groups to Israel several times a year, and who trains pastors, who are also expected to bring groups to Israel.

The experimental phase of the entry of tourist groups was launched in April of this year, after many efforts by the Minister of Tourism, Orit Parkash and Cohen and in cooperation with the Ministers of Health, Transportation, Foreign Affairs and the Interior, and resulted in a great deal of interest from tourism organizers.
As part of the experimental phase, 20 groups of tourists will be hosted in Israel, having received a vaccine recognized by the Ministry of Health in Israel.
The countries authorized to participate in the experimental phase are those that meet the requirements of the Ministry of Health.
Also, the tourists participating in the pilot must perform two PCR tests - one up to 72 hours before entering the country and one upon their arrival.
The group that entered today undergoes the serological test at the hotel where they will be staying and will begin the visit upon receiving the answers.
Each group will have up to 30 participants.
In the next stages of the plan, the arrival of groups of tourists will be allowed without restriction.
After that, individual tourists will arrive and in the final stage - a wide opening and a return to normality.

The Minister of Tourism, Orit Farkash HaCohen said that "After over a year the skies of Israel were closed to tourists - today an exciting event took place that we worked hard on at the Ministry of Tourism - the first group of tourists will land in Israel.

Every process begins with a first step and today is a sign of the beginning, for the revival of the tourism industry that has been bleeding for over a year, for economic growth and a real return to normality."
The minister added: "This is only the first stage of a gradual process.
This is the result of my great effort as Minister of Tourism in cooperation with the Ministers of the Interior, Foreign Affairs, Transport and Health.

Until we bring the tourists back to Israel, the hundreds of thousands of workers in the hospitality industry, catering, transportation, guides and many tourist cities such as Tiberias, Nazareth, Jerusalem and Haifa will not recover.
According to the summary, in the next step we will allow the arrival of groups of tourists without restriction and then, individual tourists until a wide and full opening.

I have every hope that the process will be completed successfully and the state coffers will return and enjoy at the end of the corona crisis - the billions of shekels that the tourism industry brought into the state coffers in previous years."
Israel will deliver corona vaccines to the West Bank as part of an agreement with the PA, Gaza will not be included

As part of an exchange deal that took shape during the days of the Netanyahu government, the new Prime Minister and Minister of Health approved the transfer of one million doses of vaccine, which will soon expire, to the Authority in exchange for receiving the next shipment that Pfizer intended to send to the Palestinians.
At this stage the agreement is valid only in the territories of Judea and Samaria and not in the Gaza Strip

Israel will transfer to the West Bank about one million Pfizer corona vaccines, as part of an exchange deal with the Palestinian Authority - this was announced today (Friday) in a joint statement by the ministries of the Prime Minister, Defense and Health.
The Prime Minister's Office stated that the decision was made after staff work and in accordance with the recommendation of the Ministries of Defense and Health.
As part of the agreement, Israel will transfer to the Palestinian Authority 1-1.4 million Pfizer vaccine doses against the corona virus that are in Israel and will soon expire.

According to the agreement, in exchange for the vaccines that will be transferred to the Palestinian Authority, Israel will receive the same amount of new vaccine doses from the Pfizer company during the months of September-October 2021, at the expense of the shipment intended for the PA.
The Prime Minister's Office stated that the outline was approved in light of the fact that Israel's stock of vaccines meets all needs today.

According to sources familiar with the details of the deal, the move to transfer the vaccines was previously approved in principle by former Prime Minister Netanyahu, but the implementation of the move was delayed.
They added that at this stage, within the framework of the agreement, vaccines will be transferred to the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank only, and not to the Gaza Strip.

The negotiations on the agreement began during the previous government and were conducted by the director general of the Ministry of Health Hezi Levy and the head of the international division in the ministry, Ashi Shalmon, in front of the Palestinian Authority's corona projector.
Levy and Shalmon conducted the negotiations in coordination with the National Security Headquarters during the time of former Prime Minister Netanyahu.

During the opening meeting between Levy and the new Minister of Health Nitzan Horowitz, the Director General of the Ministry of Health informed Horowitz about the negotiations that took place during the previous government.

Sources in the health minister's office said that Horowitz called on Levy to push the negotiations with all his might and emphasized that at the same time he would raise the issue with Prime Minister Naftali Bennett to get his approval, and later that day Horowitz called Bennett.

The Prime Minister got back to him within three hours, saying that he had no objection in principle, but asked for a final inspection of the National Security Headquarters and the security establishment.
The MLA and the Ministry of Defense approved the move.
But then another problem arose.
The agreement with Pfizer does not allow the transfer of vaccines to a third party without the company's approval.
The Ministry of Health officials contacted Pfizer and asked for its approval.
After a short negotiation, approval was obtained and we could move forward with the agreement.
Officials in the health minister's office said that some of the vaccine doses, about 100,000, will be transferred to the Palestinian Authority today.
In total, approximately 1.2 million vaccine doses will be transferred to the Authority.
Istanbul: The round of talks between Ukraine and Russia ended without results
The next round of talks between Ukraine and Russia in the city of Istanbul ended without results.
Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich, who acts as a "mediator" for the Russians, was also present at the talks.
Russia has announced that it will formulate a practical mechanism for foreign companies so that they can pay for gas in rubles.
"No one will supply gas for free.
It is impossible, and it can only be paid for in rubles," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

Another round of talks between Ukraine and Russia is expected to begin in Istanbul as fighting continues on the ground as the two sides battle for control of the city in eastern Ukraine and a suburb of the capital Kyiv.
Ukrainian forces have retaken Irpin, northwest of Kiev, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelzansky said last night.
"We still have to fight, we have to hold on," he said in his nightly video speech.
"We must not express our feelings now.
We mustn't raise our expectations so we don't wear ourselves out," he added.
Ahead of the talks in Istanbul, the Ukrainian president said that his country is ready to declare neutrality, as Moscow demanded, which may have a positive effect on the negotiations.
The President of Turkey, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, said this morning that advances in talks between the negotiators may pave the way for a meeting between the leaders of Russia and Ukraine.
He was charged that the time had come for the talks to produce concrete results and called for an immediate ceasefire.
"Stopping the tragedy is the responsibility of both sides."
Report in Ukraine: A local telecommunications company suffered a major cyber attack.
The Special Communications Service of Ukraine reported that Ukraine's telephone and Internet company, Ukrtelecom, suffered a major cyber attack.
The agency said Russian forces were responsible.
The company is the largest Internet provider in the country in terms of geographic coverage, and second only to Kyivstar in terms of the number of customers.

The provider reduced service to most private users and business customers during the attack so that it could continue to provide it to the Army of Ukraine, the Technical Security and Intelligence Service of Ukraine.
NetBlocks, an independent global internet monitor, reported that this was the worst attack on the provider since Russia invaded Ukraine last month.
It was also reported that several hours passed before the company was able to stop the attack and restore normal services to all customers.

In its latest operational update, the ministry said the group is expected to deploy more than 1,000 people -- including senior leaders of the group -- to "conduct combat operations" in Ukraine.

The important test that went into the basket but no one bothered to update you
In January 2020, eligibility for a free genetic screening test to detect mutations in the BRCA gene for women aged 25 and over of Ashkenazi origin entered the health basket.
Certain mutations in this gene significantly increase the risk of getting cancer, especially ovarian cancer.
Among Ashkenazi women, the frequency of the dangerous mutations is relatively high and stands at 1 in 40, so it was decided to allow them to undergo this genetic screening test free of charge.

However, although the test went into the basket and many women are entitled to perform it for free, and despite the fact that it is a simple blood test, until recently the response of women from the general public was quite low.
And the reason for this is probably the lack of sufficient awareness of the test and the eligibility conditions.
This situation greatly disturbed Dr. Lena Sagia-Dain, a gynecologist and geneticist from the Carmel Hospital and a senior lecturer at the Technion.

Dr. Sagia Dain wrote a poignant and witty post on her Facebook page, in which she explained in simple language the importance of the test, the conditions of eligibility and also gave vent to her frustration that the health insurance funds do not communicate this important information well enough to their insureds, something that has a large part in the degree of compliance the low
Dr. Sagi-Dain's post quickly became viral and was shared more than a thousand times in women's groups on Facebook, in private profiles and was also passed on WhatsApp from woman to woman.

In a follow-up post that she put up a few days later, Dr. Sagia-Dain already got into the thick of it and due to the great interest shown by the women's public, she gathered information from the various health insurance funds and even from the IDF regarding the procedure for receiving a referral for testing (the procedure differs from insurance fund to insurance fund).

In a telephone conversation with her today and after contacting the representatives of the various health insurance funds, Dr. Sagia-Dain is now less stingy towards them: "The Ministry of Health has been talking about putting the test in the basket since January 2020, but it is a big project and it took time for the insurance funds to organize for it, only now are they Really prepared for it," she says.

Let's not forget that during this year they also dealt with the corona epidemic and with the logistics of deploying a nationwide vaccination system, so it is possible that there really is a justified reason for the delay in communicating the eligibility for testing to the insured.
"It sounds like following my post there really was an increase in applications to the health insurance funds, I heard from several places that they were flooded with applications.
I wrote it in my own style and I have a lot of readers so I wanted to act in as many directions as possible to raise awareness for women.
The truth is, I didn't think it would be so viral, but it caught on well," she concludes.
Breast cancer - the most common among women in Israel.
Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women in Israel.
It develops following genetic mutations that cause healthy breast cells to become malignant.
The most common genetic mutations that cause breast cancer are in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes.
Women (and men) who carry the mutations in these genes have an increased risk of getting several types of cancer, especially breast cancer and ovarian cancer.
Also, the mutation increases the risk of getting sick at a younger age.
"Mutations in this gene are found in all ethnic groups, but for Ashkenazis the risk is 1 in 40, which is a lot.
That's a 2.5 percent risk.
This increases the risk mainly of breast and ovarian cancer, therefore if carriers are discovered, then the recommendation is for a very organized follow-up in favor of early detection.
Usually this follow-up will include an examination by a breast surgeon twice a year and an imaging test once a year.

In addition, carriers of the mutations in the BRCA gene are also entitled to a breast MRI test, which women who are not in the risk group are not entitled to," explains Dr. Shagia-Dain of the practical implications of the test.

Along with the close follow-up, the carriers will receive information about all the treatment options open to them, including complete excision of the breast and ovaries (as the actress Angelina Jolie chose to do several years ago).

"There is a difference between the breast and the ovaries," points out Dr. Sagia-Dain, "the breast has good tests for the early detection of cancer and the ovaries have less - there is currently an ultrasound test and a blood test for the early detection of ovarian cancer, but they are still not good enough.
It is a cancer that is often discovered late and is relatively aggressive.
Therefore, a woman who is pregnant has a fairly unequivocal recommendation to have her ovaries removed, after she finishes giving birth."

A spokesman for the United States Embassy in Jerusalem refused to comment on diplomatic talks with the Israeli government.

The Prime Minister's Office also refused to comment on the matter.
