In addition, the White House knows that tensions with Israel regarding the settlements will expose Bennett to attacks from the right, something that could harm the stability of the government - something that the Americans want to avoid as well.
Senior officials at the Ministry of Health fear the expansion of the green classroom: "It cannot be determined that it is safe"

Senior officials at the Ministry of Health said today (Tuesday) to Walla! Because they do not agree with the expansion of the green class outline, because there is not enough data to determine whether it is safe.
Last night the outline was increased to 90% of the settlements in Israel, after it was also extended to yellow cities, starting from Sunday.
The reason for the paucity of data is the short time that has passed since the beginning of the outline in the green cities, only a week ago.

The Ministry of Health explained that in the current state of morbidity, the decided outline is "reasonable" and will not cause the infection rate to rise above 1, although there is a high chance that it will lead to multiple infections.

From yesterday's discussion, it appears that only half of the classes required for the pilot were recruited, and in the classes that were recruited, the elements of the outline were partially implemented.
According to the Ministry of Health data, only 50% of the students in isolation performed the second antigen test on the seventh day, and less than 25% reported in a computerized manner.
Also, manual reports were not collected, and the information required to carry out control was not available in the Ministry of Education.
The data also shows that of the 400 children verified in the pilot, only 30% performed a PCR test after they came out positive in the rapid antigen tests. 80% of the subjects tested positive.
Also, 75% of those infected who came out negative in the antigen test, were found to be positive in the PCR test.
Wow! It was learned that in the "Eshkol" school in Rosh Ha'Ain, 65 confirmed cases were discovered in the last two weeks.
The district doctor recommended closing the school, but studies there continue as usual after the Ministry of Education's objection to its closing.

Despite the pleas of Health Minister Nitzan Horowitz and Education Minister Yifat Shasha Biton, due to the paucity of data, the Ministry of Health opposed expanding the outline in red and orange communities because there may be excess morbidity in at least 50% of them.
Senior officials at the Ministry of Education said, Wow!
Because the Ministry of Health claimed that there was not enough data, but they did not claim that the plan was dangerous.
However, officials in the Ministry of Health claimed that they are only an "advisory body" and they cannot stop the decision makers.
In the end, Prime Minister Naftali Bennett did not agree to expand the outline to red and orange settlements and the proposal fell through.
Only 8% of the settlements are not part of the map.
There are currently 72,315 isolated students in the education system, of which 9,959 are verified.
The data from the Ministry of Health shows that only 8% of the settlements in Israel are red or orange, and the outline will not apply to them.

According to the green class outline that has been in effect until now, in the class in which a confirmed patient is discovered, the students of the class will be tested with a PCR test that will be performed at the frontline command posts or the health funds.

The students will remain in isolation until a negative answer is received, and after it is received, they will return to the classroom routine, with the obligation to perform rapid tests using antigen kits for seven days.
On the seventh day they will perform another PCR test again.
After they receive a negative answer - the class will return to normal.

The Tax Authority came unprepared, and the Finance Committee did not approve a new tax against fuel laundering The phenomenon of fuel laundering harms the state's tax revenues to the extent of NIS 100 million per year, according to the Tax Authority and the Fuel Administration.
Although the authority tried to locate establishments worthy of exemption from the tax, many areas were not examined and may be unfairly affected by the new tax
The Finance Committee again did not approve the Tax Authority's request to impose a new tax, amounting to a billion shekels per year, on oils and taxing substances.
Next week the committee will meet again to discuss the issue.
The tax authority's decree, signed by Finance Minister Avigdor Lieberman, is set to expire at the end of next week if it is not approved by the committee.
Most likely, a new and updated decree for determining the tax will be published later.

The new tax is officially intended to combat the phenomenon of the fuel halo, which, according to the Tax Authority and the Fuel Administration, harms the state's tax revenues to the extent of NIS 100 million per year.
The solvents and oils help mix fuels.

At today's hearing (Wednesday), the Director of the Fuel and Gas Administration at the Ministry of Energy, Chen Bar Yosef, said that while in the past about 15 violations of fuel regulations were caught per year, now we see a sharp increase - five times cases of improper fuel, in a way that damages vehicles, pollutes , and endangers human life.
According to Bar Yosef, it is very difficult to combat this phenomenon, partly because in legal proceedings a low fine of only NIS 10,000-15,000 is usually imposed on fuel sellers.

Bar Yosef also said that although the fuel administration locates mixing facilities, which are usually located on private areas in the settlements, it does not have the ability to impose sanctions against them since there is no proof that the mixing facility actually sells mixed fuel.
Chen Bar Yosef, Director of the Fuel and Gas Administration at the Ministry of Energy Maged Guzani.
These mixed materials are also used by other industries in Israel such as the printing industry, the oils for vehicles and more.
Last week, the Tax Authority presented 12 exemptions for factories from paying the tax, but in many industries they made it clear that the new tax will affect them.
For example, the HP Indigo company, which employs 2,500 workers in Kiryat Gat, claimed at today's hearing that the new tax would harm it and its subcontractors.

In the discussion, it became clear that although the tax authority sent out questionnaires to many industries and tried to locate the establishments deserving of exemption, many areas have not yet been examined and may be unfairly harmed in other ways.

For example, a representative of a company that produces fine chemicals in the medical field and a supplier of hospitals may be harmed by the new tax, even though the material that the company supplies to the hospitals is not at all suitable for use in the mixing of fuels.
HP Indigo's factory in Kiryat Gat.
The company because the new tax will hurt it and its subcontractors Ilan Assig.
The Union of Chambers of Commerce claimed again today that the move is wrong and that it will actually punish law-abiding people.
"It will never be possible to close the list of factories, it is constantly being updated," said Omer Sela, director of the auto parts department at the Union of Chambers of Commerce.
"The tax authority tries to make a thorough analysis, but it is impossible to segment all industries and sub-classifications.
This tax should be completely abolished."
Other representatives from the industry warned against price increases and concentration in the oil sector.
Ronan Levy, the chairman of the garage union, said that "we received very stressed calls from small oil suppliers, who they claim are going to drop out of the competition completely.
The quality of the fuels should be taken care of through legislation.
There is no enforcement in this area," Levy said.
Ronan Levy, chairman of the association of the garages without credit.
On the other hand, representatives of the various government ministries supported the imposition of the tax.
Amir Salzberg from the Ministry of Environmental Protection said that the fuel incineration facilities could damage and be toxic to the environment.
The Ministry of Economy clarified that they support the law, but the exemptions must be extended to industry.
The applicability of the current decree, signed by the Minister of Finance, has already been postponed to January instead of December.
However, without the approval of the finance committee, the order should expire on December 24, 60 days after it was amended.
Apparently, following the comments, the Tax Authority will publish a new order with additional exemptions, and its expiration date will be postponed.
Alex Kushnir, Chairman of the Finance Committee, Ohad Zweigenberg.
At the end of the discussion, the Chairman of the Finance Committee, Alex Kushnir, said that "the problematic phenomenon of the diesel fuel mix cannot be ignored.
That's how this money goes to crime.
The Tax Authority and the Fuel Administration do a lot of work.
We are also here to help you create another change to increase the ability to enforce and punish if there is such a need."

However, according to Kushnir, at the moment it is not possible to advance the approval of the order and the additional industries that may be affected by it must be examined, including bakeries or chip processing companies.

Kushnir also proposed, in accordance with the position of some manufacturers, to impose the tax only on large packages that are purchased by the fuel suppliers and not on small packages intended for small consumers.
Gantz and Bibi join forces for the benefit of the defense system budget during the coalition negotiations, the government will come up with a plan to improve the reconstruction department on Sunday.
The cost of the reform will be about one billion shekels per year - without a budgetary source - and it will not deplete the defense budget.
What is included in the reform?

While Prime Minister Binyamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Benny Gantz waged a global war last week over the appointment of a Minister of Justice for the State of Israel, in recent days there has been unanimity between them regarding an issue costing about one billion shekels per year.

There is an agreement between the two rivals that this coming Sunday a proposal by the Ministry of Defense will be put forward at the cabinet meeting to add to the base of the state budget an expenditure of 900 million shekels, and another 325 million shekels in a one-time manner.
The budget is intended to carry out a reform in the care that the IDF disabled receive.
The only question mark that currently stands regarding it is regarding the budgetary source for the reform.
The Ministry of Defense may have initiated the reform, but it is not prepared for the fact that it will cost the defense budget.

The event that led to the desire to launch the reform is the tragic case in which Itzik Saidian, a fighter suffering from battle shock, set himself on fire in front of the offices of the Ministry of Defense's Rehabilitation Division.

However, only about NIS 360 million from the reform budget that will be brought to the government is intended for the treatment of post-traumatic cases, and from the information received by TheMarker about the sections of which the reform is made up, it seems that there are some that deserve further discussion.
Thus, approximately NIS 100 million from the budget increase will eventually end up in the hands of lawyers.

The reason for this is that, as part of the reform, the funding received by the disabled IDF will be expanded in order to pay for legal aid - which is intended to help them get their rights from the state.
If as of today the disabled IDF must pass a test indicating that they are entitled to assistance due to their low income - following the reform this test will be abolished.
Demonstrators in front of the Tomer Appelbaum Ministry of Defense's Rehabilitation Division.

Another NIS 100 million is a cost resulting from the fact that, according to the reform, the period of time in which the state replaces the vehicle that they receive from the state for disabled persons who are entitled to it, will be shortened from 4.5 years to 3 years.
Aid to Beit HaLochem will also triple, rising from about NIS 25 million today, to NIS 75 million a year.
Alongside these, there are sections in the reform whose necessity is hard to argue with.
Thus, about NIS 100 million from the budget that the reform talks about will be allocated for service dogs to accompany post-trauma victims.

About NIS 90 million will finance a hospital that will be built for those victims by the sea. NIS 80 million from the budget that will be brought to the Knesset will be used to add 240 standards to the rehabilitation division, at a cost of NIS 80 million per year - a move that should double the division's manpower.

The jump in personnel of the rehabilitation division is connected to another move as part of the same reform, in which it will transfer the care of the disabled in the light grades to the responsibility of the National Insurance Institute.
The treatment of these mildly disabled people is currently part of the activities of the Rehabilitation Division of the Ministry of Defense.

The transfer of this responsibility requires a budgetary addition designed to fill the gap between the assistance currently received by the disabled from the Ministry of Defense, and that received by the disabled treated by the National Insurance.
Only about 11% of requests for recognition of disability from the Ministry of Defense are based on belonging to the "mental illness" category - mainly post-trauma.

Even if there is a need for an overall reform in the treatment of the disabled in the IDF, there is no need to use the tragic case of Saidian to set it in motion without discussing its sections thoroughly.
There is certainly no reason why part of its cost should not be charged to the defense budget.

"There is no logic in any aspect": the Minister of Finance issued a statement - and received criticism from all directions from the head of the organization of cleaning companies: "It is not clear why the minister refuses to encourage the workers to return to work and chooses to pay them for sitting at home."
His decision is contrary to the position of the professional ranks, and also requires legislation, which is doubtful if it can be advanced in the current political situation

Even though the election period is over, Finance Minister Israel Katz continues with a policy that is contrary to the position of the professional ranks and employers' organizations, and is trying to lead a program that will cancel the reduction of unemployment benefits.

The minister's policy is now being criticized by many in industries that are desperate for workers but have difficulty re-recruiting them, as many prefer to continue receiving unemployment benefits and not return to work.
Katz announced that he will work to cancel the apparent 10% cut in unemployment benefits in May, after a decrease in the unemployment rate in March according to data published yesterday.
This means an additional expenditure of about NIS 200 million per month.
However, the cancellation of the cut requires a legislative procedure and it is doubtful that it will be possible to advance in the current political situation.

The expected cut in unemployment benefits stems from an automatic mechanism approved at the beginning of the Corona crisis, which stated that the scope of unemployment payments would be adjusted to the severity of the unemployment rate in Israel.

It was determined that if the unemployment rate falls below 10%, there will be a 10% cut in the amount of unemployment benefits paid to the unemployed who are eligible to receive unemployment benefits as part of the Corona aid program, for example the workers who are in Halat.
If the unemployment rate falls below 7.5%, the reductions in unemployment benefits will be canceled altogether.

"Economic and social disaster" "The Ministry of Finance behaves as if it is not interested in the economy returning to activity," says Veronika Rosenberg, CEO of the Organization of Cleaning Companies in Israel.
"In the Israeli economy there are many vacant jobs in all industries, and the employers are calling for the return of the workers.
It is not clear why Minister Katz refuses to encourage the workers to return to work and chooses to pay them for sitting at home.
This is a decision that has no economic logic, no occupational logic, and no logic in any aspect."
Closed business in Holon Tomer Appelbaum.

Shai Berman, CEO of the Association of Restaurants and Bars, also believes that this is a grave mistake. "The Holocaust is the biggest economic and social disaster for the State of Israel in the last 30 years," he said.
"The economy is hungry for workers, who prefer to sit at home and get paid while the Israeli government pays them a salary in return for sitting at home and not returning to the workforce.
It is very difficult to separate the endless election systems, for the preservation of the system that there is unanimity regarding its inefficiency."
Shay Berman, CEO of the Association of Restaurants and Bars.
"We fear that after the initial enthusiasm, they will balance out" Daniel Chechik.
The decision of Katz is contrary to the position of the professional ranks in both the Bank of Israel and the Ministry of Finance.

The professional ranks believe that the mechanism of cutting unemployment benefits is correct and important because it is an incentive to return workers to the economy, and this is against the background of the findings and reports from employers that many workers who receive unemployment benefits until June are not looking for work and do not wish to return to work in the businesses where they worked.

According to the professional ranks, such a cut will not be a significant harm, but will send an important signal to the unemployed that the safety net is disappearing and they must go out looking for work.
The decision also contradicts the position of external experts.

Thus, for example, in the plan formulated by the former Governor of the Bank of Israel Prof. Karnit Flug, now at the Israel Democracy Institute, it was proposed to preserve the mechanism of reducing unemployment benefits in accordance with the decrease in the unemployment rate and even to exacerbate it.

For example, it was suggested that the unemployment benefits would be cut in any case in June (even if the unemployment rate does not drop by 10%) and that if the unemployment rate continues to fall, the unemployment benefits would be cut every month by an additional 10%.
Karnit Flug, former Governor of the Bank of Israel Tomer Appelbaum.
The conflict between Katz and the professional ranks regarding the incentive mechanism for the return of the workers is broader.

Katz, for example, initiated plans to pay thousands of shekels to every unemployed person who would return to work as part of the economic plan presented before the elections, while the professional ranks believed that the incentives should be focused on the unemployed who would return to work at low wages.
The chairman of the presidency of the business sector, Dobi Amitai, who represents the majority of employers in Israel, also expressed his opposition to the move of the OT.
"We are in favor of anything that will put people back to work, even if it is legal and we have been waiting for this moment," Amitai told TheMarker.
"The economy is in need of workers and the state needs to do everything to make people want to come back and set the wheels of the economy in motion."
Dobi Amitai, president of the Farmers' and Farmers' Association.

Attorney Roy Cohen, president of the Chamber of Independent Organizations of the Hebrew Bible, believes that a more significant change should be made in Israel's attitude to the compensation of the unemployed.

"Instead of dealing with the essence of the unemployment benefit model, which has failed and is causing hardship for workers in entire sectors of the economy, they find interim solutions of reducing unemployment benefits and also harm the working public who really cannot return to work.

I call on the Minister of Finance to act immediately to activate a flexible unemployment insurance mechanism through the employers, which will provide a real answer to the needs of the economy and the workers."
Hashomer Mori Enochi - who will guard our educators?
Today the school year opened, and the breath of relief released by the parents can be heard all the way to the offices of the salary commissioner and the chairman of the teachers union.

However, after we are done with the basic anxiety and we have somewhere to send the children, we should raise our heads and look at the disturbing and challenging reality that educators face, a reality that is already causing many teachers to leave the education system and threatens to leave many schools without teachers and our children without proper educators.

A recent report by the Knesset's Information and Research Center shows that 85 percent of the schools reported a shortage of teachers, in the Tel Aviv area and the center no less than 95 percent of the schools reported a shortage of teachers and 58 percent of the principals reported that they assigned teachers to classes without appropriate training .

These data are not surprising when you read the data published in the latest study by Dr. Tamar Trevalos from the Faculty of Education in Bar Ilan, according to which 45% of teachers in Israel have experienced violence.

About half of the teachers who participated in the study testified that they had experienced physical and verbal violence, damage to property or sexual harassment and online violence by students, and the higher the frequency or level of the harm was, the less the affected teachers wanted to ask for help and most of them refrained from complaining for fear of harming their status and reputation.
Dr. Treblos attributed this fact to a low sense of belonging to the school and the lack of an address to turn to at the school.

According to the researcher, violence against teachers and their loss of authority vis-à-vis students is one of the reasons for teachers dropping out of the education system, and to this should be added the data from the latest study by Dr. Uri Sternberg from the Open University and the Lev Academic Center, who for the past eight years investigated the reasons for the retirement of teachers from the system and discovered that the low salary is indeed an important reason, but it is only one of the reasons for leaving the profession: the issues of feeling unappreciated, a negative attitude towards new initiatives by teachers, work environment and school climate had a significant effect on their decision to leave, which according to the data of the Central Bureau of Statistics, only in the last measurement year More than 8,600 teachers left the education system!
So what is possible and necessary to do so that in a few years we will not find ourselves without teachers and educators at all, especially quality ones?

It is important to understand that it is impossible to solve disciplinary problems only by providing specific solutions to cases of violence - a social and school infrastructure must be built that will lead to an environment in which there are fewer cases of violence from the start.
In the same way, it is not possible to create a sense of value and belonging among teachers and educators just by giving them a good word and gift vouchers for the holiday.

It is necessary to invest in the education teams, to train the principals of the schools for inclusive and empowering management, and to give space to the teachers, the vast majority of whom came from a sense of mission and a search for meaning, to find the same mission and meaning within their daily activities, and to help them and their students create a conceptual and visionary horizon and a sense of pride and belonging to the school - this while creating a community of meaning.
We know the well-known saying of Rabbi Karlibach "Every child needs a significant adult to believe in him".
In the same way, every man and woman in education needs a system that will believe in them and allow them to find and realize the educational mission inherent in them.
The author is the CEO of "Derech Kfar Yozamot Shinoch", which works to change the face of society through empowering and inclusive education.

The association accompanies and guides dozens of educational communities, educational leadership development programs and pre-military training programs in the social and geographic periphery of Israel.
The police attribute to the three suspects in throwing the Molotov cocktail that led to the injury of a 12-year-old in Jaffa the crimes of attempted murder and arson with a nationalist motive.
This is after they allegedly thought it was a Jewish home - this is how the Tel Aviv Magistrate's Court allowed publication today (Wednesday) at the request of "Haaretz" and "Walla".
The investigation shows that the suspects were equipped with a large number of Molotov cocktails and started throwing them at windows and courtyards of houses.
The main suspect in throwing the bottle, which seriously injured Mohammad Gintazi last month, lives in Jaffa, but not in the Ajami neighborhood where the boy's family lives.
Allegedly, he mistakenly looked at the window and threw a bottle at the Gintazi family home.
The place was not lit and no lights were on in the house for the occasion of Ramadan.
At this point the suspects realized that they were wrong, fled the scene and hid with a relative.
The other two suspects are brothers who live next door to the Gintzi family.
DNA of one of the brothers was found on bottles in two places where Molotov cocktails were thrown that evening, including where Gintazi was hit.
In his investigation, the brother claimed that others may have used the bottles or the rag that he threw in the garbage can near his house.

The police and the Shin Bet defined the suspects' actions as an attack, and said that they planned in advance to throw Molotov cocktails at Jewish homes out of a nationalistic motive of revenge against the background of the riots in Lod and the clashes on the Temple Mount.
According to the police and the Shin Bet, the suspects planned to damage other Jewish homes in the area, but stopped their actions after realizing that they had accidentally damaged an Arab home.
A submachine gun and pistols were found in their search.
The police said that they looked into allegations of a real estate dispute between the suspects' family and the Gintazi family, but denied it.
The three deny what is attributed to them and their detention was extended by five days.
The Tel Aviv District Attorney's Office is expected to file charges against them in the coming days.
Meanwhile, during the investigation, one of the brothers was hospitalized for three days with bruises on his body, after he claimed to have been beaten by his interrogators.
His lawyer, Ahmed Younes, claimed that he was not informed about his hospitalization and the Shin Bet refused to inform him where his client was.
"They blindfolded him.
He didn't even know where he was and who the investigator was who beat him," said Younes.
"These are shocking acts that are against all laws.
This is a predatory violation of the suspect's rights."
Although the Shin Bet denies it, the medical opinion given about him at the hospital after hospitalization indicated bruises on his body.
The judge at the Tel Aviv Magistrate's Court demanded an explanation for the bruises when he arrived yesterday for a hearing on the extension of his detention.
Following the allegations, the Investigative Complaints Investigation Unit (Mabtan) opened an investigation.
The investigators carried out many interrogation exercises against the suspects and brought them to the scene several times in order to reproduce the acts attributed to them.
On one of the occasions one of the suspects, who according to his lawyer is in an unstable state of mind, was brought to the scene and refused to get out of the car while shouting and resisting.
According to the lawyer, even in this case the investigators exerted physical pressure on him.
The incident was recorded and presented to the district court as one party.

The suspect who was admitted to the hospital claimed to his lawyer that he was interrogated by a large number of investigators in a way that did not allow him to know who was interrogating him, and thus, according to him, confessions were extracted from him under duress.
The Shin Bet denied the allegations.
According to an official in the law enforcement system, he was hospitalized due to a medical problem unrelated to his investigation.

Attorney Yigal Dotan, who represents one of the suspects together with Attorney Dean Haim Itzhaki, responded: "In this case, another aspect of the exploits of the General Security Service was revealed before the court, which as part of its investigation did not use any means of pressure, including physical means, pressure Psychological, threats to family members and the suspect himself of harm.
Some of the threats did come true.

The court also heard direct testimony from the suspect's mouth regarding the mental and physical pressure and the inhuman conditions of detention, and we hope and believe that these things will receive the appropriate expression in the next decisions of the investigating authority and the court in Israel."

The American report was published in July and claimed that Israel did not recognize the transgender woman as a victim of human trafficking, which would have allowed her to obtain a work permit.
Senior Israeli officials, on the other hand, claim that she was in the process of obtaining such a status when she committed suicide.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Justice were angry that the new report leaves Israel at "level 2" according to the ranking of the American State Department.
Level 2 includes countries that do not fully meet US standards for the protection of victims of human trafficking but are making efforts to meet those standards.
But in Jerusalem they were especially angry that the case of the Palestinian transgender woman was mentioned in the introductory chapter of the report.

On page 15 of the report is told the story of "Amira", a Palestinian transgender woman, who was a victim of human trafficking and fled to Israel from the West Bank when she was 19 to save herself from persecution.
According to the report, she asked the Israeli authorities to recognize her as a victim of human trafficking.
"Instead of helping her, the authorities arrested her, prosecuted her and deported her because she was in Israel illegally," the report states.

According to the report, only after the intervention of Israeli non-governmental organizations that helped the woman did the Israeli government give her a temporary residence permit but did not recognize her as a victim of human trafficking.
The recognition would have given her a work permit and housing assistance.
"After months of living in the shelters of various aid organizations without the legal right to work and earn her own money, she died by suicide," the US State Department report said.

After the report was published, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Jerusalem summoned a diplomat from the United States Embassy for a frank conversation during which Israel protested the contents of the report, senior Israeli officials said.
According to a summary of the meeting that came to me Walla!

Senior officials at the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs told the American diplomat that they were "surprised" to see a mention of the case of the Palestinian transgender woman in the introductory chapter of the report.
The Israeli officials claimed that the details that appeared in the report regarding the case were not accurate and constituted a "serious violation of her right to privacy".
Another reason for the Israeli protest was the use of the word "Palestine" in the text.
"This is an inappropriate thing in the report of the US State Department," the Israeli officials told the representative of the US Embassy, ​​according to the summary of the meeting.
In mid-September, Emily Korinac, a representative of the US State Department, who compiled the part of the report that dealt with Israel, arrived in Israel.

During a meeting at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, she apologized for including the case of the Palestinian transgender woman in the introductory chapter of the report and used it as an example of Israeli conduct in the fight against human trafficking.
According to the summary of the meeting, Korinac said that this was a "significant failure of the US State Department".
The US Embassy in Israel and the State Department in Washington declined to comment.
The Israeli Foreign Ministry also refused to comment.

The anchoring of the "line of buoys", which starts from the coast in the border area at Rosh Hankara and stretches west about five kilometers into the Mediterranean Sea, and turning it into a recognized international border line was Israel's main demand during the negotiations with Lebanon in recent months.

Senior Israeli officials stress that the anchoring of the "Line of Lines" is extremely important for security reasons, because until today it was a line up to which Israel acted unilaterally, which had international legitimacy for the Lebanese side to challenge it.
In addition, if the "floating line" were to move south from where it is today, this would allow a line of sight and observation from the Lebanese side towards the coastline of northern Israel.

About a week ago the salmonella case exploded in Strauss, and since then the Ministry of Health has been busy defending itself and minimizing damage, and probably rightly so.

The Food Health Division of the Ministry of Health bears a heavy responsibility, but in fact it is a weakened division and does not have any working protocol with the companies, who prefer to continue to weaken it.
This week too, we saw how the Ministry of Health abandoned our health in favor of industrial peace with the companies it should monitor, but which it mostly fears.

Health Minister Nitzan Horvitz's first response to the case said that "this is a good example of why regulation is needed and why the state needs to monitor, especially when dealing with powerful corporations.
Because if we don't save - there will be a jungle."
Well, Minister - we lived in the jungle under your responsibility.
The regulator was not there to supervise at best, and at worst even silenced criticism and tried to sweep the faults under the carpet.

In the food division of the ministry there are rather lax work protocols, most of the responsibility lies with the companies, and there is no work procedure that specifies when the products should be tested and who is responsible for expediting the results if there are worrisome findings that could endanger the public.
And that's why Horvitz was quick to praise the regulator, so that we don't notice how much oversight there really is.
Let's get down to the details.
Strauss informed the Ministry of Health that they found initial findings in their products already on Tuesday, in the middle of the holy month.
Since it takes between four and five days to receive the results of the tests, the company apparently performed the tests on the products on the eve of Passover, at the latest.
But no one in the Ministry of Health demanded that the company get results as quickly as possible because it was a holiday, and government offices work in a reduced format.
Even after it was already known to the public that there was a problem, it took another five days until results were received on the finished products.

So if we put it all together - from the moment the company tested itself, just out of kindness and not by virtue of the regulator's decision or requirement, until the moment it was known for sure that there was salmonella in the products that were marketed - more than two weeks passed, during which the public consumed the product and was exposed to unnecessary risk.
Then, only then, the senior officials of the Ministry of Health, including the Ministry's CEO Nachman Ash, came to inspect the factory.
What is the regulator worth if he is not there on a daily basis to supervise and check that everything is in order and for us citizens?
More than that: what is the work of the regulator worth if even in a crisis it takes him two weeks to wake up and realize that there is a problem?
It's true, the Ministry of Health has gone through two very difficult years because of the Corona crisis, and other diseases that are coming back to us like polio.
But if the office's work was affected by this, we as a public must know about it immediately.

And the most difficult information of all, and the worst of all, is that there was an audit by the Ministry of Health on March 30 at the finished products factory - two weeks before the company decided to inspect itself.

The Ministry of Health refuses to reveal the report from that audit, but we are all required to ask: are these audits useful and effective, or do the Ministry's people come there to eat Borax, or in this case chocolate, just to sign V and leave.

The study was conducted in the city of Leicester in central England, and compared the exposure to the three types of air pollution while driving a car with the exposure to them while walking and riding a bicycle.
The researchers tested four different possible routes, all of which end at the city hall building in the center of the city (where all the participants worked).
In two of the routes the researchers compared pedestrians and car passengers, and in two others between cyclists and car passengers.

While the starting and ending points were the same for the participants in each route, the travel routes were determined in advance by the Google Maps application, and the pedestrians and cyclists were free to choose their preferred route - whether along roads, through public parks or using special bicycle lanes.
The measuring device checked every 10 seconds the concentration of pollutants in the air to which the participant was exposed, and a total of 132 journeys were recorded.

According to the researchers, the air pollution caused by the use of means of transportation within cities tends to reach its peak during the commute to work in the mornings, and therefore the study was conducted during these hours.
According to the researchers, the general public perception is that pedestrians and cyclists are more exposed to air pollution.

Therefore, the results of the study were surprising: the researchers found that the average concentrations of nitrogen dioxide and ozone were higher for car passengers than for pedestrians or cyclists; This, despite the fact that the vehicle's ventilation system operated on the circulation of the air inside the vehicle and did not introduce air from the outside.

In the case of ozone, for example, it is an increase of up to 69 percent of the concentration to which the cyclists were exposed, and of up to 80 percent of the concentration to which the pedestrians were exposed.
That is, two of the three pollutants tested in the study were found in a higher average concentration inside the vehicle than outside it.
Average concentration of the third pollutant tested, PM2.5, was lower for car passengers.
How is the difference between the first two pollutants and the third explained?

Well, air filters that are installed in the ventilation system in most cars are designed to reduce particulate air pollution (such as PM2.5) that flows into the vehicle from the outside, but they do not treat the pollution of gases such as nitrogen dioxide and ozone.
Because of this, pollutant gases like these enter the car and accumulate there as the journey goes on, when the car is not ventilated (that is, when the windows are closed).
In contrast, pedestrians and cyclists are exposed to varying levels of air pollution, depending on the winds, their proximity to the moving vehicles and the type of space in which they walk or ride.
In addition, the cars used by the subjects are electric and do not release particulate pollution themselves as a result of burning fuels.

Therefore, the researchers claim that it is possible that in non-electric cars the particulate pollution inside the passenger compartment will be higher than that to which pedestrians or cyclists are exposed.
However, the study revealed that although pedestrians and cyclists were exposed to lower concentrations in the air of the dangerous pollutants NO2 and ozone, they inhaled a greater amount of each.

The explanation for the situation described lies in the duration of the exposure: the car journey was shorter, and therefore the participants who used to work actually inhaled a smaller amount of the same pollutants.
In addition, pedestrians and cyclists perform physical activity and therefore inhale more air per unit of time compared to a passenger sitting in a car.
Why then do the researchers still state that, from a health point of view, it is better to walk or ride a bicycle than to drive a car on the way to work?

"Studies show that it is usually better to do sports even if you are exposed to air pollutants, than not to do sports at all," explains Dr. Zohar Barnet-Yitzchaki, head of the chair for environmental and social sustainability and a faculty member in the Faculty of Engineering at the Rupin Academic Center.

Although Burnett-Yitzhaky previously published an article calling for an air pollution threshold to be set at which sports events in Israel would be canceled, both he and the researchers in the new study agree that as long as it is not a particularly unusual air pollution (which is far from the values ​​measured in the study) - the health benefits of physical activity outweigh its harm polluting factors.
"Recently, in the world of research, there has been a lot of talk about the problem of 'sedentary'", says Brent-Yitzhaky, and explains.
"Humans are not meant for prolonged sitting, which is problematic from a health point of view.
If it is possible to avoid sitting at home, then in the car, then in the office - it is better to do it."

In addition to the health benefit of walking or cycling to work, reducing the use of vehicles that burn fossil fuels will benefit the health of the entire public by reducing general air pollution, and will not add to the greenhouse gases that are released into the air and exacerbate the climate crisis.
"The less we drive in cars, the less fuel we will burn and the cleaner the air will be," states Brent-Yitzchaki.
If you have been convinced to give up the car on your way to work, Brent-Yitzchaki has an important tip regarding choosing the route.

"It's better to stay away from roads, which are the source of pollution, and get as close as possible to vegetation, which absorbs pollutants and contributes to cleaning the air," he concludes, "according to what emerges from the research, the recommendation is unequivocal: walk or ride a bicycle."
And there is also advice for those who choose to stay in the car: open a window every now and then (and not when you're driving behind a diesel truck spewing smoke).
Last week there was an important development in Israel's energy market, when it became known that two giant foreign companies are interested in entering gas drilling in Israel.
The British energy companies BP and Abu Dhabi-based ADNOC have offered to purchase 50% of "New Med Energy" (formerly: Delek Drilling), which owns 45% of the Leviathan natural gas field.
ADNOC is the state-owned national oil company of the United Arab Emirates.
The deal, if signed, will give it and BP a foothold in Israel's offshore natural gas fields and will symbolize the warming of ties between the United Arab Emirates and Israel.
All of this is in sharp contrast to reports published in mid-March, about a "cooling in relations between the Emirates and Israel" due to the legal legislation.
"First of all, it's bullshit.
This is not true," Dr. Omar Dostri, an expert on strategy and national security from the Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security, tells us.

"Ultimately, what is really important for countries like the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, with which there is now an attempt to reach an agreement, is not whether Israel is a democratic country, not human rights, not the law and not the rule of law.
This is what interests the US and European countries.
What is really interesting to the United Arab Emirates, and what we are currently dealing with - is political stability.
For their part, they want to see Israel and the region stable.
Therefore, the attempt to claim that the legal legislation will endanger relations with the United Arab Emirates is incorrect."
What is bothering the United Arab Emirates?
"They are mainly disturbed by the construction in the settlement.
The statements of Minister Bezalel Smotrich, for example, who says that there is no Palestinian people, disturb them.
This angered the UAE.
I am not speaking factually whether it is true or not.
Even if it is true, these things should not be said at a time when trying to develop a relationship with an Arab country.
The United Arab Emirates wants to show that it has not abandoned the Palestinian issue, even though it is not really of interest to it.
In the United Arab Emirates, they understand that Israel needs to build, but it needs to be done quietly, wisely, sensibly, not jumping over the navel."
We have seen reports that the UAE is now moving closer to Iran.
"They are not doing it out of love for Iran.
They do this because they want to keep a small fire with the Iranians and prevent them from attacking them.
At the same time, they are still deepening the normalization with Israel.
In other words, normalization with Iran does not come at Israel's expense, but on Israel's side."
Dr. Dostri says that the significance of the business proposal now on the table, regardless of whether it will eventually mature into a deal, is very significant.
"This means that the United Arab Emirates sees Israel as a strategic asset, it sees Israel as a regional power.
What is important to her, as I said, is geo-strategic stability."
What could be the effect of such an agreement on Israel?
"Look, I don't know yet if it will pass.
When an Arab company wants to buy almost 50% of the rights to a gas reservoir in Israel, it has to go through the security agencies and regulations in Israel.
Therefore, I would not rush to claim that this deal will be signed.
Obviously, if everything is approved, it's a game changer.
This will open the door for more companies from the Emirates to come here and certainly for gas drilling.

This brings a strategic group here from Abu Dhabi, which in itself strengthens the economic and political relations between Israel and the Emirates and makes the chance of the Emirates cutting off relations with Israel almost impossible."
How do you prepare for a demographic explosion known in advance?
On the one hand there is absolutely good news: the average life expectancy continues to increase and improve, and we are expected to live longer compared to previous eras.

On the other hand, there is a constant increase in adults suffering from the problems of old age - starting with the minor problems, and ending with diseases that also force family members to choose between nursing care at home and care in nursing homes.
It was not for nothing that the nursing allowance was reformed in 2018.
The three levels of nursing that were originally defined (a, b, c) did not correctly represent the changing conditions in the real world.

The move to six new nursing levels allows more adults to be eligible for a nursing benefit from the National Insurance, and therefore to receive more necessary services: from nursing care at home to community and other support.
The change was necessary because there was an increase in the field in people needing close nursing care of one kind or another, due to illness, cognitive decline, and more.
The nursing reform was a necessary and certainly welcome step, and additional steps were taken alongside it in the years that followed.
One of them was carried out very recently, with the establishment of a special ministerial committee for the elderly in Israel.

If until today there was no single body that centralizes the entire issue of old age in front of the relevant parties, then today the ministerial committee for old age affairs is expected to fill this void.
It was also recently decided to allow nursing benefit recipients to hire foreign caregivers directly.
According to data from the employer line, Israel currently has over 278,000 people entitled to a nursing allowance, as well as over 77,000 who have a permit to employ a foreign nursing worker.
The problem lies in the number of foreign nursing care workers, which reaches a little over 57,500 foreign workers.
This number is not enough to provide home care to all holders of the permit to employ a foreign caregiver.
That is why the Population and Immigration Authority decided to change the existing employment method, to make it easier for the nursing staff and their families.

It is hoped that another 20,000 foreign caregivers who are currently missing will be found, along with solutions and answers for the 1.3 million Israeli citizens who are caring for at least one family member themselves.
So far all is well and good, but what next?

Dr. Avi Bitzur, head of the field of gerontology at Beit Berel College and former director general of the Ministry of Pensioners - claims that the days when all adults are defined as "elderly" are over.
This phrase is wrong and misleading, and accordingly the attitude and form of treatment given to the adult population.

Since those aged 60 to 80 have fundamentally different needs than those aged 80 and over, Dr. Bitzur wants to redistribute the elderly population into two types, and not just one type as has existed until now: 60 to 80 year olds are the third age group, and 80 and over will be the fourth age group .
It may seem like a mere semantic change, but in fact it is much more than that.

When these populations are defined correctly, in accordance with the real needs on the ground, it is also possible to give them a more accurate answer at all levels of life: medical, economic, social and more.
All this with an emphasis on aging in the community and home care, and less in institutions of any kind - which is the preferred choice for most people anyway.

Beyond that, Dr. Bitzur calls for the establishment of an adult party that will run for the Knesset, and this against the background of the success of other sectoral parties in recent years. 1.3 million people aged 60 and over are 16 mandates as of today, and as life expectancy increases this number will increase accordingly.
Only in this way will we be able to promote the support and services that the older age group in Israel needs.

A few weeks ago, the bids were submitted in the tender for the mining of the "green line" tunnels of the light rail in Tel Aviv.
Five companies approached the tender, the scope of which is estimated at NIS 15 billion.
Their common denominator is that they are all Chinese.
Some of them, according to authorized information, simultaneously maintain trade relations with Iranian companies.
This is not the first time, and probably not the last, that Chinese companies are involved in large economic ventures in the Israeli economy.

The seaports in Haifa and Ashdod, the light rail in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, the mining of the Carmel tunnels, huge projects in the fields of energy, water, huge food companies, chemicals, communications and cyber - these are just a few examples.
Among the Chinese companies that take part in the country's giant tenders, there are companies that maintain a commercial relationship with Iran and other terrorist entities.
As long as it is free and fair competition, there is nothing wrong with that.

A point for thought: why are there fewer women in technological professions?
Many talk about the inequality in science and technology professions between men and women.
The picture is familiar: for every 20 men in electrical engineering classes in Israel there are two women, at best.

Many governments in the western world invest a considerable budget in order to change this and encourage women to integrate into the STEM professions - science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

But a study by Prof. Gisbert Stowet from the Department of Psychology at Leeds Beckett University in the UK offers a different explanation for the phenomenon and claims that the large budgets will not solve the matter.
The picture is familiar: for every 20 men in electrical engineering classes in Israel there are two women, at best.
Governments invest significant budgets to change this.
For the purpose of the research, Prof. Stowet and his partner examined the findings of the OECD PISA tests for 2015, in which the skills of high school students in 70 countries were estimated.
In that year's test, emphasis was placed on the skills in the field of science, but the areas of mathematics and reading literacy were also examined.
When Prof. Stowet and his partner compared the achievements of boys and girls in science and mathematics, they saw no significant differences.

On the other hand, when we examined the students' strengths, i.e. in which areas the students were most successful, they found that for most of the girls the strong area was reading literacy and for most of the boys - mathematics or science.
The differences are also evident when the boys being tested estimate their own skills.
In the questionnaire given to the subjects, they were asked to report how they estimate their ability to deal with a variety of scientific questions.
It turns out that many of the girls perceive themselves to be much more efficient in the areas of reading literacy.
But when it comes to dealing with problems in the fields of science or mathematics, the boys perceived themselves to be more effective compared to other fields.
The surprising part became clear to Prof. Stowet when he examined the differences among different countries.

Precisely in the countries that, according to the Global Gender Gap Report of the World Economic Forum, are characterized by relative equality among the sexes, such as Norway for example, the gap between the self-esteem of the boys and that of the girls was the highest.
The gap is also reflected in later stages of life.

When Prof. Stowet examined the proportion of women among those graduating with a master's degree in the STEM subjects, it became clear that precisely in countries characterized by gender equality, the proportion of graduates in these subjects is relatively low.
In Finland, which is considered egalitarian, 20 percent of STEM graduates are women compared to Algeria with 38 percent.
This is where the issue of personal satisfaction with life comes into play, which according to Prof. Stoat can explain the differences among the different countries.
According to him, when the economic situation is difficult, many times the young people choose the profession according to economic constraints.
However, in countries characterized by a better economic situation, where young people enjoy a better sense of satisfaction with life, additional, more personal considerations also come into play.
There is a tendency to look for the professions in which the young man is expected to realize his potential more.
Whereas among many young women, because the feeling is that their personal strength is in professions that are not scientific or technological, fewer young women choose these professions.
How to clean the environment - without big government
Vien Salat is the founder and CEO of The Ocean Cleanup - a company that uses innovative technology to remove plastic from the world's oceans.
He founded the venture at the age of 18 in his native country - the Netherlands.

In October 2019, Salat gave a presentation demonstrating the company's groundbreaking machine called The Interceptor - a catamaran-type barge designed to float across rivers and "intercept" the plastic waste before it spills into the ocean.

The development is a technical marvel: it works without the need for a grid connection, is powered entirely by solar energy, stores energy in lithium-ion batteries for use at night, directly measures the amount of waste collected and can measure local weather conditions.
From the moment it is activated, a single interceptor can clean about 50 tons of plastic a day from the river - a figure equal in value to one million plastic soda bottles.
Salat's venture was largely funded by donations, and as of 2017 raised more than $31.5 million.
Nowadays there is no lack of articles dealing with the human influence on the earth.
Most people agree that more can be done to reduce our impact on the environment, but the range of existing solutions is highly controversial.
Such a controversy is, for example, the idea of ​​the "Green New Deal" in the USA and in Israel (proposed by Knesset member Stav Shapir).

The purpose of the program is to stop the production of energy by means that are perceived as polluting and to switch to the production of 100 percent of the energy using "renewable energy" facilities (wind, water, solar).

The plan will draw a huge amount of money from the state (USA), will cause a more than 30 percent increase in the cost of electricity for every household by the year 2040, and will result in the loss of approximately one million jobs per year.
And at the end of the day, its effect on temperature will be negligible, as analysts from the Heritage think tank have shown.
What will the program do?
You will collect a huge fortune from the taxpayer's money and redistribute it into the hands of politicians who are not skilled at all in dealing with environmental issues.
A beautiful socialist idea and that's all.
Salat's achievement, however, is living proof that the world does not need invasive, big-government socialist policies to maintain a healthy environment.
Salat was about Greta Tonberry's age when he noticed the need to solve such issues.
But instead of condescendingly preaching to the world about what the planet should look like, he took action and initiated the change he would like to see himself.
Salat's team conducted a study and determined that 80 percent of the plastic that spills into the world's oceans comes from a thousand rivers alone.
His company focuses on those rivers and hopes to finish treating the plastic waste in them by 2025.
Two Salat interceptors are already collecting debris in Indonesia and Malaysia, and a third interceptor will soon be deployed in Vietnam.
A fourth interceptor will be sent to the Osama River in the Dominican Republic.
Salat's company also uses systems designed to capture and remove plastic that has already made its way into the ocean.
According to the company's website, there are more than 5 trillion pieces of plastic polluting the world's oceans.
Most of the plastic is concentrated in five areas of marine debris in the oceans, the largest of which is called the "Great Pacific Garbage Patch" and is located between Hawaii and California.
Salat's systems are designed to complement - not replace - the existing waste management methods.

Salat's company estimates that it can clean 50 percent of the waste area of ​​the Pacific Ocean in just five years, and it is expected to do so at a minimal cost compared to traditional cleaning methods.
Deploying these systems around the world will bring tremendous value to the ecosystems in our world.
Salat shows that you don't always need big, inflated ideas with a socialist flavor.
Private ventures can be the most efficient and morally correct way to deal with our environmental challenges, on the way to a cleaner and healthier world.
A point for thought: which prevention campaign is better - positive or negative?
According to the National Road Safety Authority, it is estimated today that 20 percent of fatal accidents in the Western world are caused by drinking alcohol.
In a survey conducted by the Authority in 2015 in Israel, one out of every five drivers admitted that they had driven in the last month after drinking an alcoholic beverage.

So much so that even the World Health Organization came to the rescue and initiated several campaigns and funds aimed at warning and influencing the public.
Most of the campaigns conducted to date are focused on scaring drivers against the devastating consequences of drunk driving.
Studies have proven that campaigns of this type are indeed effective in reducing accidents.
But despite all the intimidation, the Polish mothers and policemen with breathalyzers lurking for drivers on dark nights, still, the phenomenon is far from disappearing.
Many researchers have examined the issue of the effect of campaigns on drunk driving.

In a new study conducted at Loyola University in the USA and universities in China and Canada, the researchers wanted to examine the effect that positive campaigns have compared to negative campaigns on the motivation to refuse to drive drunk.
The researchers started from the assumption that messages of intimidation will work to a different extent on different types of people and in different situations.
That is, there will be those who will be affected by negative messages and others for whom positive messages will be more effective.
Therefore, they created positive and negative ads, and compared their effectiveness.

With the help of questionnaires, they classified drivers into different personality characteristics: drivers whose nature is to seek pleasure, enjoy life and are not afraid of danger, versus drivers whose nature is to play it safe and avoid pain and difficulty; And drivers who by nature think about future results, versus drivers who think mainly about short-term results.
All 105 participants in the study were exposed to four types of ads.
Two were negatives: a driver was caught drunk by a policeman after crashing into a wall and becoming sore and miserable.
And a driver sat with his friends, agreed to drink and the end was bad.
And two positives: a driver was stopped for testing by a policeman and got away clean.
He then happily arrived home safely.
And the driver sat with his friends, refused to drink and the positive reason for his refusal is emphasized - his thought of a safe future.
The results of the study showed that the positive ads worked better on the drivers who were focused on enjoyment and not afraid of danger (which the negative campaigns can emphasize).
But there was a condition for this: that they also belonged to a group that was focused on short-term results.

The negative ads worked better on drivers who were focused on avoiding pain and difficulty (those who play it safe and dangers have a psychological effect on them), but this time too there was a condition: that the participants were also focused on future results.
In other words, the response to a certain campaign depends very much on the target audience.
The question remains how to know where to find the right audience for which ad?
This, the researchers say, is the next step in their research.

The victims of the Farhud are not entitled to compensation yesterday

Yesterday, the Supreme Court unanimously decided that according to the Nazi Persecution Disability Law, which for this purpose adopts the German Compensation Law, the victims of the pogrom of Iraqi Jews in 1941, known as the "Farhud", are not entitled to compensation.

The Supreme Court emphasized that it is possible for the Knesset or the government to expand the scope of compensation by way of an amendment to the law or an administrative decision, similar to laws and decisions made in the past that granted additional compensation beyond what is stated in the Nazi Persecution Disability Law.

The judges insisted that the Farhud events in Iraq are a black stain in human Jewish history, that they have an important place in the collective memory of the Jewish people, and that the pain of the appellants was before his eyes.
The court also noted that the persecution of Jews outside the borders of the German Reich and Iraq in general was influenced by the anti-Jewish propaganda and that Nazi Germany was involved in this.
However, as long as the eligibility conditions stipulated in the law are not met, there is no escape from the rejection of the appeals.

However, the head of the panel, Judge Barak-Erez, wrote that "the focus of the Nazi Persecution Law on the scope of entitlement to compensation in Germany, which the courts are bound by, is a kind of miss.
This law reflects German policy, a policy that does not necessarily express the public position in Israel at this time...
The Gordian connection to German law and Germany hinders the possibility of giving full recognition to the victims."

On the recommendation of the Supreme Court, the state representatives agreed to allow the parhud victims to receive an annual grant for 2018 as part of an administrative decision issued in their case.
Also, even though the appeals were rejected, the Supreme Court ordered the restitution of the expenses awarded to the Parhud victims by the appeals committee in Haifa in the amount of NIS 215,000.

The appellants before the Supreme Court are Jews from Iraq, who were harmed in the pogrom and who claim that they should be recognized as entitled to compensation according to the Nazi Persecution Disability Law.
The Authority for the Rights of Holocaust Survivors at the Ministry of Finance rejected the applicants' application because they do not meet the requirements of the law.
For the same reasons, the appeals committees acting under the same law, as well as the district court in Haifa, rejected the appellants' claim.
The applicants turned to the Supreme Court with a request to examine their case once more.

The legal question that was up for decision by the Supreme Court was whether and in which cases the German compensation law, which, as mentioned, was adopted by the Israeli Nazi Persecution Disability Law, applies to events that took place outside of Germany, at the hands of non-Germans, and whether the Farhud is one of those cases.

The Nazi Persecution Disability Act states that entitlement to compensation under its authority will only be given to those who could receive compensation from the German government in accordance with the German Compensation Act, which was enacted in the 1950s.
In practice, German law saw before its eyes those who were harmed in the territory of the 'German Reich', and the injustices caused directly by Nazi Germany or its people.
Accordingly, the limits of applicability of the German law were also outlined.

To the German territorial rule that accompanied the law and its interpretation from its inception, limited exceptions were established: acts committed by a state that was a 'carrier' of Germany, and those committed by another state that was motivated by Germany and led to a 'deprivation of liberty', provided they were 'institutionalized' acts.

In view of the territorial condition of the German law, and since the events of the parhud were undoubtedly carried out outside the boundaries of the 'German Reich', the right to compensation depended on proving that the events took place in a 'traversal' country of Nazi Germany, or alternatively that these were acts of 'deprivation of liberty' carried out in an institutionalized manner by Iraqi officials.
The Supreme Court adopted the determinations of the appeals committees and the district court because these were not the facts.

The judges criticized the fact that the German law on which the Israeli law is based was never formally translated into Hebrew, in a way that makes it difficult for the country's citizens to manage their steps on the matter.
Finally, the Supreme Court insisted that the Israeli law's focus on the scope of entitlement granted in Germany does not necessarily express the proper position in Israel at this time.

On the other hand, the court is not the authorized body to determine the compensation policy, and this is left to the executive authority and the legislative authority, when in this matter the time dimension is important in view of the age of the survivors.

Attorney David Yadid, from the office of David Yadid Attorneys at Law and Notary, who represented the Parhud victims throughout the legal process, stated that: "The Supreme Court states in this ruling that the suffering of the Parhud victims was great, but they cannot be recognized according to the Disability Law of Persecution The Nazis, since this law is subject to German law, and the judges criticized that.

"Nevertheless, the court recognized that the rights that were given to the survivors (the annual compensation) during the past few years, are a result of the legal process that we conducted, and therefore awarded the state reimbursement of expenses.

It is a great shame that those politicians who speak highly of the rights of the elderly and Holocaust survivors, are silent when action is required in the form of a necessary amendment to a law that creates a historical injustice," it said.

Request for representation against McDonald's: violates the law to prevent smoking in public places

A request for approval of a class action lawsuit was submitted today (Tuesday) against the McDonald's Israel chain and its owner Amri Padan, alleging violation of the law to prevent smoking in public places and exposure to smoking in its branch premises.
The application for approval of the lawsuit was submitted to the Haifa District Court through attorney Omer Paintoch and Ram Gorodisky.
The plaintiff requests to include in the group "every person who was in the defendant's branches and was exposed to smoking", and asks the court to approve an amount of NIS 1,000 per plaintiff.
In the lawsuit, the representative plaintiff claims that the fast food chain does not implement the provisions of the law to prevent smoking in all outdoor areas of its many branches.
According to the chain's website, McDonald's has 196 branches in Israel, 57 of which have seating outside the restaurant.

According to the plaintiff, the chain appeals to an audience of children through designated meals and special offers, and therefore this request receives a new validity, "since a large audience of the defendant consists of children of various ages who are exposed to the harmful smoke in the defendant's branches, and this while sitting in the outdoor areas and even while passing and entering and exiting the branches themselves." .
The lawsuit claims that according to the provisions of the smoking prevention law, the defendant must assign a non-smoking area in all seating areas outside the restaurant.
"The smoking area will not be larger than 25% of the area where smoking is prohibited (or up to 15 square meters)".

Immediately after that, the plaintiff states that in practice, in view of the provisions of the law for the prevention of smoking, McDonald's cannot in the current situation assign an area for smoking at all, since there is no separation in the outside areas and smoking is a nuisance to the other areas of the complex.
"Thus, the defendant violates the clear provisions of the law regarding the prevention of smoking.
Therefore, not only are there no smoking or non-smoking areas at all, but the defendant must prohibit smoking at all in its outdoor areas," according to the lawsuit.
The plaintiff also points out that in the restaurant branches there is not even a single sign on the outside areas indicating a non-smoking area or the prohibition of smoking.

According to what is described in the lawsuit, the plaintiff carried out a "comprehensive inspection and conversation with over 20 McDonald's employees in various branches, including a number in charge of the shift", from which it appears that there is no procedure prohibiting smoking in the yeshiva areas that are outside the restaurants.
"The defendant's employees pass by smokers and do not even do the minimum required to try and stop the harmful smoking," it was claimed.
"It also appears that many employees of the defendant also smoke in the outdoor seating areas of the restaurant, near the front door, near the children who are sitting at the tables.

"Since there is no procedure on the matter on the part of the defendant itself, a situation has arisen in which the defendant's customers also smoke without interruption when none of the chain's employees notices and does nothing to stop the harmful smoking."

The plaintiff attached to the request photos documenting the violations in the branch premises and stated: "There is no factual dispute in this case and the defendant must ensure that the violation of the smoking prevention law is stopped immediately.

The defendant must add clear signage stating that smoking is prohibited, prohibit its employees from smoking on the restaurant's premises, as well as give instructions to its employees to implement the provisions of the law, so that they do everything possible to prevent harmful smoking from the restaurant's customers as well."

The plaintiff, a customer of McDonald's, describes the sequence of events and states that on one of the Saturdays in July 2019, he visited the defendant's premises located in the Mikado Center Tel Aviv branch, together with his minor nephew, as part of a fun day they had.
When he tried to sit with his nephew outside the restaurant on a summer day, he noticed that several customers were smoking outside.
"The smoking was very noticeable on the outside and bothered the plaintiff who was also anxious to expose his minor nephew to the harms of smoking," the lawsuit states.

"The prosecutor is knowledgeable about the smoking prevention law and had a short conversation with the employees and asked that the smokers be ordered to stop and even explained to them that smoking is prohibited in the entire outdoor area.
However, he was told that nothing can be done about it and that smoking is allowed in the chairs outside the restaurant."

Attorney Paintoch told Calcalist that: "The law states that it is possible to assign an area for smoking, provided that it does not cause a nuisance to other parts of the restaurant - something that is very difficult to implement in the outdoor areas in this case.
There are very few branches where you might be able to assign a smoking area.
Anyway, they didn't do that either.
So for example, the area near the front door - certainly must be non-smoking because everyone passes through it.
"A huge food chain like McDonald's, a significant part of whose customers are children, should do its utmost to prevent harmful smoking in the restaurant.

It is unacceptable, because there is not even one sign or any procedure on the matter, when many customers, including children, are exposed every day to the harm of passive smoking, and this phenomenon must be stopped immediately."
A response from McDonald's has not yet been received.
