Aircraft carrier Cavour departs for U.S., F35B training in Norfolk
"Ready for operation" is the name of the mission that will see ship Cavour dock in the U.S. in mid-February.
Return to Italy scheduled for late April.
In between, three months of intense activity.
The mission will enable our carrier to achieve the certifications required to operate the new F-35 aircraft, in the short takeoff and vertical landing variant, i.e., the "B" version.
The 5th generation fighter will replace the now "aged" AV - 8B Plus "Harrier" fighters, which will soon end their operational life.
The first landing of a Harrier on the aircraft carrier Garibaldi was in August 1991, that is, 30 years have passed.
The transition from AV 8s to F35Bs represents a true generational leap.
During the first phase of the mission, F-35B certification tests will be conducted by the US Integrated Test Force.

In the second phase, onboard F-35B operations training will instead take place for the benefit of Navy pilots and specialists and aircraft carrier personnel, using Navy aircraft deployed at U.S. Marine Corps Base Beaufort and supported by U.S. Navy and Marine personnel.
The integration of the new aircraft will give the Italian naval team to develop a world-class potential unique among all European navies.
Once again the importance of the defense industry sector to the national economy is confirmed, especially at this time of crisis and industrial cooperation between Italy and the US.
Nave Cavour is a real floating city.
In fact, about 660 people live and work on board, including specialized components.
Covid 19 affected the "Ready for operation" mission in no small part, which was postponed precisely because of the ongoing global pandemic.
To protect personnel, the Navy set up preventive health protocols that included conducting a 2-week isolation period and performing molecular swabs on the entire crew.
Body temperature, on board, is measured twice a day, and only FFP2 masks are used.
During the U.S. campaign, the shipboard health component was increased both in terms of personnel and the specialized equipment available.
It consists of 20 people, including doctors and nurses.
The aircraft carrier, which houses a full-fledged hospital, was specially equipped with a laboratory with 24-hour swab testing capabilities accredited by the Celio military polyclinic.

A result that would not have been achieved without the tenacity, professionalism, and self-sacrifice of women and men who strongly believe in their profession and their mission, ready to demonstrate their capabilities at every opportunity, generous and extraordinary professionals of the sea," said the minister. "The convergence of intentions between Italy and the United States on the mutual strengthening and integration of their naval forces sees in this mission an important additional opportunity for operational verification.
This campaign will further increase, also from an interagency perspective, the capabilities that Defense, and the Navy in particular, will be able to make available to Italy.
You will travel to the United States, a great nation with which our country has a deep connection, which is based on history, shared values, culture and human ties.

The transatlantic relationship plays an essential role for Italy in the international scenario and in NATO's collective security framework, Guerini concluded, "I ask you to be leading players in this relationship and to help strengthen it further.
The events of recent years have reminded us that to ensure the security of our countries, it is necessary to reform the defense apparatuses qualitatively and quantitatively.
National level:
Increasing the efficiency of the defense sector and improving the distribution of spending
As of 2022, the distribution of the Defense budget is approximately as follows:
65.7 percent for personnel, 22.3 percent for investment, 12 percent for training and maintenance.

However, the Di Paola reform of 2012, stipulates that the various expenditure components should have the following weight: 50 percent for personnel, 25 percent for investment, and 25 percent for training and maintenance.
We propose to revise the current budget distribution to meet the target, have means ready for even sudden use, and increase the conduct of military exercises.
On the personnel side, under the current scenarios, the adequacy of the targets set in 2012 by the Di Paola reform must be verified.
The obvious imbalances in terms of average age and the size of the different categories must be gradually corrected, with a significant increase in the troop.

It will also be necessary to create mechanisms for fostering osmosis with civilian society so that the skills of those who are discharged after a predetermined period of military service can be enhanced and utilized to the fullest extent possible.
Increase the budget for defense spending and reach the target of 2% by 2025
Currently, military spending amounts to about 1.5 percent of Italian GDP, below the agreements made within NATO that set a target of 2 percent.
To achieve this goal by 2025, we need to increase military spending by 2.6 billion a year.
Improving interagency coordination
Collaboration among the armed forces in Italy is very limited, which generates major inefficiencies and high management costs.
As an example, suffice it to say that the Army, Navy, and Air Force have three logistics systems, three health service systems, and also three territorial services.
We propose greater interagency coordination that would achieve significant economies of scale and scope.
Cybersecurity Developing and improving the capability to operate new cyber and space operational domains by enhancing the skills that Defense expresses.
EU level:
Promote the integration of the European supply chain through greater integration of the military industry

Defense in Europe is characterized by a strong phenomenon of duplication and incompatibility of industrial products of equipment and means that needs to be resolved to enable a more efficient logistics chain and a greater degree of coordination among European forces.

This can be done by stimulating each country to specialize in manufacturing specific types of equipment guaranteed thus greater economies of scale, protection of military industry jobs in each country, greater mutual interdependence of countries (no country would be considered superfluous).
Create in the medium term European Units for specific purposes and with a common budget
It is necessary to start creating units for specific joint missions to begin a process of military integration.

Our proposal is to expand the deployment capacity currently planned (but not yet implemented) by the EU by 5,000 military personnel, gradually rising to 60,000, as already envisioned by the Helsinki Headline Goal.

The 4.0 Plan implemented by then-Minister Carlo Calenda with the Renzi government was the main industrial policy initiative of the past 30 years, thanks to which investment and productivity have reached levels above those of German companies.
That is why it is necessary to focus resources on simple and automatic tax instruments to support investments by citizens and businesses.
This is the only way to increase wages and jobs.
Zero taxes for young people starting businesses
Opening a new business involves many initial expenses that discourage entrepreneurship.

To mitigate a potential liquidity problem, we propose to postpone and installment all tax obligations for the first 3 years in subsequent periods for all young people under 35 who decide to open a new business.
Facilitating the dimensional growth of enterprises
Very small enterprises are less productive than larger ones.
In Italy, they account for about 95 percent (but only 30 percent of GDP).
It is therefore necessary to put in place measures that facilitate and incentivize the growth in size of small and micro enterprises.
Therefore, we propose to: raise the enterprise size threshold for the application of some of the heaviest bureaucratic constraints on labor;
modulate the defiscalization already provided in Special Economic Zones in order to encourage the growth of small businesses and incentivize medium and large-sized ones;
Enhance the tax credit for SME listing costs, which was already introduced by MISE in 2017.
Stimulating technological innovation and investment
Restore and re-power Industry 4.0 - depowered by previous governments - by updating the list of subsidized assets (including new technologies) and increasing the investment cap;
Extend the Industry 4.0 mechanism to investments for green transition (ex: energy production and storage facilities for self-consumption).
Helping businesses find a skilled workforce
39% of open positions for June 2022 are difficult to fill due to lack of candidates or unsuitability of candidates.
Therefore, it is crucial to implement a training policy to bridge the gap between the skills required by the market (including for NRP implementation) and the skills available to the workforce.
Especially it is necessary:
cover the costs that enterprises incur in organizing, in cooperation with ITS and other training institutions, specialized courses for creating the skills that are really in demand.
These courses should be open both to internal staff to be retrained and to workers who have not yet been hired and who will be able to conduct interviews after the training period is over.
Strengthen ITS by investing 1.5 billion euros to double the number of enrollments and graduates through an increase in the total number of institutes, in line with what was planned in the NRP.

Complete competition reforms We need to pass competition laws every year that gradually-and while respecting the social sustainability of the changes-make our economy freer and less burdened by barriers to entry and restrictions on competition, to the benefit of innovation, growth and consumer protection.

There is a need to implement the reform of beach concessions-paying special attention to households that have the concession as their main source of income and have made investments in the facility-approved by the Draghi government and implement a liberalization of non-scheduled public transport, with special attention to the adaptation of technological platforms to the rules of services in the sector and its different reference markets (Taxi/NCC).
Small businesses and handicrafts
Small and micro artisan enterprises are the places of Italian talent, where the most successful Made in Italy experiences often come to life.

To support these realities, we need to accompany generational transition, encourage direct credit and guarantees, including through private mutuality, and promote on-the-job vocational training through school-to-work alternation and dual apprenticeships.

In Italy we have among the highest rates in Europe of early school leavers and NEETs (young people not studying and not working) as well as performance in reading and mathematics that is significantly worse than international standards, particularly in the South.

The problems of schools are the problems of the country: the dramatic numbers of implicit dropout and youth unemployment mark our distance from other European contexts and dictate our agenda of work and urgencies.
We must regain effectiveness and offer young people concrete prospects for cultural and professional growth.
There are all the tools to give every intelligence and talent its own way.
In school until age 18 and full time for all
We propose a comprehensive reorganization of school cycles and in particular:
Raise compulsory schooling from 16 to 18 at the end of high school.

Revise the school cycles to equal school time attended: from 13 to 12 years, with high school finishing at 18 years of age and earlier entry of young people into college and the world of work, bringing us in line with European standards.

Extend full-time education to all elementary school to provide more space for learning by meeting the needs of families and introduce the right to canteen for all with subsidy for the least affluent households.
National evaluation system The path interrupted by the Conte governments should be resumed, because there can be no autonomy without evaluation.
And only an effective national evaluation system can make it possible to identify areas where improvement is needed.

Enhancement of professionalism and creation of a teacher's career A contract that has been expired for too many years must be signed so as to guarantee a significant increase in the salaries of all teaching staff.

And in parallel, we need to introduce career forms for school staff so as to also formally recognize the various professionals who support the school head in organizational and educational functioning, as well as the figures who constitute true middle management.
Without this step, school autonomy cannot be said to be accomplished.
For both faculty and ATA staff, the percentage of precarious staff must be brought down to physiological levels.
Overcoming disparities and territorial disadvantages
Student skills surveys show deep territorial disparities, with very critical contexts due to particularly disadvantaged social, economic and cultural conditions.
Removing these situations requires:
Build a map of crisis areas based on school dropout rates, Invalsi test results and employment data at the municipal level (municipal for metropolitan cities);

Recognize an economic incentive to specially trained teachers who remain for at least one cycle of education in a school with a high concentration of students at risk of dropping out and implicit and explicit dropout rates above the national average;

Reduce the maximum number of pupils per class to increase the amount of time each teacher is able to devote to each student and establish individualized tutoring for students with greater difficulties.
Strengthening civic education

It is necessary to strengthen citizenship skills and knowledge of the functioning of the institutions of the Republic and the EU through a systematic presence of civic education in all school curricula.
A new model for vocational training
Students in vocational colleges are below the European average especially in reading and math.
On the other hand, students in Higher Technical Institutes (post-diploma paths, alternative to university) perform very well: 80 percent of them find jobs within a year of graduation.
Freedom of educational choice
It is only through freedom of educational choice that all the energies present in our schools, both state and parochial, can be released.

Freedom that comes through both the full implementation of school parity and a Copernican revolution in the way school policies are governed: moving from the concept of school autonomy to that of truly autonomous schools.

Within the public system, it is up to the family to choose the best school or training pathways for their children; and it is up to the state to impose quality standards that define a qualitatively uniform and quantitatively homogeneous supply throughout the country, starting with early childhood education services.

Freedom of educational choice should be achieved by improving the tools available and studying others (school voucher, tax refunds, standard cost...) with the intention of enabling everyone to be able to choose education for their children without insurmountable economic obstacles.
This path must always be matched by a system of ministerial controls and checks on compliance with national criteria and rules.
Italy's ongoing demographic crisis is the most severe in Europe.

For the first time, both the natural balance and the migration balance are negative: the differential between deaths and births has been negative for years and growing rapidly (last year it was just under 310,000); the differential between emigrants and immigrants is returning to pre-Covid levels, when it too had turned negative (back in 2019, despite the perception related to landings, emigrants had outnumbered immigrants).

Between 2022 and 2030, the labor force (15-64 years old) in the North Central alone is estimated to decline by more than 1.2 million people: simply because they were never born, and thus will not be able to replace those who retire.
The ratio of workers to retirees, now 3 to 2, is expected to become 1 to 1 before 2045.

The warnings now experienced by many productive sectors, where the search for labor has become difficult (as of June 2022, 40 percent of new positions were difficult to find), are only the premises of a much more serious situation, which threatens to seriously damage the system-country.

Therefore, in addition to activating strong policies to support the birth rate, to support young people and their entry into the labor market, and to protect the family, migration flows need to be governed seriously, with pragmatic and manageable policies.
This can be done by addressing four orders of problems: entry, integration policies, asylum policies and system governance.
Combat illegal immigration by encouraging regular and planned entry
Irregular migration is a detriment to both migrants and destination countries:
encourages the development of transnational mafias and international blackmail policies.
The only way to radically decrease irregular entry is to restore regular and planned forms of immigration.

This is why we propose: cooperation agreements with countries of origin and transit (at the European level-the "Migration compact"-and national level) that include trade policies, defense, institution building, dedicated funding lines, customs union enlargement, and planning for regular migration flows based on labor market needs.
This will provide binding cooperation on returns (including voluntary and incentivized returns) in exchange for enhanced forms of control over irregular departures.

reestablish a distinction between humanitarian refugees (who have specific international protections) and economic migrants (who could only enter the regular labor market directly with ad hoc residence permits).

Functional in this regard is the reintroduction of the figure of the sponsor to facilitate the matching of supply and demand for remote labor, which is difficult especially when it comes to low-skill jobs.
This could drastically reduce the phenomenon of illegality of those who are eventually refused humanitarian visas.
Indeed, it is paradoxical that today, when there is a need for labor, visas issued for work are a laughable minority.

Betting on youth means investing in the future
One of the most important issues affecting the world of youth is undoubtedly the transition from the world of education to the world of work.
A delicate phase that has already been an element of discussion and debate not only nationally but even worldwide for years.

As Italy, the major critical issues that can be noted in this regard are certainly the late exit from the school system (compared to the European average) and the now inadequacy of high school and university training paths with the needs of the working world.
All these negative features combined with ineffective interventions implemented have resulted in Italy's youth employment rate plummeting compared to other EU countries.
The question we asked ourselves is, "How can the situation be resolved?
What tools can help?
What hasn't worked until now?"
Regarding the late exit from education and training and the related effects produced on the world of work, the national legislature had already intervened.

University studies had already been reformed in 1999 with the introduction of the bachelor's and master's degrees, and then continued with Decree 270/2004, which included the bachelor's degree (first called the three-year degree) and then the two-year master's degree and finally the postgraduate first- and second-cycle master's degrees (currently, Law and Medicine remain single-cycle).

This apparently produced a lowering of the average graduation age, but this was counterbalanced by the choice of continuation to master's degree studies due to the high degree of specialization required by the market, actually causing a null effect.
So while the reform has indeed resulted in a lowering of the average age for a bachelor's degree, it has not translated into a reduction in the age of young people entering the labor market.

On the other hand, with regard to the inadequacy of training plans and the failure to align them with the needs of the world of work, the legislature had intervened back in 1997 by introducing curricular training and orientation internships into the training pathway, a certainly useful tool that has produced good results by offering young people the possibility of direct contact with the world of work before the end of their studies.
Other contractual tools were introduced by the Biagi Law such as internships and apprenticeships, which have been useful tools for job placement.
We believe it is necessary to intervene especially in the school chain ex ante (at the school desks) and ex post, that is, at the end of the course of study and upon graduation.

MoneyBlog - American mysteries
America, the land of unlimited possibilities, both positive and negative.
This country is full of quirks, kindnesses ( Nord Stream 2 ), and economic mysteries.
No, this will not be a column about Jekyll Island in 1913; it will be about two economic mysteries going on now.
And while the possible explanations are not necessarily fully covering, at least it is a nice basis for a discussion for the commenters.
The first mystery is how it can be that employment remains so good when severe weather is forecast.
Interest rates on mortgages have skyrocketed as have rents; thus, housing has become considerably more expensive.
In addition, inflation, particularly in food and energy, has further hit American consumers.
Savings balances have also shrunk significantly, and consumer credit now seems increasingly unavailable.
In addition, companies such as Amazon, Google, Yahoo, have announced many layoffs.
Furthermore, inventories of durable goods are very high which does not bode well.
Yet unemployment remains low; how can that be?
A possible (partial) explanation is that the figures used are incorrect or then lagging behind.

For example, no distinction is made between full- and part-time, people who have given up looking for a job are not counted, long-term absentees (think long covid) are still listed as employed, and more of the same.

This may explain some, but not all, as the absolute number of hours worked has increased (admittedly not by much, but still), although again there is something to be said about how these figures are determined.

And another possible explanation may be that companies learned their lesson during Corona; a lot of people were laid off (or quit because doing nothing paid off more...) then, who didn't come back, or came back very hard, in the recovery after the lockdowns.
As a result, companies wait much longer to fire employees than they normally would.

Also, Biden's IRA ( Inflation Reduction Act ) could lead to huge green job demand, which companies are anticipating and thus keeping their capacity up now despite the short-term outlook not being good.
But what about Google, Amazon and those other companies that fire people at the drop of a hat?
These are often precisely the companies that did very well during the lockdowns and thus hired a lot of staff during that period.
With everything normalizing somewhat, it appears that there is no need for this extra capacity and so layoffs will follow, some experts say.
But then there is the second mystery: why then is wage growth in the US lagging so much?
After all, when unemployment is so low (in other words, a very tight labor market) and inflation is so high, one would expect high wage growth.
As the bar chart shows, there has been substantial wage growth, but it is now coming down hard.
But more importantly, is that adjusted for inflation, the average hourly wage has not yet returned to its end-2021 level.
In other words, in real terms, American workers have lost out, despite the fact that there is now a severe shortage of workers.
How could this be?
One possible explanation is that it could be arithmetic; if there are many layoffs in the bad sectors in the high-wage category, that could have a disproportionate impact on the average.
Furthermore, it is also possible that the survey was not representative after all.
Also, it may be that people may have had to take a second job to make ends meet and that job may not be as well paid, pushing down the average.
This could also explain why the number of hours worked went up.
Another plausible reasoning is that workers also see the bad weather coming and cave in with their wage demands.
The same, of course, could also be true for the companies, which feel emboldened by this poor outlook not to give further wage increases.

The latter two may also (also) apply with respect to inflation expectations; if employers and employees believe that inflation will come off substantially now, then the same will be true for wage growth.
Any way you slice it, many experts now find it extra difficult to predict where the U.S. economy is headed or not.
El-Erian warns that the battle with inflation is not over, and Larry Summers has made similar statements.
Michael Bury , on whom the film The Big Short is partly based, argues that great doom awaits us.
Also and Grantham view it bleakly.
On the other end of the spectrum, there is Jim Cramer and he thinks everything is mega bullish.

Nature management Catching raccoons because 'it has to by Brussels'?
In Limburg, raccoons are being trapped in an attempt to stop their advance.
This goes against common sense and knowledge about raccoons and will prove futile, writes Jaap Mulder .
3 min. reading
The raccoon is a species of predator from the group of small bears, native to North and South America.
It was brought to Europe by humans and released into the wild in various places or accidentally escaped.
Meanwhile, it is already found in Germany, Wallonia and northern France.
Now it is also entering our country, especially in Limburg.
It is a typical example of an "invasive exotic," an organism from another continent that settles and expands here.
Jaap Mulder is a biologist and predator specialist and has been researching various predator species in the Netherlands for forty years.
Policies have been developed for such invasive exotic species, both in Europe and in the Netherlands.
The 2016 EU Regulation 1143/2014 lists exotic species that member states must control, including the raccoon.
That ordinance in this case is mistakenly understood by the provinces as an order for control and eradication.
For example, it ignores the fact that there is no ecological need for large-scale control.
The raccoon does very little "damage" to our natural environment.
There are still no studies showing that animal species decline due to the presence of the raccoon.
Only on islets (the raccoon swims well and gladly) can it chase away, for example, bird colonies that were safe there from the fox.
The argument that raccoons sometimes carry a parasitic worm dangerous to humans is also of little validity : the risk of infection is extremely small.
Control does not appear to work in practice either: fifty years of hunting in Germany has not led to a decrease in the raccoon population there or even to a slowing of its expansion.
In fact, the raccoon is now considered a native game animal in Germany.
As a result, control in Limburg (and elsewhere in the Netherlands) will be mopping with the tap open: raccoons will continue to enter our country in increasing numbers from Germany and Belgium.

The Dutch Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA), in charge of implementing exotic species policy, writes so itself in a policy document : "Once influxes of raccoons occur, (continuous effort and cost-consuming) elimination is probably not feasible.
At that point, it seems more useful to focus the approach on keeping raccoon-free islands and natural areas with ground-breeding and vulnerable colony breeders."
The EU directive contains sufficient room for such policies.
Condemned to frustrating existence.
Raccoons caught in Limburg will be taken in and sterilized by the AAP Foundation and then offered to zoos.
Thus, this condemns wild animals to life imprisonment.
A strange decision.
If the county wants to get rid of the raccoons, be bold and get rid of them, instead of condemning them to a frustrating existence.
A curious aspect in this matter is that the control of the raccoon is done by the Mammalian Society, commissioned by Province of Limburg.
In the past, that association, of which I have been a member for 50 years, based its views and actions on scientific knowledge.
Study and protection of mammals were the focus then.
In this case, making money seems more important.
I wonder if the members know and support that.
Why didn't the association knowledgeably advise the county to leave the raccoons alone?

Also in the case of another exotic species, the raccoon dog (the head of this canine-like animal resembles that of the raccoon, hence the name), which is entering our country in the northeast, the Mammalian Society is urging the provinces to proceed with control.
Raccoon as ally.
And this despite the fact that two thorough risk analyses and a food study on this species have been commissioned by the NVWA that show that general control is neither necessary nor effective.
Indeed, by controlling predators, the survival rates of their young become much higher, and thus the population will remain the same.

Moreover, raccoon and raccoon dog hardly harm nature and cannot be eradicated: we will have to learn to live with them, as we already do with other exotics, the collared parakeet and the Nile goose, for example.
The raccoon could even become an ally in controlling American crayfish, which do cause many ecological problems.

Control of exotic species only makes sense if they have only just established themselves and can still be eradicated: in this respect, the Mammalian Society achieved a good result six years ago with the eradication of the Pallas' squirrel near Weert.
But in the case of the raccoon, Province of Limburg and the Mammal Society are completely missing the point.

ICT problems are risk to patient safety
Patient safety in hospitals is under pressure because digital exchange of medical data is often impossible.

Doctors cannot access patients' medical records because the electronic health records of hospitals, family doctors and sometimes even different departments within the same hospital do not communicate with each other.
A survey by the Federation of Medical Specialists (FMS) among its own constituency shows that almost all doctors who responded face this problem.

In addition to danger to patient safety, the medical specialists named more consequences of the failing data exchange: a high risk of medical errors, risks of errors with medication, annoyance and misunderstanding among patients, duplicate diagnostics, inefficient use of time, additional administrative workload, waste of healthcare money and reduction of job satisfaction.
'Something about a heart valve' Cardiologist Marcel Daniëls of the Jeroen Bosch Hospital in Den Bosch is president of the FMS.
He recently experienced a striking example with a patient who came in to his hospital with severe chest and back pain and low blood pressure.
"I could tell by the scar on the chest that he had had surgery before.
His family knew about it, but at the time could not tell much more than 'something with a heart valve' and that it had possibly been done in Amsterdam," he says.
"You need immediate access to his medical history and medications at that point to be able to make the right choices as a doctor.
There's really no time to call other hospitals and find out what that's like.
Precious time is lost."
Data on CD-ROM with patient.
What happens at the Jeroen Bosch Hospital is also no exception elsewhere.
At another hospital, a patient comes in with an acute cerebral infarction, who is quickly transferred to a specialized center.
The team there to operate on him cannot prepare because the medical records come with the patient on paper and CD-ROM.
An anesthesiologist at a third hospital makes no bones about his heart.
"I always have to request patient data from other hospitals before surgery.

Life-threatening blood poisoning.
At a fourth hospital, which like the previous one wishes to remain anonymous, a patient with blood poisoning (sepsis) is admitted to the intensive care unit in the middle of the night.
No one is known to be able to tell anything more about the patient.
"Only the next morning were we able to request the patient's home medication via fax to gain some insight into his medical history.

When sepsis occurs, rapid intervention is vital, otherwise a patient will go into septic shock in which vital organs are compromised.

In septic shock, that rate is three to four times higher.
Nurses complained before.

Risks to patient safety, an excess of administrative tasks at the expense of patient care and a high risk of errors.
These errors creep in because nurses often receive patient medical records on paper from other healthcare facilities or other departments within their own hospitals.

For example, a dose of a drug of 0.1 milligrams then becomes 1 milligram.
Justification.
The Federation of Medical Specialists has had a questionnaire online for its more than 22,000 members since last Tuesday.

That Europeans had something else on their minds other than buying a new car in recent months is obvious.
But that car sales plummeted as they did in the month of April is unprecedented.
To be precise, 270,682 new passenger cars were registered in Europe in that month.
A decline of 76.3 percent from the same month a year earlier.

More than 1.14 million cars left showrooms last April.

France recorded an 88 percent decline.

Closed showrooms.

Insurers New Hope for Mass Usury Policy Claim After Supreme Court Opinion The Advocate General believes that insurers who had given too little information about high costs of investment policies should not be allowed to hide behind industry rules of the time.
Claim clubs for usurious policyholders have been given new hope after a weighty opinion to the Supreme Court.
In this, they get it right on one important point: life insurers who failed to warn customers about the high cost of the product should not hide behind the industry's lax 1990s rules.

Should the Supreme Court adopt this opinion of the Solicitor General, published Friday, it will mean important new ammunition for the claims clubs that believe insurers still have many billions to pay to the holders of usurious policies.
So far, the claim clubs - of which the Vereniging Woekerpolis.nl is by far the most active - have had little success with collective cases.
Only in individual cases were there sometimes gains for the client and losses for the insurer.
But Woekerpolis.nl pursued a case against Nationale-Nederlanden (part of NN Group) and had questions of principle raised with the Supreme Court.
This also addressed the key question in the usury policy affair: did insurers adequately inform customers about costs?
About seven million of these products, officially called investment insurance policies, were sold in the 1990s and early this century.
Only later did it turn out that most were very unfavorable to the client due to high, unforeseen costs.
This left very little money actually invested.
Insurers have always defended themselves by pointing to the special rules established for the industry.
In the 1990s, there were special laws specifying what information had to be provided.
At the time, the prescription was to work with sample capitals.
Most insurers have done just that and that, they argue, is the end of the matter.
'No hiding' But decades later, Solicitor General of the Supreme Court Hartlief thinks very differently.
"Insurers themselves are responsible and cannot hide behind regulators with respect to disclosures about their own products," he stated.
Moreover, he delicately points out that the regulator (the House of Representatives) would probably have made much stricter rules at the time if insurers had told MPs what costs they were hiding.
'It would have been obvious if life insurers had urged regulators to provide as much cost information as possible,' Hartlief said.
When the Supreme Court, which often but not always follows the opinions, will rule is not yet known.
Moreover, Hartlief does not say exactly what information the insurers should have provided then.
As a result, the final outcome is still uncertain.
This case plays out primarily against NN.
But Woekerpolis.nl also has cases pending, or in preparation, against Aegon, Reaal, ASR and Achmea.
Many of those cases await the NN case, the first class action.

Supervision Is Deutsche doing SRI, or greenwashing?
Regulators are investigating possible deception by DWS, the asset management arm of Deutsche Bank, about the sustainable nature of its investments.
Supervision Regulators are investigating possible deception by DWS, the asset management arm of Deutsche Bank, about the sustainability content of its investments.
No self-respecting asset manager gets away with it these days: offering sustainable investment products.
A flood of sustainability jargon meets the client: ' Impact investing', 'green future funds' and the 'integration' of 'ESG'.
That is the abbreviation for environmental, social, governance and stands for decent treatment of the environment, fellow human beings and animals, plus good corporate governance.

In parallel with the rise of SRI, there is a growing risk of greenwashing: financial institutions pretending to invest clients' money responsibly when in reality they care little about, for example, companies' carbon emissions or working conditions.
Financial regulators are beginning to lose patience with this kind of deception, it emerged Thursday.

Business newspaper The Wall Street Journal reported that the US regulator SEC and the US Justice Department have opened an investigation into possible illegal practices at DWS , the asset management arm of Deutsche Bank.
German regulator BaFin is also scrutinizing DWS, it was announced later that day.
Investors reacted with shock.
In Frankfurt, DWS' share price plunged more than 13 percent.
Parent company Deutsche Bank lost more than 2 percent.
Investigation following internal turmoil.
The investigation follows a revelation in the same newspaper, earlier this month , about internal turmoil at DWS over the issue of sustainability.
In March, the asset manager reported in its 2020 annual report that more than half of its invested assets that year - 459 billion euros - had gone through a process of "ESG integration.
Specifically, companies would have been graded on their performance on environmental, social conditions and good governance.

"We have put ESG at the heart of everything we do," Internal emails accessed by The Wall Street Journal showed a very different picture: "only a small portion" of investments had been screened for ESG, according to an internal analysis, because no reliable ESG measurements existed for these investments.
In addition, DWS's then head of sustainability, Desiree Fixler, had said in a presentation to the board in February that the company had no clear ambition or strategy in the sustainability area.
For example, DWS had no policy on companies operating in coal.
Also, according to Fixler, "ESG" was seen within DW as a specialized area - not a core business.
Critical Fixler fired.
One day before the presentation of the annual report, Fixler was fired.
The reason for this, Fixler told The Wall Street Journal , was that she had been too outspoken to the company's top brass about its failing sustainability policies.

"Making good cheer with statements about climate and inclusion, without living up to them, is quite damaging, because this prevents money and action from finding their way to the right place," Fixler judged her former employer.
A DWS spokesman declined to comment to NRC on Thursday.
The head of sustainability at DWS was fired because of her critical stance.
The SEC's investigation into DWS is not an isolated case.
Other regulators have also been paying closer attention to greenwashing recently.
In the EU, where SRI has been booming, asset managers have been required since March to be more open about whether and, if so, how they factor in sustainability.
The AFM monitors compliance with this EU directive.

The Dutch regulator is also investigating sustainability disclosures in fund prospectuses. : "We know that people are willing to settle for lower returns if the category they are investing in is green.
It is important then to be able to establish that such an investment is actually green."
A difficult problem is that there are not yet clear criteria on what are sustainable investments, and what are not.
This is what DWS staff also said internally.
The EU has now adopted a system of criteria called the "taxonomy.
These rules should take effect from 2022.

Poland taken to task again for punishing judges A new European Court ruling does little to hurt Polish government as long as the European Commission does not attach a fine to dismantling the rule of law.
Disciplinary law in Poland, instituted by the conservative-nationalist government, violates European law.
Therefore, the specially created disciplinary chamber is not allowed to judge independent judges.
That is what the European Court of Justice's Advocate General concluded again Thursday in a case brought by the European Commission against Poland.
The judges of the European Court in Luxembourg almost always follow the Advocate General in their judgments.
So far, however, their rulings have had little effect as far as the Polish rule of law is concerned.
Especially since the European Commission does not attach any consequences.
The Court in Luxembourg already ruled last year that the Polish disciplinary chamber must cease its work, but when it failed to do so, the European Commission failed to impose a penalty payment.
Since a coalition led by the PiS party came to power in Poland in 2015, it has systematically placed the judiciary under political coercion.
This is done through - not always legal - appointments of party faithful to crucial positions and the establishment of a disciplinary regime for judges who oppose the "reforms.
For the latter purpose, a disciplinary chamber was created within the Supreme Court to take away judges' immunity, office, salary and, in extreme cases, liberty.
Deterrent effect.
Attorney General Evgeni Tanchev now calls the disciplinary chamber "not an independent and impartial court" because of its political composition and far-reaching powers.

In an initial response on Twitter, State Attorney General Sebastian Kaleta called the European Union "not competent."
According to him, there is "double standards" because the Court previously ruled that judges in other countries may be appointed - conditionally - by politicians.
The Polish disciplinary chamber does not always rule against critical judges, but it already took away several judges' immunity and salary.
On this very Thursday, Wlodzimierz Wrobel, himself a distinguished Supreme Court justice and a respected scholar, must appear before the chamber.
Officially, the prosecution wants to prosecute him because his actions would have caused an innocent man to spend one month too long in prison .
In reality, the prosecution wants to get rid of Wrobel to further strengthen political control over the Supreme Court.

15 min
Insurer Axa's decision to impose a cap on the indexation of top salaries is legally valid as long as the company gives the correct notice.
So says lawyer specializing in labor law Filip Tilleman on "The Morning" on Radio 1.
Yesterday Axa's management announced that those earning more than 5,400 euros gross will no longer receive indexation on anything above that limit.
"Axa can do that because until now the company paid more than agreed upon in the collective bargaining agreement," Tillemans clarified.
Axa, one of our country's largest insurers, puts a cap on indexing wages.
From January, wages will only be indexed to 5,400 euros gross.
Those earning more will receive no indexation on anything above that limit.
So, for example, those who earn 6,000 euros gross will no longer receive indexation on the last 600 euros.
Remarkable, because in Belgium there is a system of automatic wage indexation, and so the question arises: is it allowed?
Management at Axa says it does, but unions still question the legal framework.
"The Morning" on Radio 1 checks in with Filip Tilleman, a lawyer specializing in labor law.
Yes, as long as the correct notice is given, Tilleman sounds clear.
"The situation at Axa is an absolute exception.
Every worker in our country has a fundamental right to an indexation of wages, but the system may differ in terms of time or percentage, for example.
The agreements around indexation will be anchored in sectoral labor agreements (collective bargaining agreements)."
The collective bargaining agreement for the insurance industry states that the scales should be automatically indexed, but Axa pays more than those scales.
"In the past, Axa did more than what they were legally required to do," Tilleman clarified.
"So they indexed higher than what the collective bargaining agreement called for, and it is this supplement that they now want to reverse.
That is possible, but then a certain notice period must also be used and it is not fixed, so there could be discussion about that now."
Belgian companies have also made changes to their indexing terms in the past, Tillemans noted.
"Again, these were companies that went beyond what was agreed to in the collective bargaining agreements, but changed the siutation under pressure from foreign parent companies."
Belgium and Luxembourg are the only countries with a system of automatic wage indexation, so foreign companies often look at labor costs in our country with different eyes.
"Then there is also pressure on Belgian managements," Tilleman said.
"But again, if the indexation is contained in a collective bargaining agreement, one cannot change it unless one went too far."
There, too, Tilleman is clear: If the unions or employees were in doubt about the notice period used, for example, they could go to the labor court.
"You can then put Axa in default and claim back overdue wages - because that's what this is all about."

Ecology Further migration does not always pay off for wintering sanderlings wintering in Western Europe from Greenland do better than birds migrating to West Africa.
Sanderlings that make the effort to fly all the way from their breeding grounds in Greenland to West Africa in the fall do not always do so well.
So write biologist Jeroen Reneerkens of the University of Groningen and colleagues this week in the journal Journal of Animal Ecology.
Species that choose to stay on the beaches of Western Europe are doing a lot better than "triplets" wintering under the Ghanaian sun.
There are more of them alive after a year and, moreover, they arrive back in the breeding grounds in Greenland earlier in the spring.
The sanderling ( Calidris alba ) is a small, gray bird that also dribbles along the tideline in the winter in the Netherlands in search of shrimp and other food.
Birds that breed in Greenland, among other places, winter scattered throughout the coast between Vlieland in the north and Walvis Bay in Namibia in the south.

Using observations of thousands of individually identifiable birds with color-rings on their legs, Reneerkens and colleagues were able to calculate the survival of different groups of birds in recent years.
Birds wintering in Ghana and Mauritania, with an annual survival rate of 75 percent, performed measurably worse than those wintering in Western Europe.
There, 85 percent made it to the next year.
The cost of flying on.
Yet the problem is not necessarily in distance, the researchers write.
Because remarkably, birds that flew all the way through to southern Africa also outperformed West Africa goers with 85 percent survival.
"In migratory bird biology, the adage for a long time was that the biological costs of flying through would outweigh the benefits of such an 'expensive' journey.
But further, then, is not necessarily better," Reneerkens concludes.
"It apparently does not pay for a migratory bird to fly on from the Netherlands to Ghana, but it does pay to travel an additional 4,000 km to southern Africa.

The contrast is especially striking at the border:

That difference evokes surprise.
The main explanation is that there is still a lot of CO2 gain to be made in Germany by switching to gas.
Whereas the majority of Dutch households have had natural gas connections for years, in Germany a quarter of homes still have oil-fired heating.
Most are over 20 years old.
Those boilers are very polluting.
If all those oil boilers were replaced by a new high-efficiency natural gas boiler, the total CO2 emissions of German households would be reduced by about 30 percent.
Trade-in bonus.
The dirty boilers are also a thorn in the side of the German government, which is why there is talk of a "Wärmewende."
But how do you reach them?
A few weeks ago, the president of the CDU, Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer, suggested introducing nationwide a so-called Abwrackprämie, a trade-in bonus for old oil stoves.
How high that premium will be is not yet known.
When asked by NIS, the ruling CDU party could not yet answer questions.
It is assumed that a large proportion of switchers prefer gas.
This is mainly because the infrastructure is already there.
Of the 5.6 million households with oil stoves, more than 2 million can switch to the gas grid fairly easily.
Also, gas boiler installation is cheaper than most renewable energy sources.
There is another reason why natural gas is seen as a reasonable alternative to oil in Germany.
"There is a very different view of this energy source here," says Philipp Pausder, ceo of a large installation company based in Berlin.
"This is because politics responds to the emotions of the population."
Those emotions vary from country to country.
In Germany, after the Fukushima disaster, the consensus has emerged that nuclear power is too dangerous.
"In the Netherlands, the earthquakes have had that same effect on natural gas: there is popular support for turning off the gas tap.
Thus, in Europe, different events leave their mark on climate policy," is Pausder's impression.
Dead end road.
So switching from oil to gas is a step in the right direction for Germany.
But there is also criticism.
Experts call this choice a short-term solution and under-ambitious.
One such critical expert is Christoph Podewils of climate think tank Agora.
"Choosing natural gas may be good for now, but it's also a dead end," he says.
"Because those boilers often stay in place for 20 to 30 years.
With gas, we won't succeed in getting CO2 emissions to zero."
According to Podewils, it is therefore better to skip gas as a heat source and go for insulation and truly renewable sources.

Never before so little sea ice measured around Antarctica 15:10 in Interior Yet this is not necessarily bad news, climate scientists say.
The amount of sea ice at both the North Pole and the South Pole is being closely monitored by climate scientists.
Still, it is too early to say whether current developments around Antarctica are worrisome and indicate an acceleration of melting.
Indeed, the new record may also have been caused by natural variations.
Until recently, ice at the North Pole in particular was melting more and more; since measurements began, the area of sea ice there has decreased by about half.
Also, the ice there is not as thick now.
If you combine thickness and surface area, about 75 percent of all sea ice there is gone.
By the way, this does not cause sea level rise because that ice floats on the Arctic Ocean.
However, it does result in solar radiation being reflected less by the ice, warming ocean water instead.
This is one of the reasons why this area is (much) than the rest of the world.
Around Antarctica, the amount of sea ice remained virtually stable for a long time.
A maximum record was even broken in winter several years ago.
Consequently, many factors influence the amount of sea ice around Antarctica, says climate scientist Richard Bintanja of the University of Groningen and KNMI.
"It is a complex issue, making it difficult to say whether this situation is worrisome."
Besides global warming caused by greenhouse gas emissions, there are other processes at work here.
Such as the interaction of air circulation around Antarctica with the stratosphere and even the amount of ozone.
Bintanja: "All of these effects play a role, and they all affect the amount of sea ice around Antarctica.
As a result, we cannot rule out the possibility that this low was caused by natural variability."
However, the amount of sea ice does affect the ice shelves that surround Antarctica.
Ice shelves act as a kind of plug or cork, holding back mainland glaciers, so to speak.
If those ice shelves also disappear, glaciers can flow faster into the sea, scientists expect.
Sea ice reduces the contact of ice shelves with wave action.
"Sea ice has a fine property, which is that it dampens waves," says Bintanja.
"I've been there a few times, and was always happy when we sailed through an area with sea ice, because then there were less high waves."
Sea ice is a few meters thick frozen sea water, which shows great differences in summer and winter.
The ice shelves, attached to the mainland, are regularly a few hundred meters to even a kilometer thick.
Incidentally, these ice shelves are more vulnerable to further global warming than previously thought, researchers from TU Delft and Utrecht University concluded in a study last month .
Their findings show that lakes of meltwater can form faster on those ice shelves.
And such lakes are bad news.
When an ice shelf cracks, water from those lakes can flow into the cracks and shatter the ice shelf in a short period of time.
More than 60 percent of Antarctica's ice shelves have such cracks.
Thus, if melt lakes form everywhere, they could potentially break up faster.

Secretary of State Decision Banning Recreational Use of Nitrous Oxide Individuals may no longer purchase nitrous oxide.
Research shows that inhalation, among other things, is more likely to cause brain damage.
The Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport (VWS) bans the recreational use of nitrous oxide and places the drug on list 2 of the Opium Act.
As a result, nitrous oxide may no longer be sold to individuals.
Through a special dispensation, it does remain possible to use and sell the drug for whipped cream sprays, for example.

The decision by State Secretary Blokhuis (Health, Welfare and Sport, Christian Union) follows research by the Coordination Point for Assessment and Monitoring (CAM), part of the National Institute for Public Health and the Environment.
In a report published this Monday, the CAM states that recreational nitrous oxide use "poses a risk to Public Health."
This "substantial risk" justifies placing nitrous oxide on the list of banned substances, the study says.
Nitrous oxide thus joins the ranks of marijuana, hashish and heavy painkillers available only through a doctor's prescription.
The decision comes after a period of much uncertainty.
In recent years, the number of incidents in the Netherlands following nitrous oxide use increased significantly, but municipalities could do little to counter it.

Due to a decision by the European Court three years ago, nitrous oxide suddenly no longer fell under the Medicines Act, but under the Commodities Act and was therefore subject to less strict sales regulations as well as being legal for trade and sale.
Each municipality tried in its own way to get a grip on the use and sale of the drug.
Because nitrous oxide will now fall under the Opium Act, it will be removed from the Commodities Act.
Especially for adolescents and young adults, nitrous oxide has enormous appeal.
In a few years, sucking on a balloon has become commonplace for this group, according to research conducted by the Trimbos Institute two years ago.
Inhaling nitrous oxide produces a brief intoxication lasting from thirty seconds to a few minutes.
Users become lightheaded and euphoric, sounds blend together.
Drug problem.
"The use of nitrous oxide has developed into a drug problem," said State Secretary Blokhuis in a press release issued by VWS this Monday afternoon.
Experts have repeatedly called attention to this.
The National Poisoning Information Center (NVIC) at UMC Utrecht has seen an increase in the number of nitrous oxide "intoxications" starting in 2015: from 13 in 2015 to 54 in 2018.
In the first half of 2019, 67 poisonings include chest pain, tingling in arms and legs, dizziness, confusion.
Excessive and long-term use of nitrous oxide can cause vitamin B-12 deficiency and there is a risk of brain damage or paraplegia.
Dangerous in traffic.
Nitrous oxide use is also increasingly causing problems in traffic, police report.
Figures show that between 2017 and 2018, the number of traffic incidents possibly involving nitrous oxide tripled from 130 to 380.
Through June this year, the tally stands at 960.
Motorists lose control of the wheel after "ballooning" or are not paying attention while driving because they are filling a balloon with gas.
About 20 users have also been treated at burn centers across the country this year.
Those while filling the balloon clamped the gas tank between their legs and did not realize that the tank got very cold.
A spokesman last summer in NRC : "They suffered very severe frostbite injuries."
Because nitrous oxide is also used as a propellant in the food industry, an exception is made for those applications.
The Opium Law Decree will include an exemption that does allow nitrous oxide to be sold for those purposes.
Blokhuis: "After all, it should remain ordinary to be able to order a topping of whipped cream with your apple pie."
According to Blokhuis, the "proposed measure" requires "complex elaboration."
According to criminologist and drug researcher Ton Nabben of the Hogeschool van Amsterdam, compliance with the new measure may still cause problems in practice.
"How do you know that the whipped cream cartridges bought at the Blokker are used to spray whipped cream and not to fill balloons?"
With trafficking in nitrous oxide becoming punishable, the question is how the market will develop.
Several cases are known to police, the CAM investigation reported, with "known drug criminals fully engaged in the import, wholesale and distribution of nitrous oxide."
The study also shows that many more criminals are engaging in laughing gas.
By prohibiting sales for recreational use, it creates the risk that they will completely take over the illegal market.

That lifestyle helps stay healthy is well known, but the authors of the volume want to show that sometimes it also makes patients better.
Gerjan Navis, internist-nephrologist at UMC Groningen, for example, wrote a contribution on lifestyle and chronic kidney injury.

Positive effect.

"Evidence folder" is a big word for the volume.
The studies show that lifestyle changes can sometimes help fight a disease or reduce medication use.
But most of the studies described are still waiting for better scientific evidence.
The authors therefore argue for more funding for research.
"There are few large-scale, long-term studies on the effect of lifestyle," says Hanneke Molema of the Netherlands Innovation Center for Lifestyle Medicine.

"It turns out that if we use a lifestyle coach with some of this group, many of the symptoms disappear spontaneously."

Kinepolis Group was formed in 1997 by merger of two family-owned companies, from the Flemish Bert and Claeys families.
A year later, the company went public on the Brussels Stock Exchange.
Years earlier, founder Albert Bert had established a reputation as an innovator in the previously fragmented Belgian cinema industry.
He was the first to build a megaplex, in the late 1980s, a 25-screen cinema complex at the foot of the Atomium in Brussels.
Thus Kinepolis developed into the market leader in Belgium - which did not escape even cartel watchdog BMA.
Kinepolis focused on foreign countries for further growth.
Not every cinephile gets hot for such a megaplex, but a revenue model it is.
Today, Kinepolis has this kind of huge cinema complex in all the countries in which it operates.
"The quantity of theaters and being able to tailor movie offerings to local audiences works in many places," said analyst Kris Kippers of financial services firm Kepler Cheuvreux from Brussels.
What also characterizes this cinema company is the collection of customer data - on favorite movie genres, actors and directors.
Kippers: "Kinepolis has a broad knowledge of its customer base and does a lot of direct marketing .
Top executive Eddy Duquenne himself says that this is how they want to become 'the sommelier of film.'"
Duquenne came to the helm as an outsider, after difficult years with an expensive German takeover and the exit of the Claeys family.
Nevertheless, Kinepolis is still listed as a family business; roughly half of the shares are held by the Bert family.
Joost Bert, son of founder Albert, is chairman.
Kinepolis now operates in nine countries, including the Netherlands.
It has eighteen cinemas here, following the recent opening of a complex in Den Bosch and an acquisition in Spijkenisse.
The most high-profile acquisitions in recent years have been more distant.
After expanding in Europe, Kinepolis made a huge move in 2017, to Canada.
In one fell swoop, it bought 45 cinemas with 325 screens from Landmark Cinemas.

Canada provided a springboard to the U.S., where Kinepolis bought 10 complexes last quarter.
De Boer sees a risk: "Managing becomes more difficult with different time zones and cultures."
For now, the expansive strategy is not harming the group.

Operating income grows correspondingly to about 100 million euros.

Each week, Annemiek Leclaire presents a reader's question to experts.
Mother: "Our 15-year-old son's best friend has been in contact with the police several times for vandalism.

Should we start discouraging friendship (temporarily) or is there no point?
My son himself is doing well, at school and beyond."
Creating resilience.
Jelle Jolles : "Many boys at this age stage like excitement.
They are "sensation seekers," but still have little idea of possible consequences.
Obviously, you want to prevent your son from being involved in transgressive behavior, or getting a criminal record.
"Engage with him in an interested manner.
If you strongly disapprove of his friend's behavior, or forbid the friendship, there is a danger that your son will continue the contact but not tell you about it.
"Create a situation where your son can easily describe what happened, and how he feels about it.
It is possible that he too sees his friend's behavior as a problem but does not know how to talk to him about it.
Middle adolescents are often stuck in a social group or friendship in which they feel uncomfortable but do not yet know how to deal with it.
"That the police disapprove of the behavior is not an incentive for some boys of this age not to do it, quite the contrary.
Perhaps your son needs his friend's esteem, and wants to belong.
"Show your understanding for your son.
Polish what his own ideas are on how to deal with this pre-treatment.
Ask what it does to him that his friend has now come into contact with the police several times.
And how do other friends feel about that?
"Through this joint 'articulation,' your son develops the skill of thinking more nuanced about his own position toward his friend and his behavior.
This also makes it easier for him to start the conversation with this boy.
This is how you create resilience in your child."
Doors open.
Loes Keijsers : "Try to assess how serious your son's friend's behavior is.
In criminal behavior among young people, we distinguish two forms: you have the serious variant, in which children often get into trouble from an early age.
As a result, they miss out on a normal school career and grow into a more serious form of crime.
"The other form is more innocuous, and is part of experimental growing up: a shoplifting, setting a fire, too much booze.
This is something most children grow over.
"Make sure you properly inform your child of the consequences.
Coming into contact with the police can have far-reaching consequences.
For example, those with criminal records are sometimes not allowed to take internships.
You can say, "Do that kind of thing a little bit with reason.

Talk through scenarios: "Suppose it goes too far for you, do you have an excuse ready to walk away?
"Banning the friendship may be counterproductive.
Children may well accept that parents set rules about drinking and drug use, for example, because that is part of parental caring.
Banning friends is a different story: that is about the personality of young people, and in this they do not allow themselves to be thwarted.
"Instead, invite this boy and the rest of the group of friends home.
Put up a projector, a PlayStation.
Then they have something to do, and you can watch a little bit."

Privacy Soon Consumers Bank at BigTech.
Time for adequate action by regulators and consumers, argue Tijn Croon Lisa van den Boogaard and Jurriaan Parie
The banking industry is being shaken up considerably by European Payment Service Directive 2 (PSD2) legislation.
With the user's explicit consent, third parties can access the individual's financial transaction history.
The legislation aims to increase competition, lower prices and improve services in the financial services industry.
But in practice, consumer financial data risks being siphoned off to the already supreme technology companies.
Lisa van den Boogaard Tijn Croon and Jurriaan Parie won the Bank of England's PSD2 Technology Competition and are currently doing a month of research at the bank's Fintech department in London.
Applications of the PSD2 legislation are fast approaching.
As of Sept. 14, 2019, all European banks must comply with technical standards to enable financial data sharing.
Newly introduced apps from technology companies could soon then point consumers to cheaper loans, insurance or energy contracts, and they could take care of the administration.
Because consumers can switch more easily and quickly, competition among companies results in more user-friendly services and lower prices.
In short, the consumer benefits.
Yet that coin also has a flip side.
Technology giants are cashing in on adding consumer financial data to existing user profiles as well.
With their capital and knowledge of building large-scale digital infrastructure, they are able to gain significant market share in the financial services sector in no time as well.
Thus, the "data silos" of banks are in danger of merging into the already overflowing data barns of BigTech companies.
Many users say they find financial data too personal to share.
At the same time, they have been trading highly confidential location data for the use of seemingly free and efficient online services for years.
That users still share personal data against their own intentions is also known as the privacy paradox.
So why not allow access to bank records if there is more convenience or a financial benefit to be gained from doing so?
Competition watchdogs, privacy regulators and (inter)national financial authorities need to anticipate BigTech interference in financial services to protect consumers.
Amazon issued more than a billion in loans to US SMEs in 2017.
In 2018, GooglePay took over the Indian payments system at a breakneck pace.
And this year, AliPay and WeChat already provided more online payments in China than Visa and MasterCard worldwide.
Are European regulators able to prevent disruption of the financial services sector by PSD2 in time?
It is troubling to note that this question is not being asked in the public debate.
Let alone a unified European response.
That other European legislation, the General Data Protection Regulation (AVG), is a good start.
It gives regulators the ability to impose strangling fines on companies - up to four percent of total revenue - if they fail to comply with the new privacy requirements.
Consumer rights are more deeply entrenched than ever in the AVG, but even so, it does not break the privacy paradox.
It is naïve to expect that placing more checkmarks will stop consumers from using data-guzzling apps.
PSD2 and the AVG offer consumers more choices and control over their own data, but that is not enough.
Without redefining the concept of competition and dominance in the digital age, PSD2 opens the door for Google, Amazon, Facebook and Apple to expand their service offerings even further.
These companies are not out to dominate the entire financial sector, but only pick the profitable cherry-picked and buy up potential competitors.
Without regulatory action to name and curb the dominance of BigTechs, we are heading toward a world where only a handful of companies call the shots.
A world in which consumers go through life less and less anonymously.
Until regulators really wake up, the future of a healthy digital society is also in your hands.
Break the paradox and think twice about whether the benefits of a free service are worth giving up your (financial) data.

US rivals will try to recover the wreckage of the downed F-35C, experts say
Istanbul.

Experts stated that many countries such as China and Russia, which are in competition with the US, will try to reach the wreckage of the F-35C fighter jet that crashed during the exercise in the South China Sea, and that if it reaches the wreckage, all critical information about the aircraft will fall into the hands of these countries, while the US will make a great effort to prevent this.

Prof. Dr. Mesut Hakkı Caşın, a lecturer at Yeditepe University Faculty of Law, and Arda Mevlütoğlu, a defense policy expert, evaluated the crash of the "F-35C Şimşek" type fighter jet of the US Navy on January 25 while conducting exercises in the South China Sea, the allegations that China is trying to reach the wreckage of the plane and the possible crises between the US and China due to the downed plane.

Prof. Dr. Caşın said that the accident, which occurred while the Carl Vinson and Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier fleets were conducting joint exercises in the South China Sea, could escalate tensions, especially by confronting China and the US, which see the region as their territorial waters.

Noting that the US-China intelligence war has begun in the Pacific and that the US will not allow the wreckage of the high-tech aircraft, which cost 110 million dollars, to fall into China's hands, Caşın stated that reaching the wreckage of the plane would mean that very critical information about the plane would fall into China's hands.

Noting that not only China, but also Russia and other countries that compete with the US in the defense industry will try to reach the wreckage, Caşın said, "If China reaches the wreckage, it will access all the critical information of this aircraft, which has radar concealment, sensors and data processing equipment, 5th generation advanced warfare technology, learn and copy its hardware, and do the same."

Caşın said that according to the law of the sea, the loot found at sea belongs to the finder and emphasized that the US will never allow the plane, which belongs to the US, to fall into the hands of China.
Caşın said that the US could take control of the area where the plane crashed and even legally try to prevent China from reaching the wreckage.

Similarly, Caşın reminded that 5 aircraft crashed in 2018-2022 and said, "On April 9, 2019, a Japanese F-35 crashed in the Pacific Ocean, and in November 2021, a British F-35 that took off from Egypt crashed off the coast of Syria.
Three other F-35s crashed inside the US, there is not much information about them."

Caşın said that the F-35, F-22, C-17 transport aircraft, the most strategic aircraft of the USA, and the B-2 heavy bombers that will change the fate of the war were produced by the Chinese by copying them one-to-one: "On April 1, 2001, China forced the US EP-3E intelligence plane to make an emergency landing on Hainan Island.
He detained the pilots.
After the plane's hardware was copied, the crew was handed over to the US.
Therefore, China not only avenged the shooting down of the Chinese Embassy in Belgrade by the United States on May 7, 1999, but also obtained intelligence information about its plane.
By copying these US strategic weapons, China has gained superiority over the US in the air force as well as in the navy.
This has actually been China's biggest challenge to the US in the 21st century."

"Reaching the wreckage is important for all countries competing with the US" Defense policy expert Arda Mevlütoğlu stated that at the end of such accidents of systems such as aircraft, ships and submarines with advanced technology, parts or all of them are tried to be seized and that there are many similar examples.

Mevlütoğlu emphasized that the US will make great efforts to reach the wreckage of the plane, which has serious intelligence information due to its critical systems, sensors and structural features, and that it will take the necessary measures to prevent the plane from falling into the hands of China.
"Since the F-35C contains very advanced technologies, reaching its wreckage as soon as possible is a very critical event for a country like China.
It is also extremely important for countries in competition with Russia or the US.
Therefore, these countries can be expected to compete for access to the wreckage."

Mevlütoğlu said that similar incidents had happened before and that the F-117 aircraft of the US army, which was invisible, was shot down by the Serbs during the NATO operation in the former Yugoslavia on March 27, 1999 and that the Serbs gave the downed plane to Russia.

Mevlütoğlu reminded that the wreckage of a Golf II class Soviet submarine that sank in the Atlantic Ocean in 1968 was also recovered by the United States in 1974 with a specially equipped ship called Glomar Explorer and a top secret operation: "On April 1, 2001, China forced the US EP-3E intelligence plane to make an emergency landing and detained the crew.
He had released the pilots after copying the plane's intelligence information.
In another example, in December 2011, Iran forced a US drone to land on its territory and then captured it.
Iran, which examined the vehicle, later built a similar one itself."

Omar Khayyam, a poet who left his mark with his contributions to the world of science as well as his poems
Istanbul.

It has been 891 years since the death of Omar Khayyam, who wrote 18 important works in the fields of philosophy, literature, mathematics and astronomy in addition to his poems and had an important place in the history of world science.
Although the exact date of birth of the Iranian poet, philosopher, scholar and astronomer Omar Khayyam is unknown, according to various sources, he was born on May 18, 1048 in Nishapur, Iran.
The poet spent most of his life in Nishapur and Samarkand and completed his education in these cities.

Khayyam received his first education under Sheikh Muhammad Mansuri, a well-known researcher in Balkh, and then continued his studies under Imam Mowaffaq of Nishapur, one of the greatest teachers of the Nishapur region.

Khayyam attended the same madrasah as Nizamül-Mülk, the vizier of the Great Seljuk Empire and the author of the book "Siyasetname", and received education from the famous scholar of the time, Muvaffakeddin Abdüllatif ibn al-Lübad.
He served as an advisor to the Seljuk ruler Melikşah.
In his ruba, Omar Khayyam dealt with life and human issues such as the world, existence, God, the state and forms of social organization.
He transferred his internal reasoning to understand the universe into his quatrains with a rare literary language.
Khayyam, who has an important place in the history of world science, became one of the world's leading scientists in mathematics and astronomy and conducted many scientific studies.
Khayyam prepared the "Jalali" calendar, more precise than the Gregorian and Hijri calendars.
The poet and scientist Khayyam, who was mostly interested in astronomy at night, also worked on geometry and medicine.
According to research, he was the first to use the Binomial expansion with the "Pascal triangle", named after the French mathematician Blaise Pascal.

Although there are 158 rubais in which Omar Khayyam expresses his thoughts and feelings in a subtle language and which have been translated into many languages, especially Turkish, the number of rubais attributed to him exceeds a thousand.

Khayyam, who preferred to wander from time to time in science and art centers such as Samarkand, Bukhara, Balkh and Isfahan, wrote 18 works in the fields of philosophy, literature, mathematics and astronomy.
Khayyam, who also served as an advisor to the Seljuk ruler Melikshah, is believed to have followed the school of Ibn Sina and to have preferred the beliefs of the Batinites and Mu'tazilites.
He was the subject of the best-selling book "Samarkand".
Omar Khayyam passed away on December 4, 1131 at the age of 83.
Khayyam's mausoleum is located near the square that bears his name in Nishapur, a city in Reza Khorasan in northeastern Iran.
In 1934, Reza Shah Pahlavi commissioned the architect, sculptor, painter and Dean of the Faculty of Fine Arts at the University of Tehran, Prof. Reza Shah Pahlavi.

The tomb, which was built by Hosheng Seyhun and completed in 1963, was designed in the shape of a tent in reference to his nickname "Khayyam", meaning tentmaker.

Khayyam's rubais were written in talik calligraphy in the color of Nishapur's famous turquoise stone on the sides of the monument, which is made of white marble, 22 meters high and 18 meters wide, in a 20 thousand square meter garden.
