Unconscious whitening can damage teeth
Teeth whitening is the treatment of removing the colored substances formed in the porous enamel and dentin structure on the surface of the teeth with teeth whitening gels.
Tooth color may vary according to individuals.

These internal and external discolorations have different causes such as physiological discoloration, discoloration after amalgam filling, discoloration due to antibiotic use during pregnancy and infancy, internal discoloration of the tooth due to root canal treatment, discoloration due to frequent use of products such as coffee, tea and cigarettes, and discoloration caused by the loss of vitality of the living tissue inside the tooth as a result of trauma.
THERE ARE DIFFERENT METHODS OF TEETH WHITENING.

Teeth whitening methods that differ according to their techniques and application areas include home-type teeth whitening, office-type teeth whitening (whitening in a clinical setting), combined teeth whitening and single teeth whitening.
In the home-type teeth whitening method known as home teeth whitening, first of all, personalized whitening plaques are prepared by taking measurements from inside the mouth.
A certain amount of teeth whitening gel is placed in these plaques and applied.
These people should use the plaque for an average of 1-15 days, using it for at least 4-6 hours during the day or 8-10 hours during night sleep.
The important thing to be careful about home teeth whitening is not to apply the gel more than described.
Otherwise, the gel overflowing through the plaque will irritate the gums.
In such a case, the gums should be washed immediately and the dentist should be contacted.

The application time of the laser teeth whitening method is shorter. "Laser teeth whitening method, also known as office-type teeth whitening, which is performed in a clinical environment, is performed by a specialist physician.
This process, which is performed by activating the whitening gel applied on the teeth by the dentist with the help of UV light or laser, takes about an hour on average.
Two methods are used together in combined teeth whitening In the combined teeth whitening method, which is home and office whitening, two methods are applied together.
After the procedure performed in the clinic, the whitening process is supported by home application for 2-3 days.

In the single tooth whitening (internal whitening) method applied to teeth that change color after root canal treatment, the filling in the tooth is removed, whitening gel is applied to the opened cavity and the tooth is closed with a temporary filling. Sessions are repeated every 3 days until the desired color is reached.
Smoking, tea and coffee consumption increases tooth discoloration Teeth whitening method suitable for each individual's condition varies.

Under normal conditions, only laser or home whitening is sufficient in cases where the tooth color is not too dark and a few tones are desired to be lightened, while the application of the combined teeth whitening method to lighten the color of teeth that are over-colored due to smoking, coffee or tea provides more effective results.
Whitening done under the control of a dentist is not harmful It is among the issues that are wondered whether teeth whitening is harmful in the society.
Whitening performed under the control of a dentist does not harm the teeth.
However, whitening methods can cause sensitivity to air, very hot or cold foods and drinks.
This sensitivity of the teeth is usually expected to disappear within a day or two.
This is normal and expected.
The permanence of the procedure varies depending on the consumption habits of the person The whitening process varies according to the person.
While it takes about two weeks to achieve the result of the procedure, the removal of discoloration due to antibiotic use is more difficult and requires a longer period of time.
The permanence of whitening varies according to the patient's use of colored liquids such as tea, coffee, cola, wine and smoking.
If the whitening process is repeated every 6 months, teeth whitening becomes permanent.
Today, many products are promoted and sold on the internet and social media channels under the name of "Natural" teeth whitening method.
Different whitening applications such as turmeric, coconut, strawberry, aluminum foil, lemon and walnut shell are tried and recommended.
However, it should be kept in mind that such substances do not help whiten teeth and will cause irreversible damage and sensitivity on the teeth and should never be used.

Building tax exemption for pensioners

Considering that May is the month of payment of the first installment of the property tax, I wanted to devote this article to a subject related to the property tax, or rather, I wanted to remind you of a subject I have written about before.

Article 8/2 of the Real Estate Tax Law authorizes the Council of Ministers (President of the Republic after the Constitutional amendment) to reduce the tax rate up to zero for "those whose income consists exclusively of pensions received from social security institutions established by law (), if they have a single dwelling (including usufruct rights) within the borders of Turkey that does not exceed 200 square meters gross".

The Law also emphasizes that this provision will also apply to the part of the shares of the above-mentioned persons if they own a single dwelling with shares, but it will not apply to the dwellings used for recreation purposes at a certain time.

I will leave aside for now the discussions on the contradiction of the authorization granted to the President of the Republic to the principle of legality of taxation. Let us examine the subtleties of benefiting from the zero-rate tax by stating that the zero-rate tax application is also in question for 2020 in accordance with the authorization used for 2006 and subsequent years with the Council of Ministers Decree No. 2006/11450 dated 20/12/2006, and that the said authorization has been used.
Only those who receive a pension from a social security institution established under Turkish law are eligible for this benefit.
This can be a pension or a death pension for a deceased person such as a father or spouse.
Even those who receive both a pension and a death pension can benefit from this opportunity.
However, those who receive pensions from foreign social security institutions cannot benefit from this opportunity.
An important condition to be eligible for this benefit is that "the income consists exclusively of social security pension".
Those with other income cannot benefit from this facility.

For example, those who receive a monthly salary from the Social Security Institution but also earn income by engaging in commercial or self-employment activities, those who have rental income, those who continue to work for wages by paying social security support premium cannot benefit from this opportunity.
The limits of the condition that the income should only "consist of a social security pension" are important here.
There has to be a limit to this.
It would be appropriate to draw this limit as income subject to income tax.
Otherwise, a pensioner winning a lottery jackpot or a pensioner selling his or her car is also income.
The fact that a widowed pensioner is entitled to compensation or receives alimony from a divorced spouse does not, in my view, violate the eligibility requirements.
If viewed in this way, the concept of income becomes unlimited, and there is no indication that the Legislature intended this result.
The pensioner can even invest his or her pension in time deposits, treasury bills, funds or repo transactions.
Although such income is subject to income tax as income from movable capital, it is the income brought by the ordinary course of life.
I think these should be considered separately.

For this reason, the Ministry of Finance stated in the General Communiqué on Real Estate Tax No. 45 that "all kinds of securities capital income income obtained by those whose income consists exclusively of salaries received from social security institutions established by law and whose annual amount does not exceed the amount in the second income bracket of the tariff written in Article 103 of the Income Tax Law, which is valid in the year preceding the year in which the building tax discount is utilized, will not be considered among the incomes that constitute an obstacle to benefit from the reduced (zero) building tax rate."
According to this statement, those whose total gross securities capital revenues do not exceed 40,000 liras in 2019 will be able to benefit from this opportunity in 2020.

However, the fact that this explanation is only for securities income, and that the ministry is not authorized to discriminate between income categories, is contrary to the principles of equality and justice in terms of subject matter, as well as contrary to the law in terms of authority.

For example, a retiree who meets the other conditions in 2019 but earns 39,000 liras of deposit interest will not pay property tax in 2020, while a retiree who earns 5,200 liras of residential rental income and does not even submit an income tax return due to the exemption will pay property tax for his only residence.

Although this issue was notified by the Ombudsman's Office with the Decision dated 16.1.2019 and the Ministry should take action in accordance with Law No. 6328, it does not correct the General Communiqué in question, leading to the continuation of unfair practices.
This General Communiqué should be corrected.
I will discuss other details in my next article.

Chinese Lunar Festival, a Traditional Day, is Lovingly Commemorated
The Moon Festival, also called the Chinese Mid-Autumn Festival, is one of the most important traditional public holidays celebrated by the Chinese people as well as by people of other races.
The Traditional Moon Festival, celebrated on the 15th day of the 8th lunar month every year, falls on September 10 this year.
The festival was first introduced as a public holiday at the beginning of the Tang Dynasty and was widely celebrated during the Song Dynasty.
During the Qing Dynasty, it became as important as the New Year (Yuan Dan).

Like any other traditional Chinese festival, the origin of the Moon Festival is told through a story passed down from generation to generation, and as usual, the story is about the "Moon Goddess Mrs. Chang", who represents the moon.
According to a Chinese legend, there was a time when 10 suns were in the sky, cooking the earth dry and taking away life and water from people.
A hero named Hou Yi climbed to the top of Mount Kunlun and shot 9 out of 10 suns with his bow and arrows, thus saving people on earth.
One day Hou Yi met the Queen Mother and received an immortality potion from her.
The potion was for one person only, and when he drank it, he would be immortal forever, living in the heavens.
Ho Yi gave the potion to his wife Chang for safekeeping.
A neighbor found out about the immortality potion and tried to take it from Chang by force while Hou Yi was away.
Desperate, Chang drank the potion and immediately became a Goddess and flew into the sky.
Because she still cared so much about her husband, she settled on the moon, a place close to earth.
When Hou Yi returned, he was devastated not to find his wife.
When he looked up at the sky to shout her name, he saw that the moon was much brighter and full that night, and he realized that Chang was on the moon.
He immediately offered Chang his favorite cake and prayed for the blessings of Heaven.
Since then, it has become a tradition for people to worship heaven and celebrate that day with cake.
Thus, the Moon Festival became well-known among the Chinese.
There was so much to do to celebrate the Chinese Lunar Festival.
However, the traditions have begun to be forgotten as most people have now started buying cakes (round cakes filled with sugar, sesame seeds and other spices).
The first time I saw the Moon Festival was in my hometown in China, I was a little girl of about 7 or 8 years old and I was introduced to it by my grandmother.
My grandmother was a traditional Chinese woman who wore buttoned Chinese shirts and had her feet tied.
On the night of the Moon Festival, my grandmother slipped quietly out of our room to go somewhere.
I was curious about what he was doing, so I tried to follow him.
My grandmother quickly pushed me back and told me to go play.
Nevertheless, I followed him out of sight in the backyard of our house.
I saw him arranging fruits and mooncakes on a plate, then he lit incense and knelt down to pray.
I watched him for a while and then I left quickly.
Later, I learned that my grandmother prayed for Heaven and Earth.
The Moon Festival is not only a festival to worship the Moon Goddess, but also to express gratitude for Heaven and Earth.
On this day, families gather together and celebrate the holiday in unity.
Fruits and moon cakes are offered to the Earth and Moon gods, and people also share them among themselves.
Traditionally, mooncakes are cut into many pieces and each member of the family receives a single piece.
If a family member is not there, a slice is always reserved for that person.

The MeerKAT Radio Telescope in South Africa,
On May 18, 2012, dawn breaks over a radio telescope dish antenna pointed skyward at the KAT-7 array.
This is a proposed site for Square Kilometer Array (SKA) telescopes in South Africa, near Carnarvon in the country's remote Northern Cape province (Reuters/Mike Hutchings).
CARNARVON, South Africa - 64 MeerKAT dish radio telescopes have been installed in the remote South African town of Carnarvon.

The goal of this scientific mega-project is to uncover extraterrestrial life and bring cosmic mysteries out of the dark. Built at a cost of $2.8 billion, MeerKAT will be incorporated into the complex Square Kilometer Array (SKA) instrument, which, when fully operational in the late 2020s, will be the world's largest and most powerful radio telescope.

According to SKA scientists, the 3,000 or so dishes to be installed in Africa and Australia will be able to scan the sky 10,000 times faster and 50 times more precisely than other telescopes, producing images that exceed the resolution quality of the Hubble Space telescope.

"MeerKAT will answer some of the key scientific questions of modern astrophysics - how galaxies formed, how they evolve, how we got here... and for these purposes MeerKAT is the best instrument in the world," said Fernando Camilo, who heads the scientists at the South African Radio Astronomy Observatory who built and operate the telescope.

At a launch attended by government officials and foreign dignitaries, Camilo released new images taken by MeerKAT of the region surrounding a supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy, 25 million light-years away.
"We weren't planning to use our telescope this early, or even before it was optimized," he told Reuters.
But what we got by rotating it to the center of the galaxy, and these stunning, best-in-the-world images show that we're doing something right, or even better than right," he said.
MeerKAT follows KAT 7 (Karoo Array Telescope), which was built in the vast semi-desert Karoo region north of Cape Town to see if South Africa could host the SKA.
There is a pun in the name: "meer" in African means "more".
MeerKat thus stands for "more than KAT".
But it is also the name of a small mammal native to the Karoo, famous for standing on its hind legs to see its surroundings.
Alongside groundbreaking astronomy research, MeerKAT is also expanding the frontiers in massive data and high-performance computing.
It is doing this with support from IBM to develop systems that can process the dizzying amount of data from each antenna with supercomputers buried underground to reduce radio interference.
When you drive an hour from Carnarvon and see MeerKAT, the largest radio telescope of its kind in the southern hemisphere, for the first time, it looks like eggs laid side by side.
But above all, each highly sensitive dish is the height of a three-story building and rotates on a fixed pedestal as it scans the sky.

Due to its remoteness and the hills that provide an extra shield against radio interference, the project site was chosen as the African home base, home to hundreds of antennas placed as far apart as Kenya and Ghana.
"The first phase of SKA 1 in South Africa is to add 133 antennas [to MeerKAT]," said Rob Adam, SKA international councillor.
The expansion is scheduled to start next year, Adam said.
The first prototype dish, made in China, has already been installed in the Northern Cape region, about 450 kilometers north of Cape Town.
He also said that MeerKAT will operate independently until it is merged with SKA 1 in 2023.

A Master's Helpers: Michelangelo's Sistine Ceiling
It was a success that needed no embellishment.
Only a small number of the greatest masters of art could have designed such a beautiful work.
Perhaps few other craftsmen could have realized its most complex parts with anything close to this success.
By some accounts, however, it seems impossible not "only" that he was so artistically brilliant, but that Michelangelo could have done it physically.
According to this legend, Michelangelo worked alone in the Sistine Chapel, as if he were working in a studio.
But it was beyond human ability for one man to do all the work required in that time alone.
Written records confirm that he used an assistant.
Teamwork
It was actually standard practice for fresco painting to be done by a team, and great masters were more likely to use this method than lesser artists.
Great craftsmen were more in demand and commissioned for the biggest projects.
Assistants were necessary because of the sheer volume of work.
Raphael, Botticelli, Masaccio, Fra Angelico and many others relied on them.
Without assistants, far fewer masterpieces would have been created.
Assistive support was not only used for mundane tasks.
Assistants with insufficient experience or skills were really doing nothing more than preparing plaster or paint.
But most of the painting was done by those with more experience and talent, under the supervision of the master and in accordance with his detailed plans.
Typically they painted the less complex parts of the fresco.
The relative simplicity of these pieces made the differences between the work of masters and helpers irrelevant.
It may seem strange that a creative master hand cannot do better technically than a skilled assistant hand.
But the reason for this is easily understood when one looks at the difference between fresco and oil on canvas.
Artists working with oil paint first paint the surface of the canvas.
This means that additions can be made after the previous paint has dried.
It also means that an artist can use as much or as little paint as they want.
Such a method of application allows for a different experiment with each brush stroke.
This is the work of the creative mind of a master.
Numerous layers of paint allow for more intricate detailing on even the smallest parts.
This is the handiwork of a master.
Fresco artists work on a piece of wall or ceiling, on wet plaster.
The painting work should be finished while the gypsum plaster is wet.
This process has two consequences: First, it is illogical to experiment while painting.
Plaster dries very quickly and does not allow artists to rethink their plans while painting.
For any changes, a section of the plaster has to be broken off and the whole picture redone.
Second, because of their size, fresco paintings cannot be as detailed as oil paintings.
This means both less detailing and greater detail.
Larger details are easier to paint than smaller ones.
Such a practice limits the space within a fresco that can benefit from the craftsman's skill.
At the same time, it requires strict adherence to a pre-existing design.
It's All in the Design.
For a fresco artist, the design creation phase of his work is the part of his work most similar to what an oil painter does on his canvas.
When the fresco artist is making preparatory drawings, he has the opportunity and time to experiment.
When the drawings are completed, the trials end.
The final drawings were prepared in the exact size of the planned fresco.
Small holes were drilled in them and fixed to the surface to be painted.
Coal dust was then pushed through the holes to outline the figures in the fresco.
Finally, the assistants could be trusted to do most of the painting.
The craftsman's dexterity was most needed for important figures and more elaborate parts of the background.
Their drawings could never be detailed enough.
The master's work had to come from his own mind.
He had to transfer the idea from his mind to the paint perfectly on the first try.
And in doing so he had to follow a strict timetable.
The success here was among the greatest feats of painting.
For the Benefit of All.
The acquisition of the necessary skills could not be achieved through school practices alone.
Renaissance apprentices worked as assistants to their masters.
They were then employed as fully trained assistants.
It was then decided who would remain in these positions and who would become a master based on their skills.
This teamwork approach was at the heart of the Renaissance's achievements.
Thanks to this, the great masters increased the number of their works.
Smaller artists contributed to the larger works, rather than taking "leftover commissions" and painting lesser works.
Geniuses were able to gradually build art from a large traditional formation to highly individual artistic interpretations.
T.S. Eliot emphasized that this combination was necessary for outstanding artistic achievement.

He recently hired a group of builders to remodel his bathroom.
But while the men were working in the house, they noticed a problem with the oven and water heater and eventually uncovered why Wilson was suffering.
The furnace was leaking carbon monoxide.
As it is an odorless and colorless gas, carbon monoxide, which is also difficult to detect, can be lethal.
In the US, it killed more than 400 people in one year.
But in Wilson's case, he had been poisoning him slowly and subtly for ten years.
"I was very surprised by that," Wilson said.

Wilson's health began to improve rapidly.
Although his voice is still not fully recovered, Wilson feels like his old self.
"I feel great," he said.
"I can't remember the last time I was this happy."
And he hugged the builders - the unexpected heroes who saved his life - one by one.
"Thank you for giving me my life back," he told them.

(Inside Edition / Screenshot) It's a great liberation, and now that Wilson has recovered after years of suffering, he hopes his story will alert people to the effects of carbon monoxide - the "silent killer".
"I feel like I've come back to life," he told ABC News.
"And I hope it will bring someone else back to life."

Sleep Apnea Symptoms Increased During Pandemic
Medicana International Izmir Hospital Chest Diseases Specialist Merda Erdemir Işık stated that the incidence of sleep apnea has increased.

Merda Erdemir Işık, Pulmonologist at Medicana International Izmir Hospital, made statements about the epidemic period. According to the statement made, sleep apnea, which is defined as respiratory arrest during sleep, threatens a large part of the society.
While sleep apnea is more common in obese people, neck thickness above 43 cm in men and 38 cm in women also predisposes to sleep apnea.

The way to get rid of sleep apnea, which can cause sudden death and heart attack during sleep, as well as work and traffic accidents due to excessive daytime sleepiness, is through weight loss, surgery or respirator treatment.

Sleep apnea, a disease caused by stenosis in the upper respiratory tract and defined as stopping breathing for more than 10 seconds during sleep, is more threatening to people with a body mass index over 30. - "The epidemic increased weight, weight increased sleep apnea" Medicana International Izmir Hospital Chest Diseases Specialist Dr.
Merda Erdemir Işık stated that the incidence of sleep apnea in the society is around 5 percent and said, "During the epidemic period, people's movements inevitably decreased with the effect of bans.
The eating habits of people who have to spend the whole day at home have also changed drastically.
These changes have led to weight gain.
Since sleep apnea is mostly seen in overweight people, the incidence of sleep apnea has also increased."

Stating that apart from obesity, neck thickness above 43 centimeters in men and 38 centimeters in women, anatomical disorders in the nose, throat and jaw that may cause stenosis in the upper respiratory tract trigger sleep apnea, Işık said, "Thyroid diseases, alcohol use, some drugs with sleep-inducing effects, advanced age, menopause in women are among the risk factors for sleep apnea.

The most common symptoms of sleep apnea syndrome are noisy snoring every night, diagnosed apnea, excessive daytime sleepiness, waking up tired in the morning, headaches and frequent trips to the toilet at night.
Witnessed apnea is when the bed partner who sleeps next to the person describes that the patient stops breathing for a while while sleeping."

Stating that the ground will be prepared for other diseases due to decreased oxygen saturation during apneas that occur during the night, Işık noted the following: "It is observed that the incidence of diseases such as heart attack, sudden death during sleep, stroke, type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure and depression is increased in people with sleep apnea.

In addition, the patient with frequent sleep interruptions due to apneas during the night cannot switch to deep and restful sleep and loss of concentration, irritability, forgetfulness, school failure, low performance at work are frequently observed due to excessive daytime sleepiness, while the risk of work accidents and traffic accidents increases."

Stating that the diagnosis of sleep apnea is made by the method called polysomnography, which is based on taking sleep records throughout the night in the sleep laboratory within the hospital, Işık said, "The severity of the disease is determined by finding the number of sleep apneas per hour in the records taken.
If the number of sleep apneas is between 5-15 per hour, it is defined as mild, between 15-30 as moderate, and above 30 as severe sleep apnea.
Patients diagnosed with sleep apnea are advised to lose weight first.
Patients with mild to moderate sleep apnea should undergo an otolaryngology examination to assess whether there is a chance of surgical correction of the disease.
Respiratory device treatment, which we call CPAP treatment, is the only treatment option for patients with severe sleep apnea."

Some daily whims may be met with 'let's get it over with', but we are in a pandemic process.

Minimum Wage Hike Falls Short of CPI and Food Inflation
The minimum wage increased to 5,500 liras as of July 2022.
According to the statement made by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, the minimum wage increased to 5,500 liras as of July 2022.
While the minimum wage was increased by 29 percent, this rate remained below the 5-month inflation and food inflation.

With the announcement of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for June, this difference will widen even more. On January 1, 2022, 333 liters of diesel or 329 liters of gasoline were purchased with one month's net minimum wage, while these amounts decreased to 206 and 202 liters as of July 1, 2022 with the new minimum wage.
Despite a 29 percent increase in the minimum wage, minimum wage earners can buy 38 percent less diesel fuel than 6 months ago.
The new minimum wage was also below the 6,391 lira hunger limit announced by Türk-İş.
The annual inflation rate announced by the Turkish Statistical Institute reached 74 percent in May, while the 5-month inflation rate was 36 percent.
In response to the rapid decline in the purchasing power of wage earners, the government raised the minimum wage by 29.3 percent.
Thus, the monthly net minimum wage increased from 4,253 liras to 5,500 liras.
However, the minimum wage hike was below both inflation and food inflation.
We analyzed the decline in purchasing power based on official data released by TurkStat.
The increase in the minimum wage is 29 percent.
However, the CPI increased by 36 percent in May compared to December of the previous year.
That's five months of inflation.
The six-month CPI should be calculated by adding the June inflation, which will be announced next week.
The food price index rose 46 percent in five months.
All these official data show that a minimum wage earner cannot buy as much food as in January 2022, despite the 29 percent increase.
Because food prices have risen much more.
Minimum wage earners can now buy much less food, despite the hikes.
In January 2021, we equalize the minimum wage and the food price index to 100.
This means the following: The minimum wage is 100 liras and the price of the food basket is 100 liras.
Although the minimum wage remains the same throughout the year, the price of the same food basket keeps rising.
In December 2021, the minimum wage is still 100 liras, but the price of the same food basket is 141 liras.
In January 2022, the minimum wage rises to 151 liras.
However, the food basket was 157 liras this time.
In May 2022, the minimum wage is still 151 TL, but the food basket is now 205 TL.
In July 2022, the minimum wage rises to 195 liras.
But the price of the food basket was 205 liras in May.
This food basket will include the increases in June and July, while the minimum wage will remain the same.
In other words, despite all the increases, the food that could be bought with the minimum wage in January 2021 is less in July 2022.
Minimum wage: 393 liters of gasoline on 1 January 2021, 329 liters on 1 January 2022 and 202 liters on 1 July 2022.
Fuel prices make it clearer how the purchasing power of the minimum wage has fallen.

Accordingly, while 393 liters of gasoline could be purchased with the monthly net minimum wage on January 1, 2021, this amount decreased to 329 liters on January 1, 2022 and 202 liters on July 1, 2022.
In the same period, the minimum wage increased from 2,826 liras to 5,500 liras.

There is a similar situation in diesel. On January 1, 2021, 428 liters of diesel was purchased with the minimum wage, while this amount dropped to 333 liters on January 1, 2022 and 206 liters on July 1, 2022.

The amount of change in LPG was as follows: 696 liters of LPG could be purchased with the minimum wage on January 1, 2021, 470 liters on January 1, 2022 and 460 liters on July 1, 2022. Between January 1, 2022 and July 1, 2022, when we look at the amount of fuel that can be purchased with one month's minimum wage, it becomes clear how the purchasing power has decreased.
Despite the 29 percent increase, as of July 1, the minimum wage can only buy as much gasoline as on May 13.
The minimum wage increased by 29 percent compared to January 1, 2022.
However, between January 1 and July 2022, the amount of gasoline and diesel fuel that could be purchased with the minimum wage decreased by 37 percent and 38 percent, respectively.
On the other hand, despite the increase, the minimum wage remained below the hunger limit.

According to the results of the TÜRK-İŞ survey for June 2022; The monthly food expenditure amount (hunger limit) that a family of four should make in order to have a healthy, balanced and adequate diet is 6 thousand 391 TL; The total amount of food expenditure and other compulsory monthly expenses for clothing, housing (rent, electricity, water, fuel), transportation, education, health and similar needs (poverty line) increased to 20 thousand 818 TL.
Meanwhile, all calculations, except for fuel oil, are based on the May index of TURKSTAT.
Therefore, when June inflation is announced, the difference should be added.
Despite the increase in the minimum wage, if fuel and food prices increase in the July-December period, purchasing power will start to fall again.

The eighth Georgian-Turkish-Azerbaijani Defense Ministers' Meeting was held in the Tsinandali region of Telavi, Georgia.

Stating that they held an important meeting hosted by Georgian Defense Minister Burchuladze, whom he addressed as "my dear brother", Akar said: "I believe that the meeting we held in Georgia, an important country in the Caucasus, will provide important benefits for our countries and our armed forces.

In addition, we looked at the events from a broad perspective, especially Georgia, Azerbaijan and Turkey, and evaluated what can be done for the peace, stability and future of the region."

Pointing out the importance of the geography of the three countries, Akar said, "It has a vital importance in terms of the operation of important energy resources such as oil and natural gas and their transportation to other parts of the world.
Therefore, the peace and stability of this region is important not only for us but also for all countries in the region."

Reminding that the Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in the Field of Defense, which determines the principles and principles of joint cooperation of Georgia, Turkey and Azerbaijan in the field of defense, was signed last year, Akar continued as follows: "This memorandum of understanding makes our work extremely easy.
We have made significant progress, especially in the field of defense and security.

We are pleased that relations between the three countries are developing day by day.

2019-nCoV infection, many associated with travel from Wuhan, is being reported in an increasing number of international locations, including the United States.
The United States reported the first confirmed case of human-to-human spread of this virus on January 30, 2020.
Corona viruses are a large family of viruses that are common in many different animal species, including camels, cattle, cats and bats.
Rarely, animal coronaviruses can infect humans and then spread between humans. 2019-nCoV is a betacoronavirus and, like MERS and SARS, all have bat origins.

Risk Assessment.

Earth Friendly STEM+A Project Raises Earth Friendly New Generations

The "Earth Friendly STEM+A" eTwinning project prepares children for the 21st century by bringing together 22 teachers from 9 countries and 330 children between the ages of 4 and 6 with an eco-friendly approach.

The "Earth Friendly STEM+A" project, designed and implemented by Sibel Furtana and Esra Gültekin, teachers working in different schools in Mersin, brought together twenty-two preschool teachers and 330 students between the ages of 4 and 6 from Turkey, Spain, Slovakia, Romania, Poland, Portugal, Greece, Bulgaria and North Macedonia with an innovative approach.
The young students in the project were supported with a fun learning environment with the STEM+A education model and enjoyed learning with an eco-friendly approach.
STEM+A education aims to develop students' 21st century skills.
The STEM+A education model is an acronym that stands for STEM, Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics.

STEM applications, which are an interdisciplinary approach, are seen as a necessity of the rapidly changing and transforming information age in terms of enabling students to follow scientific and technological developments from an early age and to have basic science and engineering knowledge.
STEM applications for preschool students increase students' sense of curiosity and improve their ability to recognize, examine and explore their environment.
With this model, students learn by doing, experiencing and discovering, not by rote.
In the STEM+A model, art and design are also involved.

With STEM+A education, students have the opportunity to develop skills such as problem solving, asking questions, analyzing, researching, critical thinking and being a group by communicating effectively.
In this system, activities are project-based and multifaceted.
The aim of this system is to keep children's sense of curiosity alive so that they can investigate and question the events around them and develop appropriate solutions.

In addition, the main theme of the project, climate change, environmental education and recycling, is integrated with STEM+A to raise students' awareness, especially by using nature and nature materials.

Teacher Sibel Furtana, one of the designers of the project, stated that they created the EARTH FRIENDLY STEM+A project in order to contribute to the raising of environmentally and nature-friendly individuals on the use of natural resources, climate change, environmental education and recycling.

Stating that raising environment, nature and climate-conscious individuals within the scope of the United Nations Development Goals is of great importance for our world and future generations, Furtana stated that the project aims to contribute to the raising of environment - nature-friendly individuals on climate change and the use of natural resources, as well as to create behavioral change by enabling them to establish a relationship between 21st century skills and STEM, nature and environment.
The project was recognized as exemplary by the Mersin Directorate of National Education.

Furtana said that awareness-raising activities in the triangle of teachers, students and parents played an important role in the creation of the project, thus ensuring that parents also support students' learning processes.

He also emphasized that with the support of Mersin University Faculty of Engineering / Department of Environmental Technology and the Chamber of Environmental Engineers, they organized teacher, student and parent trainings on "The Impact of Environmental Pollution on Climate Change, Waste Management and Zero Waste", and as a result of the analysis, they observed that there was a significant difference in the knowledge and equipment of teachers, students and parents on waste separation, zero waste, environmental education and climate change.

He added that the fact that most of the activities were in nature and that children touched and examined soil, sand and different natural materials excited the children and positively supported their learning process.

Within the scope of the project, especially "World Water Day", "World Soil Day", "Energy, Water Saving Week" and "Forestry Week" activities were participated and collaborative and joint product outputs were also obtained.

In line with these results, the EARTH FRIENDLY STEM+A project was selected as one of the "Good Examples" among the projects implemented by Mersin Provincial Directorate of National Education in the 2021-2022 academic year and published in the R&D Bulletin.

Birkan BULUT Ankara.

In the Gebze-Orhangazi-Izmir Motorway, which was built with the Build-Operate-Transfer model, the company has not paid 568 million TL in usage fees for 9 years, despite paying over 1 billion 750 million as a vehicle passage guarantee for the first half of 2020.
The Gebze-Orhangazi-Izmir Motorway, including the Osmangazi Bridge, was one of the public-private partnership (PPP) projects that drew reaction with billions of lira in guarantee payments.
Undertaken by Otoyol Yatırım AŞ (Nurol, Özaltın, Makyol, Astaldi, Yüksel and Göçay), Osmangazi Bridge was opened in 2016 and all stages were opened last year.
Due to the fact that vehicle passage remained below the guarantee, a guarantee payment of 2.6 billion TL was made in 2019 and 1 billion 750-800 million TL in the first half of 2020.
DEBT IS ALSO GUARANTEED.
In PPP projects, in addition to the revenues of the companies, the Treasury also provided guarantees for the debts they borrowed from banks.
Due to the payment commitments made by the Treasury in mega projects, the total amount of debt rose to $17.2 billion this year.
The Gebze-Orhangazi-Izmir Motorway ranks first among the projects that the Treasury is committed to pay, with a loan of USD 4.9 billion.
HE TAKES BILLIONS OF DOLLARS, BUT CAN'T SPARE 568 MILLION LIRA!
However, it was revealed that the state failed to collect a total of 568 million TL in usage fees in 9 years in this project, which received millions of dollars in revenue guarantees until 2035.

According to the 2019 Audit Report of the General Directorate of Highways of the Court of Accounts, it was found that the usage fee that the company in charge had to pay for the immovables whose expropriation cost was covered by the administration in the Gebze-Orhangazi-İzmir (including Izmit Bay Crossing and connection roads) Motorway project was not collected.
HE WAS SUPPOSED TO PAY 5 THOUSAND TL PER PARCEL.

According to Article 26 of the administrative specifications, it was stated that the expropriation cost up to 400 million TL would be paid by the company in charge, the expropriation cost above this amount would be covered by the administration, and the company in charge would be obliged to pay the usage fee for the immovables whose expropriation cost was covered by the administration for the duration of the contract from the date of delivery to the administration.
The price of each parcel for 2010, the year the contract was signed, was set at 5 thousand TL excluding VAT.

The Court of Accounts auditors noted that 2 billion 453 million 446 thousand TL was paid within the scope of the work and that 400 million of this amount was covered by the company in charge in accordance with the administrative specifications and contract provisions.
However, it was determined that 568 million 151 thousand TL should have been collected from 2010 until the end of 2019.
With the law that entered into force in 2011, it was stipulated that no usage fee would be charged for works carried out within the scope of Law No. 3996.
The General Directorate of Highways argued that according to the contract, the company was obliged to comply with changes in the legislation and that charging a usage fee was against the law.

The Court of Accounts Auditors reminded that it was stipulated that no usage fee would be charged for works carried out within the scope of Law No. 3996, but this tender was awarded in 2009 and the contract was signed in 2010.

Drawing attention to the principle of non-retroactivity of laws, the auditors said, "The fact that the company is obliged to comply with the legislative change or court decision does not mean that it will no longer pay the usage fee that it is obliged to pay in accordance with the implementation agreement."

Competition Authority warns of "distance" for chain markets 01.04.2023

In the Competition Authority's "Final Report on Turkey's Fast Moving Consumer Goods Retailing Sector Review", it was stated that some regulations should be implemented to prevent the abuse of buyer power in the sector.

In this framework, some suggestions regarding the provisions that should be included in the "Draft Law Proposal Amending the Law on the Regulation of Retail Trade" are listed as follows "Regarding unfair commercial practices in the draft law, it is considered that payment terms exceeding 30 days in terms of perishable agricultural products and food products, payment terms exceeding 60 days in terms of other agricultural products and food products, cancellation notices made in a short time in perishable foods, unilateral contract changes of the buyer, transfer of the risk of lost and damaged goods to the supplier should be prohibited.

Within the scope of the same regulation, there is a need for a regulation that prohibits the return of unsold products, the payment of listing, shelf and stock costs by the supplier, the payment of the supplier for promotion, marketing and advertising, or that retailers may charge a fee in these matters only if there is a contract between the parties in this respect."

In the report, the establishment of an independent unit for the monitoring and supervision of these regulations was requested and the following statements were used: "The unit in question should be structured in a task-specific manner, have the authority to conduct complaints or ex officio inspections, have the authority to conduct unannounced inspections, request information, impose fines, and directly terminate the violation.

It is considered that the fines to be imposed to prevent unfair commercial practices should be of a deterrent nature, and in order to ensure deterrence, the administrative fine should be imposed on the turnover of the undertaking and there should be the possibility of an increase in the penalty in case of repetition."

The report pointed out that the linking of new store opening permits of chain supermarkets to population criteria may have some anti-competitive effects, and therefore it would be appropriate not to implement this regulation.

Regarding the distance requirement for chain stores, the report stated the following "With regard to store openings, it is considered that retailers within the same economic integrity may be prohibited from opening a second branch within a distance to be determined and these undertakings may be prevented from making a takeover transaction within the same distance.
As a matter of fact, chain stores belonging to the same group can be seen in very close proximity to each other in certain regions, which may prevent the entry of a new retailer in that region.
Therefore, we are of the opinion that the relevant regulation will have positive competitive effects in the market."

The report pointed out that some regulations can be made regarding some practices that may have a negative impact on the competitive structure of the sector or mislead consumers in the retailing of fast-moving consumer goods.

The report emphasized that it should be ensured that the product is available in the store during the period when it is announced to be discounted (through traditional media, social media or other announcements and advertisements) and that the product should be sold at the announced discounted price during this period, "Consumers often raised similar issues in their complaints and stated that the products announced to be discounted could not be found in retailers.
It is considered that this regulation will be beneficial for the protection of both consumers and competition."

In the report, it was stated that it was evaluated that the agreements made for suppliers to produce specially packaged products for a single chain market should be prevented, and it was noted that "In this context, it can be seen that a certain size of the products, different from the known or standard packaging, can be produced exclusively for only one retailer.
These practices are becoming widespread in the sector.
These agreements are likely to adversely affect competition and may lead to various illusions among consumers.

Regardless of whether such weight-packaging-size differences can be easily perceived by the consumer or not, it is considered that the production of a certain packaging specific to only one retailer can be prohibited by a regulation."

Yoruk women have been producing hand-woven carpets for 5 centuries

İpek YAVAŞ/AYVACIK (Çanakkale), (DHA)- In Çamkalabak village of Ayvacık district of ÇANAKKALE, Yoruk women are trying to keep alive the 500-year-old hand-woven carpet weaving from the Ottoman Empire, which is very laborious to produce and whose colors do not fade because root dye is used.
Yörük women living in Çamkalabak village of Ayvacık district struggle to keep the hand-woven carpets, which are about to be forgotten, alive.
Yoruk women, who obtain wool from the fleece on the backs of sheep, complain that there is not as much demand for the hand-woven carpets they make with a lot of effort.
They state that the carpets woven to order are mostly placed in the dowries of young girls during this period.
Ayşe Çarıksız (48) from Çamkabalalk village, who stated that she learned hand-woven carpet weaving at the age of 10, said, "We are trained from the core in carpet weaving.
I started carpet weaving in the 4th grade of primary school.
We learned from our grandmothers and mothers.
There used to be a lot of carpet weaving.
Now carpet weaving is not practiced as it used to be.
I have been carpet weaving for 38 years.
We make ornaments and sell the products we produce.
Our own people are buying these.
There was an incredible demand beforehand.
We could sell every week.
It was sold every week in Ayvacık.
Now there is no space," he said.
'LOTS OF LABOR' Describing the production process of hand-woven carpets, Çarıksız said, "We make our carpets from root dye.
Our carpets never come out of dye.
No matter how much you wash it.
We get wool from the fleece from the backs of sheep.
We wash the fleece in the stream.
Then we dry it.
We clean the inside.
Then we send it to the card, make a ridge, spin it on the spinning wheel.
We'll make a ball again.
We'll give it to paint.
When the dye is ready, we start weaving.
It would be a lot of work," he said.
Hicran Demir (38), one of the village women, stated that the demand for hand-woven carpets has decreased and said, "Before, our woven carpets were sold.
It's not for sale now.
It decorates the walls.
We use these woven carpets and rugs for everything.
Now there are no more people coming to our village.
We weave to order.
We embroider the motifs we learned from our grandmothers and mothers on carpets.
We sell the carpets we can sell.
We prepare the carpets we cannot sell as dowry for young girls."

'I hope our carpets will be in demand again' Sabır Çetin, who stated that they learned the production of hand-woven carpets as a child, said, "I learned carpet weaving from my elders when I was 8-9 years old.
There used to be a lot of demand for our carpets.
It was our livelihood.
Our only profession is carpet weaving and animal husbandry.
And there are no more bum-sweepers.
Nowadays this carpet business is over.
This profession is no longer preferred.
When we get old, we won't be able to do it anymore. 2 people can produce a carpet in 30 days.
Before, we used to weave carpets day and night.
Now, since it is not preferred, it is included in dowries.
So we have to go to work.
No one buys, no one sells.
We don't know any other profession.
I hope our carpets will be in demand again."

According to Professor Jean-Jacques Muyembe Tamfum, who helped discover the Ebola virus in 1976 and has since researched new pathogens emerging in Africa, humanity is facing an unknown number of new and potentially deadly viruses emerging from Africa's tropical rainforests.
Speaking to CNN International, Tamfum said, "We are now in a world where new pathogens will emerge.
People should be ready for more than just a new type of coronavirus pandemic."

As a young researcher in the 1970s, Muyembe sent blood samples to laboratories in Belgium and the United States to determine the origin of a mysterious disease that killed about 88 percent of patients.
The disease, then known as Zaire, was later renamed "Ebola".
The detection of Ebola is based on a chain linking the remotest parts of Africa's rainforests to high-tech laboratories in the West.
"I THINK THERE WILL BE WORSE CONSEQUENCES THAN THE NEW TYPE OF CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC" Now the West is waiting to hear from African scientists in Congo and elsewhere to warn of future disease.
One of these researchers, Muyembe, warned that many more zoonotic diseases (jumping from animals to humans) are coming.

The novel coronavirus, yellow fever, various types of influenza, rabies, AIDS, brucellosis and Lyme disease are all diseases that are usually transmitted from animals to humans via a vector, such as a rodent or insect.
HIV jumped from a chimpanzee species to humans and became a worldwide epidemic.
Covid-19 is thought to have originated in China, possibly in bats.
However, Muyembe said he thinks future outbreaks will cause worse consequences than the new type of coronavirus pandemic.
3-4 POTENTIALLY DANGEROUS VIRUSES ARE DISCOVERED EVERY YEAR.
Since the discovery of yellow fever in 1901, the first disease identified as transmitted from animal to human, researchers have found at least 200 other viruses known to cause disease in humans.

According to research by Mark Woolhouse, professor of infectious disease epidemiology at the University of Edinburgh, three to four new strains of viruses are discovered each year that can cause epidemics in humans.
The majority of these viruses come from animals.
A CONSEQUENCE OF ECOLOGICAL DESTRUCTION AND WILDLIFE TRADE.
Scientists say the rising number of viruses is largely the result of ecological destruction and the wildlife trade.
As the habitats of large animals are destroyed, the mice, bats and insects that prey on them continue to survive.
As their habitats become closer to humans, the diseases they have jump to humans and cause new outbreaks.
EBOLA OUTBREAK EMERGED IN DEFORESTED AREAS.

Experts believe the cause of widespread Ebola outbreaks in Africa is a massive human assault on rainforests. According to a 2017 study, using satellite data, researchers found that 25 of the 27 Ebola outbreaks along rainforest borders in Central and West Africa between 2001 and 2014 started in areas that had experienced deforestation about two years earlier.
A CALL TO INVESTORS AND POLICYMAKERS FOR EARLY DETECTION OF VIRUSES.

"The emergence of a new virus in Africa means it will affect the whole world," said Muyambe, an employee of the Democratic Republic of Congo's national medical research organization at INRB, which is funded by grants from Japan, the United States, the World Health Organization (WHO), the European Union and other international donors, including NGOs, foundations and academic institutions.
But if this virus is detected early, the world will have the opportunity to develop new strategies against the disease."
Muyambe also emphasized the importance of governments and organizations investing in science laboratories for early detection of viruses.
On the other hand, Muyambe noted that dozens of new coronaviruses have been discovered in bats over the years, but politicians and investors ignored them until one threatened all of humanity.

Current In Moldova, A Pro-Russian Region Welcomes Ukrainian Refugees
In Congaz, a small village in Moldova's Gagauzia autonomous region, a statue of former Soviet leader Lenin watches over a reception center for Ukrainian refugees.
I learned only good things about Lenin: that he was an important leader, that he was a hard-working man like us.
So I don't mind standing next to Lenin's statue," Margarita, who came from Odessa and now lives on Lenin Street in the village, told Al Jazeera.

A few weeks ago, Margarita and her nine-year-old son left Tiraspol, the self-proclaimed capital of Moldova's pro-Russian breakaway region of Transnistria, for a city that seems to be involved in the Ukrainian war.
followed.
At the time, Russian officials said they were seeking easier access to Transnistria, where Moscow's military already had a presence, in order to seize more of Ukraine.
"If something had happened only here, in Gagauzia, we would have gone further," Margarita said, "but now we feel safe here, quiet, like at home in Odessa.
And it helps everyone here to speak Russian."
Gagauzia is the poorest region of Moldova, inhabited by a Russian-speaking Turkish minority settled during the Ottoman period.
Now the European Union, Russia and Turkey are vying for influence in the region.
Like everyone in Moldova, the Ukrainian war took the people of Gagauzia, just 200 km (124 miles) from Odessa, by surprise.
The office of George Sari, deputy mayor of Komrat, the capital of Gagauzia, is decorated with Turkish flags and a Turkish eye-shaped amulet.
He's talking to Al Jazeera and his phone rings.
"Sorry, I have to answer, this is a call from Turkey," he said.
Ankara has made significant investments in Gagauzia's infrastructure, hospitals and schools.
According to Sari, Turkey has donated significant amounts of aid to host Ukrainian refugees here.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan visited Gagauzia in 2020 and opened a new consulate in Comrat.
After World War I, Gagauzia became part of Romania, a period when many in this region were persecuted.

For this reason, Gagauzians generally do not like Romanians, do not learn Romanian and do not accept reunification. In 1940, along with Moldova, Gagauzia was annexed by the Soviet Union following an ultimatum given to Romania by then Soviet leader Joseph Stalin.

Like the breakaway region of Transnistria, Gagauzia declared independence in 1990 when the Soviet Union dissolved. In 1994 it was reintegrated into Moldova and has been an autonomous region ever since.
Responding to Chisinau, it has its own police force, regional laws and unique economic ties with Russia, the EU and Turkey.
About 150,000 people live here, mostly Gagauz, with some Bulgarians, Russians and Ukrainians.
The Gagauz make up five percent of Moldova's population.
They are Orthodox Christians and speak primarily Russian, but also Gagauzian, the language closest to Turkish.
The national language of Moldova is Romanian.

The Gagauzian language was not taught properly when the region was part of Romania, so the main goal of the authorities and Turkey is to revive the local dialect and give it more importance in schools where Russian is overwhelmingly spoken.
Meanwhile, the EU is investing in the region's infrastructure through its development bank.
Gagauzia's Governor Irina Vlah believes in balancing the competing interests of Brussels, Moscow and Ankara.
The region's biggest challenge is its distrust of Chisinau, especially since the pro-European, democratic President Maia Sandu took office in 2020.
"The government in Chisinau is against our people.
Because we don't speak Romanian, they think we are Russian," says Nikolai, a native of Komrat.

UK and EU reach new agreement on Northern Ireland Protocol

British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak announced that the European Union (EU) and the UK have reached a new agreement on the Northern Ireland Protocol, which regulates trade between Northern Ireland and EU member Ireland after Brexit, and that the protocol will now be known as the Windsor Framework.
The UK and the EU have reached a new agreement on the Northern Ireland Protocol, which is part of the Brexit deal and regulates trade between Northern Ireland, part of the UK, and EU member Ireland.
British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen held a joint press conference after their meeting in Windsor, England.

In a statement, Sunak announced that the European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on the Northern Ireland Protocol, which sets the trade rules for Northern Ireland after Brexit, and that the protocol will now be known as the Windsor Framework.

Stating that the new agreement ensures a smooth flow of trade across the whole of the UK, Sunak said that Northern Ireland retains its place in the union and Northern Ireland's sovereignty is secured.

Describing the agreement as a "new chapter" in the UK's relations with the EU, Sunak said it would preserve the "delicate balance" in the 1998 Belfast Agreement (Good Friday Agreement) that protects the "aspirations and identity" of all people in Northern Ireland and "ends uncertainty" for people in Northern Ireland.

Stating that they have taken three big steps with the agreement, Sunak stated that the first step will be "a smooth flow of trade within the UK" where goods are separated into green lane and red lane.
"We have eliminated any sense of a border in the Irish Sea," said Sunak, explaining that with the green lane, laborious customs bureaucracy will be shelved.
In the second step of the agreement, medicines approved for use by the UK health regulator will automatically be available for sale in Northern Ireland, Sunak said.

"This creates a clear process whereby the democratically elected assembly can put the emergency brake on changes affecting EU goods and everyday life," he said, referring to the third step taken by the agreement, which allows the Northern Ireland assembly to not only have a say on legislation but also to stop its implementation in Northern Ireland.
He added that the UK government would have a veto on the issue, which he said gave "strong new protection" to the Belfast Agreement that helped end decades of conflict in Northern Ireland.

"I also remember that we were honest with each other about the difficulties in our bilateral relationship, and it was vital to put it on the right footing," von der Leyen said, adding that she and Prime Minister Sunak had fulfilled the "important commitment" they made a few months ago.
Stating that they had reached an agreement in principle on the Windsor Framework, von der Leyen described the agreement as a "new page" for UK-EU relations.
"We have agreed on strong measures to protect the integrity of the EU's single market," Von der Leyen said.
Stating that the Windsor Framework has benefited people in Northern Ireland, von der Leyen explained that it will make EU-UK relations stronger.
Northern Ireland Protocol.

Golden recommendations for candidates who will take YKS Başkent University Faculty of Arts and Sciences, Department of Psychology Faculty Member Assoc. Prof. Dr. Okan Cem Çırakoğlu made suggestions for candidates who will take the Higher Education Institutions Examination (YKS) to cope with stress.

Çırakoğlu asked each candidate to do something that will make them feel comfortable and happy the day before the exam and suggested that candidates do breathing exercises to cope with stress during the exam.

Assoc. Prof. Dr. Okan Cem Çırakoğlu said that there is a serious perception of competition among the candidates who will enter the YKS and that disaster scenarios are activated in the minds of many people because the evaluation is indexed to the exam.

Çırakoğlu, who asked the candidates to do activities to relax themselves before the exam in order to get rid of disaster scenarios such as 'what if I forget something on the way to the exam, if I get sick', pointed out that since the structure of each person is different from each other, a single prescription cannot be offered for relaxation.
"Of course, we do not want them to engage in some risky behaviors.

For example, he wants to go and have fun with his friends before the exam, he may go out in the mountains and there are always accidents, or he may eat in an unfamiliar place and his stomach is sensitive.
It is not possible to take precautions for each and every one of these, but there is no need to take such obvious risks.
I think it would be good for people to engage in some work where they can feel comfortable, feel happy, control and regulate their anxiety."

'ARE MY DISASTER SCENARIOS REALISTIC?' Stating that in order to control anxiety, we must first find out what makes us anxious, Çırakoğlu pointed out that there may be some thoughts that trigger test anxiety.
Çırakoğlu said, "Your fellow candidates should ask, 'What are my disaster scenarios?
What's scaring me?
and are these things I'm feeling actually realistic?
So are there really hints that this could happen or is it just my misperception?'
"We would like them to review themselves," he said.

Çırakoğlu underlined that disaster scenarios in the mind are usually not very suitable for reality and pointed out that candidates who question the reality of what goes through their minds can reduce their anxiety and increase their sense of control.

"DO NOT TRY RISKY THINGS BEFORE THE EXAM" Çırakoğlu stated that candidates can relax themselves before the exam without disrupting the integrity of their lives, for example, they can get together with their friends, play games, listen to music, watch a movie they have been wanting for a long time, "So there is no single right way for people.
There is an old saying; 'you don't change horses while crossing a stream'.
Two days before the exam, people know what will make them happy, what will relax them, instead of trying too risky things.
We would like them to trust them and put them into practice."
'BE A BRAVE FAMILY, SUPPORT THE CHILD' Çırakoğlu also made suggestions for families whose children will take the exam and asked parents to be a 'brave family'.

Noting that families under the pressure of the perception of the good life and social values may overlook the needs of their children, Çırakoğlu said, "They should allow their children to live the way they really want.
Let them see their needs in that sense.
They may refrain from being critical of them for a while.
At this stage, they should give more emotional support to their children."

Office rents are expected to bottom out.

According to the report, the demand for office investments is expected to gradually increase with the increasing number of properties for immediate sale, and the environment in favor of tenants is expected to continue in the medium term, with prices approaching buyer expectations.

Accordingly, while total leasing transactions were almost at the same level of 278,828 square meters in 2019 compared to the previous year, transactions are expected to increase further in the coming period.

In the report, it was stated that the office supply increased in parallel with the existing development projects, albeit at a lower rate, and that the overall office supply in Istanbul remained at the same level of 6.46 million square meters, while new building permits decreased.

In the fourth quarter, 66.78 percent of the deals on a square meter basis increased on the Anatolian side, almost twice as much as in the previous quarter, while office rents were highest in Istanbul Levent with 170 liras per square meter.

With primary rents expected to bottom out in the short term, the report emphasized that primary yields are also expected to increase in the short and medium term with the increasing number of properties for immediate sale.

Tourism professionals evaluated the future of the sector

Firuz Bağlıkaya, President of the Association of Turkish Travel Agencies (TÜRSAB), stated that in a well-planned process, Turkey will heal its wounds much faster than other countries with its reassuring image.

In his speech at the One Istanbul Series events held via video conference, Bağlıkaya stated that during the coronavirus process, they took action not to collect member fees and to allow agencies to remain closed.

Stating that one of the biggest problems of travel agencies is the refund of customers' early booking money, Bağlıkaya said, "We had a request for a regulation that travel agencies, like airlines, should make refunds after life returns to normal" or "customers should reschedule their holidays".
We tried hard but we failed.
Travel agencies had to pay the money they could not collect to customers."

Baglıkaya emphasized that if there is hesitation about going on vacation, that vacation will not be taken and continued his words as follows: "We have serious concerns about when people's motivation to take a vacation will be restored. 2020 will be recorded as a lost year in our long-term records.
We are seeking solutions in good faith, but if it conflicts with the natural flow of the process, we may experience processes that are difficult to compensate for.
If the virus climbs upwards again, 2021 could also be at risk.
Spring is here and our business motivation is very high, but we are in a period when we need to be cautious."
"Will we accept from abroad?"

Bağlıkaya stated that it is a good scenario for tourism professionals that domestic tourists will be added in July and August, foreign tourists will be added in September and October, and hotels will reach 30 percent-50 percent occupancy during these periods, and noted the following: "If this happens, we will be very comfortable in 2021.
Will we accept tourists from abroad?
Will our country accept tourists from Russia, where there are 10,000 cases a day?
We are getting ready, but are we going to risk a very well-managed process in this sense?
We don't know any of this.
In a well-planned process, Turkey, with its already reassuring image, will heal its wounds much more quickly than other countries.
As long as we don't make mistakes.
If we do not lose this advantageous position, the losses of 2020 can be compensated in 2021.
First we survive and then we survive so that we can continue these businesses.
In this respect, financial support is important."

Firuz Bağlıkaya pointed out that the infection of any tourist in Turkey carries the potential for propaganda against the country's tourism, and said, "We are already in the situation of 'you have an eyebrow over your eye' in Europe.
They immediately trash Turkey on social media.
They can even blame us for something that is not our fault.
That's all I'm worried about.
So we need to be very careful."

"We will continue to implement the open buffet and all-inclusive system" Müberra Eresin, President of the Hotel Association of Turkey (TÜROB), stated that tourism activities have stopped in Turkey as in the whole world due to the coronavirus.

Eresin said that they have provided training to more than 600 hotel employees all around Turkey, and due to the high demand, they will continue the training this week and next week, and as a result, they will have provided training and certificates to more than 2 thousand hotel employees.

Stating that income and expense management is important due to the costs that will increase after the pandemic and that they have organized trainings on this issue, Eresin said that the work on the hygiene certificate of accommodation and food and beverage facilities has been going on for 1.5 months.

Stating that it is known that the tourism sector will not be able to overcome this process as easily as other sectors, Eresin said, "We are waiting for the support of the government so that the support, postponements and cancellations given to us can be made until January 2021."

Eresin pointed out that the date when the sector will control its cash flow again and bring it to proper levels will be in the first months of next year at best, and said, "This should not be ignored in the work to be done.

This will not continue.
After the measures are completed, their presentation and implementation may change, but we will continue with both practices."

"We have certification and operational concerns" Oya Narin, President of the Turkish Tourism Investors Association (TTYD), said that tourism is a capital-intensive sector, with nearly 12 thousand enterprises and investments of over 100 billion dollars.

Narin explained that the pandemic period must be overcome in order for the financial structure of the sector to settle into a system again, and reminded that the government has taken steps to provide some support.

Stating that it was the end of March when these steps were taken, Narin said, "According to our plans at the end of March, we thought that the sector would slowly open up around May and that we would gain momentum in June.

There is a trend towards the end of June, July.
We have certification and operational concerns.
There is also a financial dimension.
We need a different approach in the new period."

Narin said that if there is movement both domestically and from abroad from July onwards, they foresee that this year will be closed with an income of around 10 billion dollars at best, adding that the southern regions are more fortunate, while they estimate that Istanbul will have a spring in the spring of 2021.
