Can you buy land in the Metaverse?
Real estate is often seen as the most popular investment instrument in Turkey as it is in the world.

The fact that land plots offered for sale on the virtual universe metaverse have recently found buyers for thousands of dollars, and have even been put up for sale on Sahibinden, one of Turkey's major e-commerce sites, indicates that the real estate sector has entered the agenda of investors in the virtual environment.

The metaverse, which has become the new favorite not only of the technology world but also of investors with the "Meta" transformation of the social network Facebook, is not likely to limit its borders to a few sectors.
Among these sectors, the real estate sector has already taken its place among those winking at the metaverse.

Baki Budakoğlu, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Denge Valuation, which has been operating in the real estate and valuation sector since 2005, stated that an investor he met on social media recently mentioned that the value of the parcel right next to the metaverse parcel, which he had recently bought for 13 thousand dollars, had reached 1 million dollars and that he started to study his lesson by saying 'A new door has opened for us'.
"VALUE DEPENDS ON 4 FACTORS"

Stating that in order to be able to talk about value determination, value must first be formed, Budakoğlu stated that the value of any tangible or intangible item is not formed only by the existence of those things; 4 factors such as 'Usefulness', 'Scarcity', 'Desire' and 'Effective Purchasing Power' are needed for the formation of value.
Budakoğlu said, "This means that in the Metaverse, in order for land or any other real estate to have real value, it must be used or leased to provide benefits.
In addition to being limited to a certain amount, the presence of a willing buyer with sufficient purchasing power is also a necessity in terms of the formation of value."
"THERE IS NO SHORTAGE OF LAND IN METAVERSE"

Baki Budakoğlu said that if the land in question was not in the metaverse but in the physical real world; parameters such as 'Development Area', 'Precedent Number of Floors', 'Structuring Conditions', 'Location', 'Transportation Facilities' would be taken into consideration and continued as follows: "When evaluating the land, while developing the project on the one hand, on the other hand, we would determine the value based on the realized or demanded sales prices of the lands with the same zoning construction conditions and similar location.
In the Metaverse, however, there is a limitlessness because it is a virtual platform.
Universes that are currently at the forefront include The Sandbox, Axie Infinity, Decentraland, Our, etc.

These universes are designed independently of each other; for example, one is made up of approximately 90,000 plots of land, while another is designed to mirror the entire world and consists of 1.6 million plots of land.

You know how it is said in some speeches that there is no more land on the Bosphorus in Istanbul, well, this is only true for one of those virtual universes, because in an application, the map of Istanbul can be designed and put up for sale again, and then the investor who wants it will have the chance to buy it.
Naturally, it seems unrealistic to talk about a scarcity factor across the Metaverse."

"Referring to the parameters encountered in attempts to purchase land in Metaverse, Baki Budakoğlu said: "In priority purchases, proximity to the Metaverse Center, accessibility, population density and being adjacent to or close to the real estate purchased by celebrities are recommended or preferred.
As can be seen, there are no restrictions for the development of the land such as housing, hotel, school, shopping mall or factory area.
Moreover, there is no regulatory or planning institution envisaged, since it is assumed that the investors in the virtual universe will decide on the housing to be built.

In other words, it is essential to make a joint decision on the platform, and it is thought that by recording the owner on the blockchain, its ownership will become public, that is, it will become public for everyone to claim."

"IT IS DIFFICULT TO MEET ON COMMON STAKEHOLDER" Pointing out that it is important how the real estate provides a benefit for the real estate to gain value in the Metaaverse, Budakoğlu said, "Of course, if the board consisting of the investors in that virtual universe and the officials of the institution designing the virtual universe will decide for what purposes the land will be used in any virtual universe subject to investment, it may not be enough for them to meet at a common point.
Because that point should also be the point where valid and correct decisions are taken in terms of the existence, development and sustainability of the virtual universe in question.

In other words, it will be necessary to determine the intended use and construction conditions of the parcels by contributing from the perspectives of many disciplines based on human psychology and social life, as well as urban planning, mapping engineering, architecture, civil engineering, management disciplines, otherwise there will be an unplanned construction that will not create synergy in terms of both commercial and social life.
Not to mention the silhouette and aesthetics.
Of course, another factor for a parcel to contain value, which is usefulness, that is, to produce benefit, will only be possible with a planned construction."
CLIMBING FLOORS IN THE VIRTUAL UNIVERSE!

Stating that a YouTuber can change the two-storey building he previously built on the land he invested in the virtual universe by selecting the three-storey one from the building symbols on the side of the screen, Budakoğlu said, "Thus, did he increase the value of his real estate?
Or did his choice reduce the value of his land instead of increasing its value?
Who knows already!"
He said.
Exemplary verdict!

In the lawsuit filed in Bursa regarding the death of Erkan Uraz, a worker who fell to his death from the 9th floor of the construction site where he was working, the court sentenced 3 defendants to 3 years and 4 months imprisonment each for 'conscious negligence', taking into account the fact that 2 separate deaths occurred in other constructions of the same company.
The court did not postpone the sentences of the defendants.

The incident occurred in December 2017 in 23 Nisan neighborhood of Bursa's central Nilüfer district. On the 9th floor of the 17-storey construction, Erkan Uraz, who was tying balcony bars, lost his balance and fell to the ground.
The seriously injured worker died in the hospital.
A lawsuit was filed against the owners of the construction company at Bursa 9th Criminal Court of First Instance for 'causing death by negligence' with a prison sentence of 2 to 15 years.
THE THIRD DEATH AT THE SAME COMPANY'S CONSTRUCTION SITE.
The defendants Muharrem G., Osman U. and Ümitcan T., who were present at the verdict hearing held at Bursa 9th Criminal Court of First Instance the previous day, did not accept the accusations.
Ercan Kılıç and Osman Orhan, lawyers for the family of the deceased worker, said: "Similar fatal incidents have occurred in the construction sites of the main employer before.
We know of 3 such fatal incidents that took place on different dates and were the subject of different lawsuits.
It has been established by expert reports that the defendants and the companies authorized by the defendants are gravely at fault.
These deaths continued due to the gross negligence and chain of negligence of the defendants and their companies.
This chain of negligence most recently cost the life of a young Erkan Uraz.
Unfortunately, the decisions of the courts in similar cases are not effective and deterrent for negligent employers, as they are usually in the form of 'suspended prison sentences or fines'.

For the sake of justice, we demand that the defendants, who are company officials, be punished at the upper limit within the scope of conscious negligence, not negligence, and that they be sentenced directly to imprisonment."
DEFENDANTS DENY THE CHARGES.
Court Judge Aynur Mutlu sentenced the defendants to 3 years and 4 months imprisonment each, taking into account 'the importance and value of the crime and the gravity of the defendants' negligence'.
The sentences were not suspended.
It is reported that if the Bursa Regional Court of Appeals upholds the verdict, the defendants will be imprisoned.
PRECEDENT DECISION FROM THE COURT.

Making a statement after the verdict, lawyers Ercan Kılıç and Osman Orhan stated that the verdict would be accurate, important and precedent-setting in terms of similar cases and said, "Courts usually impose suspended prison sentences or fines for the offense of causing death by negligence.
These are not effective and do not act as a deterrent.
If it had been effective and deterrent, there would not have been 3 fatal work accidents in a chain within the same company.
However, we believe that the court's decision will be a deterrent and effective.
The decision, which relieves the pain of the family to some extent, has revealed that the concept of conscious negligence should be taken into account in work accidents."

What is Mineral Water?
Mineral water is a natural drink extracted from underground sources.
It usually contains minerals such as sodium, magnesium, calcium and potassium.
These minerals are essential for many important functions in our bodies.
Health Benefits of Mineral Water.
Benefits for Digestive System Health.

Benefits for Urinary Tract Health.
Mineral water is also beneficial for urinary tract health.
The minerals in its content help prevent urinary tract infections.
It also prevents the formation of kidney stones.
Benefits for Bone Health.
Mineral water is an important source of bone health.
Its calcium content helps strengthen bones and prevent bone diseases such as osteoporosis.
Benefits for those who play sports.
Mineral water is very beneficial for the bodies of people who do sports.
It helps replace fluids lost during exercise.
In addition, the minerals it contains help muscles recover and strengthen faster.
Benefits for Skin Health.
Mineral water is also beneficial for skin health.
The minerals in its content increase the moisture level of the skin and help the skin look healthier and younger.
Stress Reducing Feature.
Mineral water is also known for its stress-reducing properties.

Mineral water should be consumed fresh and cold.

Side Effects of Mineral Water.

A total mental eclipse!...
We are one of the few Muslim countries that are practicing democracy - albeit blindly.
But what the hell!..
There is a life-and-death struggle in the country towards every election!

00:02 - Public institutions should pay attention to the difference between permanent and temporary disability reports
Can those with a periodic disability report use administrative leave after the end of the period?

Question: Hello, I am a civil servant working in the disabled staff, my report was for 5 years and its duration ended in November 2019, my institution did not refer me to renew it again, and I did not have the opportunity due to workload.
I am currently on administrative leave, I am a disabled person, but my report has expired.
When I want to enter the committee, they say that the committee will convene at the end of May at the earliest and that the validity of the reports that expire after 01.01.2020 continues.
Is my report valid?
Will I have problems with my institution in the future for the time I spent on administrative leave?
Answer: Within the scope of the measures taken to minimize the effects of the coronavirus outbreak, administrative leave has been implemented for public personnel.
Personnel working within the disabled quotas in public administrations are also considered to be on administrative leave within the scope of the Presidential Circular No. 2020/4.
Medical board reports based on disability are given in accordance with the provisions of the Regulation on Disability Assessment for Adults.
Pursuant to Article 11 of the Regulation, the report must be issued on a permanent or temporary basis and the validity period must be specified in the report.

In addition, a temporary report is issued in cases where the disability of the individual is likely to decrease over time with medication, surgical treatment and / or rehabilitation practices and the signs of the disease are not fully visible.
In reports issued for a period of time, if there is less than six months before the end of the period, the disabled person is given a new report upon request.
According to Article 12 of the Regulation, a report can be requested by the institution for any reason regarding the reports given for a period of time.

The Regulation entered into force on February 20, 2019 and according to Article 15 of the Regulation, the validity of the reports with the phrase "continuous", which were obtained in accordance with the legislation in force before this date, continues.
Temporary reports will remain valid until the expiry date.

On the other hand, a temporary disability report does not prevent employment within the disabled quotas in the public sector, and the expiration of the period does not result in the dismissal of the personnel.
However, in order to continue to benefit from disability-related rights, expired reports must be renewed.

It would be appropriate for institutions that employ personnel based on a temporary disability report to monitor the duration of the report, ask the personnel whose report has expired to renew their reports or request a new report from the relevant health institutions.
Disabled personnel whose report period has expired should be excluded from the quota and the quotas for the disabled should be redetermined.

As a result, it is both ethically and administratively problematic for the personnel employed in the public sector based on a temporary disability report to benefit from the right to administrative leave without renewing the report, even though they have the opportunity to renew the report within 6 months before the end of the report period, and we consider that those in this situation cannot benefit from the right to administrative leave.

Emphasizing that the failure to conclude the cases in the labor courts within a reasonable time leads to injustice, Balku said: "We say that delayed justice is not justice.

I retired. 4-5 months later I negotiated for a house.
My severance pay was half the cost of that house.
At the end of the case, we realized that the same apartment corresponds to approximately 10 percent of that house when we add the severance pay and interest.
Our other application is also interesting, we applied for 8 workers. 4 of them ended up in one court and the other 4 in another court.

There was a pregnancy, the child grew up, the judge's child started primary school.
We couldn't get the result.
" - "A case that can be completed in 4 months takes a very long time" Balku conveyed the victimizations experienced by his clients in reinstatement and overtime cases, and noted the following:

"There is a time limit set by law for reinstatement cases, a case that can be completed in 1 month at the local court, in 3 months at the higher court, in a total of 4 months, takes a very long time today.

There is neither the employer nor the worker's eagerness to return to work.
We think that the right to be tried within a reasonable time should be emphasized."
Expressing that they are happy that their application was justified, Balku said, "We were entitled to 17 thousand liras in compensation.

At the end of the day, as per standard procedure, the bank was counted and the officers on duty were shocked.
The 561 million rubles (about 8.3 million euros) in the bank's vault evaporated and were replaced with office supplies.
After recovering from the shock of the incident, the officers quickly informed the police.
What emerged as a result of the police investigations stunned those who heard it and marked the beginning of an escape story that would last 4 years.

Inessa Brandenburg, who was detained as a result of an operation carried out by Spanish police in September 2021, was recently extradited to Russia.

"Russian citizen Inessa Brandenburg was arrested in Spain under the supervision of Russian and Interpol police, handed over to Russian law enforcement officers at the airport," Russian Interior Ministry spokeswoman Irina Volk said.

3 New Test Facilities for National Fighter Aircraft
TAI announced on its Twitter account the three test centers to be built for the Lightning Test, RKA Measurement and EMI/EMC Test for the National Fighter Aircraft Project.
"With our MMU project, we are preparing to shape the aviation industry by bringing three major new test centers to our country with our national resources.
While producing our domestic and national products, we always dream of more for our country."
Test facilities are more important than one might think for a project as large as a fighter jet.
No matter how much simulation software is developed to build a system, that system must also be subjected to specified conditions in real life.
Relying on software for testing can lead to design flaws that the software cannot detect, causing huge material damage in the final trial.
With the embargoes, which have been implicitly applied for a few years and have recently become official, our country has been left alone in terms of test facilities.
Thus, Turkey started to establish the necessary facilities to meet its testing needs.
Considering the importance of the MMU project for our country, we have to face the fact that we cannot meet our test needs from abroad, especially in this period.

A Lightning Test Facility, an EMC/EMI (Electromagnetic Compatibility and Interference) Test Facility and a Near Field RKA (Radar Cross Section Area) Measurement Facility are being constructed for different test requirements of the MMU.
In fact, these facilities will meet the testing needs not only of the MMU, but also of other aviation projects in the future.

For example, when TAI or Baykar Makina is working on an Unmanned Combat Aircraft project and an RKA test is to be conducted, the RKA Measurement Facility used for the MMU can also be used for the Unmanned Combat Aircraft.
Lightning Test Facility.
The greatest dangers to aircraft do not always come from the enemy, and one of these non-human dangers is undoubtedly lightning.
Especially a machine with a price tag of tens of millions of dollars, such as a fighter jet, should be protected against lightning.
This facility will be used to test the MMU against lightning strikes.

The system that will create artificial lightning in the facility will also have the signature of Molekülas, which has provided consultancy services in the development of the pulsed power supply of Şahi 209, one of Turkey's electromagnetic cannon projects.
EMC/EMI Testing Facility.

This facility, about which not much information is available, will be used to simulate electrical power problems (AC failures, overloads, voltage drops...) for MMU and other aerospace products, and to test the magnetic and radioactive susceptibility of the platform.
Near Field RCS Measurement Facility.
Low Radar Cross Section (RCS), 5.
It is one of the sine qua non of the next generation MMU.
In order to achieve this, several studies are being carried out by TAI and other companies.

Some of these studies include the optimization of the structure of the aircraft (parallel curved fuselage and similar structural features that distort and reflect the shape of radar waves), radar absorbing materials and RKA Measurement Facility.
The RKA Measurement Facility will guide other studies in this area by making measurements and showing whether the method used gives the desired result.
The facility will also be able to meet the test requirements of other aerospace products (Cruise Missile, UCAV, Attack Helicopter...) where low RKA is important.
To sum it all up, looking at these facilities only from the MMU perspective would give us a narrow view of them.

Our new facilities, which will be more advanced than our existing facilities that serve the same function in terms of the technology required, will bring our Defense and Aviation sector to a new level.

Surah Nisa 136.
What are the Messages Given in the Verse?
Surah Nisa 136.

was revealed in
Surah Nisa, the fourth surah of the Qur'an, consists of 176 verses.
This Surah talks about women's rights and their legal status in general.
This surah takes its name from the word 'Nisa' meaning women.
Many verses of this Surah contain provisions and explanations about women.
In verse 136 of Surah al-Nisa, the subject of faith occupies a large place.
This verse mentions the importance of faith in God, the Prophet and the Scriptures.
Surah Nisa 136.
What are the Messages Given in the Verse?
Surah Nisa, one of the most important surahs of the Quran, contains important information for Muslims.
Verse 136 of this Surah deals with the conditions of faith.
Accordingly, the importance of believing in God, believing in the Prophets, believing in the Books, the angels and the Last Day is emphasized.
According to this verse, whoever does not believe in them will incur the wrath of Allah.
Surah Nisa 136.
What does the verse want to tell us?
In verse 136 of Surah Nisa, the importance of the conditions of faith necessary for Islam is emphasized.
Based on the conditions of faith, the necessity of belief in God, prophets, the Quran, angels and the hereafter is emphasized.
In this verse, it is emphasized that people should be based on the Book that has been sent to them so that they do not turn to false beliefs, Surah Nisa: 136.
Verse Arabic Reading Surah Nisa 136.
Turkish Reading of the Ayat.
Ya ayyuhallezine amenu, aminu billahi wa Rasulihi wa kitabillezi nezzala ala Rasulihi wa kitabillezi enzala min kabl.
And men yekfur billahi wa melaikatihi wa melaikatihi wa kutubihi wa rusulihi wa yawmil akhari fa kad dalla dalalen baida.
Surah Nisa 136.
Verse Meaning.
O you who believe! Believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down to His Messenger and the Book which He sent down before.
He who denies Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day has gone astray.
Surah Nisa 136.
Exegesis of the Verse.
The sentence "O you who believe... believe" is at first sight a call to believers to believe again.

In order to show that there is no contradiction here, various explanations have been given by the commentators, such as "The purpose is the hypocrites who outwardly appear to be believers", "The second call to faith is a call to continue believing", "Believers are being called to faith in the fullest sense".
We understand the verse as follows: All true religions have a form and subject of belief.
Irreligion and godlessness are also a kind of belief.
In order to correctly determine the form and subject matter of belief, it is obvious that there is a need for a source of knowledge that is not contrary to reason but transcends reason.

This source of knowledge (revelation from God) explains the quality and quantity of a valid faith; it informs those who want to believe, who are inclined to believe, who decide to believe after using their own capacity for knowledge and conviction, what and how believers in this sense should believe; in this sense, it says "believe".

According to the verse, those who lived on the earth after the Qur'an came, and who wish to believe, must believe in Allah, the angels, in the Qur'an and the books that were sent before it (even if they were not preserved as they are now), in the last prophet Muhammad Mustafa and the prophets sent before him, and in the Last Day.

The faith of those who do not believe in even one of these is not valid, and those who deny even one of them are considered to have deviated from the true religion and to have failed to attain the "true, right, valid, saving" faith.
Source : Qur'anic Path Tafsir Volume: 2 Pages: 160-161.

[Esra Büyükcombak] Is it safe to sleep with a phone on your bedside table?
ESRA BÜYÜKCOMBAK Academician (Genetic and Biological Engineering) Cell phones have become indispensable in our daily lives.
We rarely turn off our phone so that we are always reachable, we spend the last minutes before falling asleep on the internet, many of us even keep our cell phone next to our bed while we sleep.
Some of us worry that we won't wake up in the morning before our phone alarm goes off.
There are even people who sleep with a phone under their pillow.
Is there a risk in keeping a cell phone so close at night?
What are the health effects of cell phones?
And how does it affect sleep patterns?
Potentially dangerous waves; Is radiation from cell phones harmful?
Risks and dangers have changed with the development of technology.
The convenience of smartphones, which are now in the palm of your hand, in every moment of your life, brings with it some concerns.
It has been proven that electromagnetic waves emitted from cell phones, which we know have many negative effects, transfer their energy to the tissues they enter and increase their temperature.
What is the effect of these electromagnetic waves?
Cell phones emit small amounts of radiation called radio frequency radiation or radio waves.
This type of radiation is called non-ionizing radiation and is the same type found in FM radio waves and microwaves.
It is different from ionizing radiation from things like X-rays and ultraviolet light.
This type of radiation can chemically damage your DNA and increase your risk of cancer.
The non-ionizing type from phones does not have enough energy to directly damage the DNA in your cells.
There are no direct biologically determined effects of radio frequency radiation absorption in humans.
However, it is still worth noting that those who want to reduce potential risks should avoid keeping their cell phones nearby while sleeping.
Is there a link between cell phones and cancer?
The possible link between cell phones and cancer is controversial.
Many years of research on cell phones and cancer have yielded conflicting results.
Currently, there is no clear consensus on the degree of cancer risk caused by cell phone use.
The primary concern about cell phones and cancer seems to be the development of brain tumors associated with cell phone use.
But members of the International Agency for Research on Cancer, part of the World Health Organization, agree that there are not enough studies on the link between cell phones and cancer cells.
The fact that not enough time has passed to show that it causes an increase in cancer cells does not mean that it does not have any negative effects.
It is therefore recommended to limit the use of cell phones.
Hypervigilance
Your brain is built to be aware of potential dangers in your environment.
Unnecessary sensitivity and agitation are known as hypervigilance.
While hypervigilance is not a diagnosis, it is a symptom that can occur as part of various mental health conditions.
Hypervigilance is associated with anxiety.
When you feel particularly alert, tense or anxious about a situation or event, you may experience high levels of awareness or arousal.
The need to check your phone by keeping it on at night is a sign of constant vigilance.
When you receive a notification, you will be alerted by sounds, lights or vibrations.
This keeps you in a state of hypervigilance, always ready to respond and never completely shutting down.
If persistent, panic attacks or anxiety are inevitable.
Therefore, keeping the phone away at least at night will protect you against these situations.
Blue Light, Circadian Rhythm & Melatonin Production I have already mentioned that your body's circadian rhythm depends on blue light from the sun.
Blue light waves are known as visible high-energy rays.
Blue light waves with short and strong wavelengths vibrate easily.
This vibration also affects visual sharpness and clarity.
This vibration causes many problems such as eye fatigue, sleep disturbances, blurred vision, difficulty focusing, eye dryness and irritation.
Light from phone screens is also known to affect the ability to fall asleep.
Artificial light from screens can cause a delay in the circadian rhythm.
The reason why the light emitted from the cell phone screen reduces sleep time is that it causes day/night confusion in the body and prevents the production of chemicals that help you sleep.
In addition, the blue light emitted by cell phones has a stimulating effect on the body.

Using your phone before bedtime and even in the middle of the night negatively affects the quality of your sleep. A 2018 study found that screen use in the one to two hours before bedtime negatively affects sleep, and this effect is particularly pronounced in young children and adolescents.
Given what smartphones in your pocket can do, it's no surprise that they are in every aspect of your life and at your bedside.
Limiting cell phone use at night and keeping your bed as a comfortable, screen-free zone can help ensure better quality rest.
Getting the sleep your body needs is a critical way to maintain your overall mental and physical health.
If Allah is the one who seals the hearts, what is the fault of the servants?
DR. ALİ DEMİREL- SAMANYOLUHABER.COM Question: "In different verses in the Qur'an, Allah says that He will seal the hearts of some of His servants.
The question inevitably arises in one's mind: "If it is Allah who seals the hearts, then what is the fault of the servants whose hearts are sealed?"
This question was asked by our young brother Ömer Faruk, who expresses that he is very interested in reading, researching and questioning, and adds: "Brother, I wrote this question hesitantly."
On this occasion, I would like to say the following especially to my young brothers and sisters in the person of Ömer Faruk.
The first step that leads to learning and knowing is obvious: Questions.
First, questions arise.
These questions are then pursued and a sweet quest begins.
Eventually we get answers.
Imam al-Ghazali was asked: "How did you reach this level of knowledge?"
"By asking without hesitation what I don't know." he says.
Yes, it is very important to ask questions.
Especially when these questions are questions of faith and worship that concern both our worlds.
So, of course, you can ask any questions you may have and write to us without hesitation.
Now let us move on to the answer to the question: In the Holy Qur'an, as stated in the question, our Lord states that the hearts of some servants will be sealed.
(Al-Baqarah, 2/7) This is true.
However, the "sealing of hearts" mentioned in the Qur'an is not a "sealing" that Allah imposes on His servants out of the blue, unjustly, so to speak.
On the contrary, it is a sealing that takes place as a result of the willful persistence of some servants in sins despite all warnings.
Let's explain a little bit what we mean.
A person's heart is sealed not by an unjust sanction of Allah, but by the person's willful and deliberate persistence in sin.

In this context, the sealing of hearts means the gradual contamination of the heart as a result of persistence in sinning and underestimation of imperfections, and eventually its complete darkening so that there is no longer a bright spot in the heart.
That is, people seal their own hearts as a result of their persistent and deliberate sins.
In one of his hadiths, our Master (s.a.s.) expresses this truth as follows: "When a sin is committed for the first time, a black spot, a black stain, forms in the heart.
If the owner repents, repents and repents, the heart will shine again.
If he does not, and the sin is repeated, the stain increases.
Then it gradually reaches a degree where the stain covers the whole heart like a sheath.
"Nay, what they have earned has put rust on their hearts."
This is the "rayn" in the verse (Mutaffifîn, 83/14)."
(bk.
Tirmidhi, Tafsiru Sûra, 83, 1; Ibn Majah Zuhd 29) Let us illustrate this further with an example.
Imagine a motor made of iron and metal parts.
If this engine is not regularly maintained by its owner, knowingly and willingly, for many years, what will become of it in the end?

This engine, which has not received the maintenance and repair it deserves over the years, and whose worn-out and deteriorated parts have not been replaced, becomes completely rusted and unusable due to lack of maintenance and takes its place in the scrap graveyard.

However, if the owner had taken the necessary precautions and carried out the necessary maintenance before reaching this stage, the engine would still be running instead of being thrown into a scrapyard.
Now let's ask the question: In this case, is it the fault of the person who built the engine that it ended up in a junkyard, or is it the fault of the person who uses it?
The blame, of course, lies with the user of the bike.
Despite the information contained in the engine's user manual and the warnings of the engineers, the user ignored them and prepared the end of the engine with his own hands.
The sealing of the hearts of sinful people is similar to the example of the engine above.
Allah has warned His servants against sins through the Book, the Prophets and the guides He has sent and has always left the door of forgiveness open for those who turn from their sins and repent.
However, if a person continues to sin in spite of all these warnings and advice, gradually the white, bright parts of his heart will also become dirty and darken.
In the end, with his own free will, he seals his own heart so that no white, bright spot remains.
In short, he himself does everything to seal his heart.
Allah will then seal his heart.

Cannabis cannot be cultivated outside the permitted provinces and districts.

200 DECARES OF CANNABIS WERE PLANTED LAST YEAR.

While there are no registered and authorized hemp varieties in Turkey, the cultivation area has declined over the years. The hemp cultivated area, which was 42 thousand decares in 1989, fell to 5 thousand 360 in 1999 and 66 decares in 2009.
Last year, 200 decares of hemp was planted for fiber and seed purposes.

DOMESTIC AND NATIONAL HEMP.

Hemp is used in a wide range of areas such as natural fiber parts in the automobile industry, wood processing industry, natural construction materials from hemp sawdust, wood materials, fabric and canvas products, ship rope, insulation materials, cosmetic products, biodiesel, energy production through biomass, hemp oil, food and feed, paper industry, banknote and cigarette paper, tea bags.

In 1 decare, where 1,500 liras of income is obtained, 800-850 liras are spent.

One thousand 250 to one thousand 500 liras of income is generated, while the expenditure is 800-850 liras.

Precedent decision: WhatsApp correspondence considered as evidence
Last semester, all over the country, within the scope of coronavirus measures, various sectors went into lockdown and interrupted service.
One of these sectors was the accommodation sector.

However, in line with the decision taken by the Ministry of Health, there was an exception for healthcare workers involved in coronavirus treatment and senior citizens living alone and in need of treatment.
Hotels that first went into lockdown and then started to serve health workers and people in need in line with this exception, recalled the staff they had put on leave.
One of these hotels was in Izmir.
A hotel in Izmir decided to reinstate its service in line with this situation and called back its staff on leave via Whatsapp.
While some staff returned to their jobs upon the call, others did not, questioning what health measures were being taken and claiming that the call via WhatsApp was not valid.
HOTEL MANAGEMENT TERMINATED THE WORKERS' EMPLOYMENT CONTRACTS.
After some hotel staff ignored all warnings and did not show up for work, the hotel management terminated their employment contracts.
The dismissed employees took their case to court.
WHATSAPP CORRESPONDENCE AS EVIDENCE.
The final hearing of the lawsuit filed by the terminated employees against the hotel was held in Izmir 5th Civil Court.
Labor Court.
Lawyers from all sides took part in the hearing and defenses were heard.

Following the arguments of the lawyers of the parties, the court panel stated that the Supreme Court of Appeals has stated that 'According to this Law, written or printed texts, deeds, drawings, plans, sketches, photographs, films, video or audio recordings, electronic media data and similar information carriers that are suitable for proving the facts in dispute are documents'.
With this regulation, e-mail correspondence has also been accepted as a document', and considered WhatsApp correspondence as evidence.

The court, which also found that the hotel had taken measures within the scope of corona virus measures and held the orange circle certificate, justified the dismissal of the staff without compensation.
RULED TO HAVE EVIDENTIARY VALUE
Emphasizing the importance of the court's decision, Ali Onar, the lawyer for the hotel, said that it is now indisputable that WhatsApp correspondence is accepted as written evidence in Turkish law.
Lawyer Ali Onar said, "As it is known, some sectors went to closure during the pandemic period.
One of these sectors was the hotel industry.
However, the Ministry of Health has made an exception here.
The Ministry has authorized hotels to provide services to health workers and elderly citizens living alone and in need of treatment.
This was a very useful service.
The hotels that will provide this service have of course canceled their closures and called back their staff.
Our client hotel also notified its staff via WhatsApp and called them back to work.
Following this information and recall, some staff returned to work, but there were also some who did not return to work and did not start work again.
The legal procedure was then followed and the service contracts of the employees were terminated.
Following the termination of their service contracts, a lawsuit was filed against the hotel concerned.
The lawsuit claimed that the necessary precautions were not taken and that the information provided via WhatsApp was not valid.
The trial established two main bases.

One of the main bases was that the measures taken by the hotel were in line with the criteria of the Ministry of Health; in other words, the contract was concluded according to the criteria of the Ministry of Health and that a hotel that had received an orange circle certificate fulfilled occupational health and safety services.

Another important point is that it has been decided that notifications made via WhatsApp are now a valid notification in line with the decisions of the Supreme Court of Appeals and that they are evidence.
From our point of view, in terms of labor law, the court has made a valuable and important decision on two fundamental issues.
The court has thus ruled that the acceptance of WhatApp correspondence as written evidence in Turkish law is now undisputed."

Lawyer Ali Onar stated that the local court made this decision by referring to the precedent decision of the Supreme Court of Appeals and said, "This is a decision made by the local court, but in terms of occupational health and safety, the court made this decision by referring to the decisions of the Supreme Court of Appeals.
In particular, WhatsApp correspondence is one of the decisions that have recently entered our current law.
In terms of occupational health and safety, the court also referred to the decisions of the Court of Cassation in this way, especially by evaluating the pandemic conditions."

March 10, 2021 Regulation on Remote Working in the Official Gazette
The expected regulation on remote working was published in the Official Gazette.
In the regulation prepared by the Ministry of Family, Labor and Social Security, "Employment contracts regarding remote work shall be made in writing.

The contract shall include provisions on the description of the work, the manner in which it is to be performed, the duration and location of the work, wages and matters relating to the payment of wages, work tools and equipment provided by the employer and obligations regarding their protection, the employer's communication with the worker, and general and special working conditions.
Organization of the workspace.
If necessary, arrangements for the location where remote work will be carried out shall be completed before the work begins.
The procedure for meeting the costs arising from these arrangements shall be determined jointly by the remote worker and the employer.
Procurement and use of materials and work tools.

Unless otherwise agreed in the employment contract, it is essential that the materials and work tools required for the production of goods and services by the remote worker are provided by the employer.
The principles of use, maintenance and repair conditions of these materials and work tools shall be clearly and understandably communicated to the remote worker.
If work tools are provided by the employer, a list of work tools indicating their cost on the date they are delivered to the worker shall be delivered to the worker in writing by the employer.
A copy of the document delivered to the worker, signed by the worker, is kept by the employer in the worker's personnel file.
If the list of work tools is issued in the labor contract or as an annex to the labor contract at the date of the contract, it is not required to issue a separate written document.
Covering production costs.

Issues regarding the determination and reimbursement of mandatory expenses directly related to the production of goods or services arising from the fulfillment of the work shall be specified in the employment contract.
Determination of working time.
The time interval and duration of the remote work shall be specified in the employment contract.
Subject to the limitations stipulated in the legislation, working hours may be changed by the parties.
Overtime work is carried out upon the written request of the employer, with the acceptance of the employee, in accordance with the provisions of the legislation.
Communication.
The method and time interval of communication in remote working is determined by the remote worker and the employer.
Data protection.

The employer shall inform the remote worker about the business rules and relevant legislation regarding the protection and sharing of data relating to the workplace and the work performed and shall take the necessary measures to protect such data.
The employer determines the definition and scope of the data to be protected in the contract.
The remote worker must comply with the operating rules set by the employer for data protection purposes.
Taking measures regarding occupational health and safety.

The employer is obliged to inform the employee about occupational health and safety measures, to provide the necessary training, to provide health surveillance and to take the necessary occupational safety measures regarding the equipment provided, taking into account the nature of the work performed by the remote worker.
Jobs where remote work cannot be done.

Remote work cannot be carried out in jobs that involve working with hazardous chemicals and radioactive substances, processing of these substances or working with the wastes of these substances, working processes that involve the risk of exposure to biological agents.

The public institution and organization responsible for the unit, project, facility or service or the public institution and organization receiving the service shall determine which of the works that are outsourced by public institutions and organizations through service procurement in accordance with the relevant legislation and which of the units, projects, facilities or services of strategic importance in terms of national security cannot be teleworked.
Transition to remote working.

The employment relationship can be established directly through a teleworking contract or the employment contract of an employee who is already working at the workplace can be converted into a teleworking contract upon the agreement of the employee and the employer.
The issues related to the employee's request to work remotely are as follows: The request shall be made in writing.
The request is evaluated by the employer in accordance with the procedure determined at the workplace.
While evaluating the request, the suitability of the work and the worker for remote working due to the nature of the work and the worker and other criteria to be determined by the employer are used.
It is essential that the result of the evaluation of the request is notified to the worker within thirty days in the same manner in which the request was made.
If the request is accepted, a contract shall be concluded in accordance with the provisions of Article 5.
The employee who has switched to remote work may request to work at the workplace again in accordance with the procedure set out in the second paragraph.
The employer will prioritize the request.

In the event that remote working will be applied in all or part of the workplace due to compelling reasons specified in the legislation, the request or approval of the employee is not sought for the transition to remote working."

3.5 MILLION VEHICLES ARE SOLD OUT OF REGISTRY! However, according to data from the Istanbul Motor Vehicle Dealers Association (IMAS), of the 6.9 million second-hand vehicles sold, 1 million were duplicate sales, 1 million were made by vehicle owners and 1.5 million by traders.

In other words, 46 percent of the total second-hand sales were reflected in the figures as unregistered.
63 PERCENT INDIVIDUAL.
The informality in the second hand is also revealed when the details of the advertisements published on digital media are analyzed.
Again, according to IMAS data, approximately 37 percent of the second-hand ads published on digital channels belong to merchants, while the remaining 63 percent belong to individual sellers.

'' These works are mostly done on the internet.

Money raised for SMA campaigns also melted against the dollar
Families of children with SMA organize campaigns and try to get treatment abroad.
But the money collected is completely melting against the dollar. 21-month-old Destan is one of them.
They now need 12 million liras for treatment.
Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) is a genetic muscle disease that occurs in children as infants and progresses over time.
There are more than 1,300 children with SMA in Turkey.
In Turkey, the drug "Spinraza 12 Mg/5Ml 1 VIAL", which children should use for life, is used in the treatment of SMA disease.
The families' only hope is gene therapy with the drug Zolgensma, which is not available in Turkey.
Families with children with SMA must pay between $1.8 million and $2.5 million to access gene therapy.
Since it is difficult to raise this money on their own, families are trying to make their voices heard through campaigns.

21-month-old Destan Duru Evren, a 21-month-old SMA Type 2 patient living in the central Yeşilyurt district of Malatya, is one of the children for whom a campaign has been launched for Zolgensma treatment.

Within the scope of the campaign launched 2 months and 16 days ago for 2 million 252 thousand dollars to be used for Evren's treatment, 28 percent of this amount has been collected so far. From 18 million to 30 million.
With the recent fluctuation in the dollar exchange rate, the money collected by the family within the scope of the campaign is melting day by day.
When the campaign for Evren was launched 11 months ago, one dollar was 8.02 TL and 18 million 466 thousand TL was available for the treatment.
Considering that the current exchange rate is 13.53, the amount needed has increased to 30 million 469 thousand TL.
In the past year, the amount to be collected for the Universe has increased by nearly 12 million TL.
His treatment was delayed because the report came late.

Father Sabri Evren, who stated that they realized the health problems when his child was 12 months old, said that the necessary examinations were done late. Stating that the gene report, which should have come in 20 days, was received 4 months later, Evren said, "If the gene report had not come late, we would have started the campaign earlier.
After the report came back, it was understood that he had SMA Type 2. 4 months is our child being dragged to death.
The countdown for Destan Duru started late.
After receiving the gene report, we applied to the governorship and the Ministry of Health for the campaign.
However, the Ministry of Health rejected our application.
After the rejection we were able to start a campaign through the court. We need access to Zolgesma treatment within 2 months.
Destan Duru will not be able to receive treatment if he gains one more kilogram. Within 2 months, if we cannot get Destan Duru to treatment, we will leave her to die."

'We are melting against the dollar' Evren said that the campaign they started 2 months and 16 days ago for treatment is melting against the dollar exchange rate, "When we agreed with a hospital in Dubai for the campaign, the dollar was 8.02 TL.
The dollar melted our campaign.
If the dollar had not risen, our campaign would be close to 60 percent now.
Children with SMA and we are also melting against the dollar."
Let's keep the saga alive.

Reminding that there are more than 50 children who have completed the campaign for Zolgensma treatment and received treatment abroad, Evren said, "Nothing happened to any of the babies who have been there, they are all healthy.
There are positive developments.
The authorities say 'it is not a cure' but the results are obvious.
Everyone can be a breath of fresh air for Destan Duru with 5-10 TL, no matter how little or how much.
Please hear our voice, let's keep Destan Duru alive together."
Mom: I'm going to bed hungry.
Zarife Kılıç Evren, mother of Destan Duru Evren, mentioned that the care of children with SMA is challenging and said, "My daughter did not walk or crawl.
The only treatment for the disease is gene therapy abroad.
Spinraza in Turkey is given with criteria.
We took 4 doses, this does not end the disease, it only slows down its course.
We need everyone's support against the world's most expensive medicine."
Mother Evren stated that Desten Duru was melting in front of her eyes day by day and said the following: "Her muscles are melting day by day.
My child breathes less and less every day.
I put my daughter to bed hungry so she doesn't weigh more than 13 kilos.
This is a very big challenge for me.
No mother wants her child to go hungry.
I have dreams about Destan Duru.
I really want him to go to the park and play and enjoy his childhood.
I want to believe that we are a social state.
For these dreams to come true, we need access to medicine.
Let's keep Destan Duru alive."

The EPKK will include representatives of teachers and students, universities, trade unions, chambers of industry and commerce, representatives from parent organizations, and representatives from civil society organizations such as bar associations.
An effective non-formal education program will be implemented with emphasis on women's education.
In this framework, Public Education Centers will be used more effectively and effective participation of municipalities will be ensured.
In all organizations of the Ministry, the number of female administrators in schools will be increased and a target of 50% will be set.
Teaching will be made a respected and attractive profession through academic, financial, social and administrative arrangements.
Teachers' long-standing problems in terms of salaries, wages, social rights and pension rights will be solved.
The school administration will be divided into a directorate and a head teacher's office, with the head teacher handling the education department and the directorate handling administrative affairs.
Provincial and District Directorates of National Education will be ensured to be guidance authorities in terms of effective execution and quality of education.
Educational institutions and staff will be inspected in terms of guidance and supervision within the framework of scientific principles.
Care will be taken to ensure that students use Turkish correctly, fluently and beautifully.
In addition, all students will be given the opportunity to learn at least one foreign language during their compulsory education.

Turkish will be used beautifully at an aesthetic level in mass media, science, art, commerce and all other areas of life; every effort will be made together with stakeholder institutions and organizations to make Turkish the language of science and communication as well as to make our terms and concepts dominant.
Language pollution will be prevented.
Other non-formal and formal education opportunities, such as student exchange programs, will be increased for Turkish children living abroad to preserve and develop their cultural identity.
Necessary support will be provided for the teaching of Turkish and Turkish Culture courses as elective courses in good relations and mutual understanding with the relevant countries.

A new curriculum program will be adopted that includes life subjects such as basic computer programming, financial literacy, political/legal literacy, oratory, manual skills, and coding and programming courses at all levels starting from primary school.
It will be ensured that arts and sports are actively part of students' lives at all levels of education.
Care will be taken to ensure that every student who completes compulsory education is interested in at least one branch of sport.
A lifelong education approach will be adopted and parents will be trained in child care and education through the "Every home will be a school" project.
Guidance and guidance services will be provided to all children, especially parents, from pre-school onwards.
The number of scientific, social and cultural venues such as science centers, museums, botanical and zoological gardens will be increased and their effective use as learning spaces will be ensured.
Our main objective is to reduce budget deficits to a sustainable level in the short term and to prevent structural and permanent deficits in the medium and long term.
Public expenditures need to support the economy in times of cyclical recession to ensure economic stability.
On the other hand, we aim for a budget surplus in times of high growth.
By subjecting public finance to a comprehensive reform, we will ensure the most efficient management of public resources.
To achieve this goal, on the revenue side, we will expand the tax base through effective tax audits while implementing reforms to ensure tax justice.
We will radically reform the tax system based on the fact that a prosperous society cannot be achieved without ensuring tax justice.
The share of indirect taxes in total tax revenues will be gradually reduced to the OECD average.
The tax burden of workers, civil servants, tradesmen and small businesses, especially low-income citizens, will be reduced.
First of all, we will abolish all taxes and deductions on the minimum wage.
The tax burden of small tradesmen and businesses will be reduced by simplifying the tax burden and legislation.
It will be ensured that taxation is predictable and related practices are regular.

On the expenditure side, we will put an end to the unregulated and wasteful spending regime observed in the budget and emphasize infrastructure, agriculture and industrial investments that provide added value and high positive externalities to the national economy, especially in investment items.
Public education and health services will be of private sector quality and free of charge.
The resources required for this purpose will be allocated by taking into account service quality, efficiency and regional imbalances.
We will make the Court of Accounts, one of the constitutional institutions for auditing budget expenditures, operational again.
Public interest, justice, fairness, transparency and accountability will be urgently established as the main principles in budget expenditures.
Due to its geography, our country is located in a region that is intertwined with complex problems in which energy policies are at the core.
These problems make it necessary to consider "energy policies" as important as national security policies and economic and social policies.
Our main priority for our energy market is to ensure security of energy supply and minimize our dependence on foreign energy.
Priority will be given to domestic and renewable resources, aiming to reduce external dependency in energy.

Arrangements will be made that prioritize environmentally friendly technologies, that envisage decision-making not at the center but on the ground and with public participation, that prioritize not only macro and large-scale projects but also micro-scale projects.

Regulations that pave the way for applications that will enable individuals to install, electricity and natural gas storage projects that are in favor of using energy efficiently rather than consuming it, and the allocation of R&D resources in cooperation with universities for the development of alternative energy resources will be prepared by meritorious staff and implemented immediately.
Our goal is to deliver quality, timely, sufficient, cheap and uninterrupted energy to users.
Illegal use of energy will be prevented, efficiency will be increased, and cheap and quality energy will be provided to consumers.
Our domestic and renewable resources such as water, wind, geothermal, geothermal, wave, hydrogen and solar energy will be utilized at the highest level.
Electricity generation with rooftop energy panels will be popularized.
Efforts to identify our coal resources will continue and appropriate technological solutions will be required for the utilization of coal in electricity generation.

In addition to being a terminal country enabling the transit of energy between energy producing and consuming countries, Turkey will be ensured to be one of the important actors in the market with the technology and infrastructure to produce energy products with high added value.

Except for the critically important dammed/storage water power plants owned by the State Electricity Generation Company (EÜAŞ), other power plants will be privatized by providing the necessary competitive conditions.
Audit activities on electricity and gas distribution companies will be carried out thoroughly.
Electricity, natural gas and petroleum transmission lines will be operated efficiently and efficiently within the scope of the country's major infrastructure projects.
Energy bureaucracy will be redesigned and dual-headedness and multiple permitting/approval processes will be eliminated.
Natural gas will be delivered to all our districts for heating.
Interconnection capacity with neighboring countries will be increased and technical and commercial opportunities will be improved.
The National Plan will be prepared in cooperation with universities, OIZs and SMEs, and its execution and updating will be carried out in consultation with the parties.
Fuel smuggling will be effectively combated, and the revenues to be obtained in this way will be used to reduce fuel consumption tax rates, thus enabling consumers to consume fuel at cheaper prices.
Biodiesel production will be encouraged.
Energy knowledge and its importance will enter the curriculum at High School level.
Principles of Our Economic Policy.
Stable and employment-friendly growth.

Our economic policy is based on preventing monopolistic formations and unfair competition by operating the rules of the market economy, limiting the role of the public sector in the economy with guiding, regulatory and supervisory activities, and realizing a stable, environmentally sensitive and employment-friendly growth that supports the dynamism and entrepreneurial power of the private sector.
A production economy with global competitiveness.

We consider it necessary to be among the leading determinants of regional and global developments by integrating with the world economy in an open and competitive structure; to support the production of information as a requirement of the information age, to realize the most effective use of information by providing fast and easy access to information; to establish a production economy based on technological development, innovation, productivity and employment instead of a rent-based consumption economy that provides easy and speculative gains.
Monetary policy and price stability.

Achieving and maintaining price stability is essential for realizing sustainable growth. To this end, we envisage pursuing a monetary and exchange rate policy that will reduce the debt stock and the current account deficit to levels that will not cause vulnerability in the economy.

While we accept the free exchange rate policy, in which exchange rates are determined according to market conditions, we believe that excessive fluctuations and speculative movements in exchange rates should be prevented in the short term.
An industry with international competitiveness will be created.

An industry that mobilizes local resources, employs a qualified workforce, uses and produces advanced technology, develops original designs and brands, observes consumer health and preferences, produces in accordance with environmental norms, envisages technological innovation, increases productivity and has international competitiveness will be established.
Emphasis will be given to the production of high value-added products in sectors with high growth, employment and export capacities.
Industrial investments that will reduce import dependency and mobilize domestic capabilities will be supported.
Turkey will become an important regional and global production center in sectors with medium and high level production technologies.
Breakthroughs will be made in the defense and aerospace, machinery manufacturing, chemical, electronics and software industries.

The defense industry, which is of great importance for our country both in terms of security and economy, will be transformed into a structure capable of producing technology and integrated with other industries.

Emphasis will be given to the development of the electronics industry and the software sector and to the development of new products in priority areas that will provide high added value based on knowledge.
Emphasis will be given to the production, development, transfer and utilization of microelectronics-based information technologies.
Democratic and virtuous generations will be raised.

The main objective of our education policy is to raise generations who are proud and conscious of belonging to the Turkish nation, who have internalized our spiritual and cultural values, who have developed thinking, perception and problem solving skills, who are open to new developments, who have a high sense of responsibility and social sensitivity, who are prone to science and technology production, who are entrepreneurial, democratic, cultured and faithful.

Equality of opportunity and opportunity shall be ensured in education and training, and it shall be essential that all members of society are educated in line with their interests, tendencies and abilities.
We see the training of a workforce that is sensitive to labor demand and has the necessary equipment and skill flexibility as a strategic element to achieve the goal of a leading country.
At all levels of education, the language of instruction shall be Turkish, and no mother tongue instruction shall be provided in any language other than Turkish.
In order to ensure the correct and beautiful use of Turkish, importance will be given to teaching Turkish well in kindergarten and primary education.
In addition, the infrastructure for teaching at least one foreign language to students in a good way will be created.
Students will be provided with computer-assisted recognition and guidance services.

In primary education, student recognition techniques will be developed through computer-assisted "guidance" and effective guidance will be provided through skill-based assessment methods, and elective courses will be emphasized from the sixth and seventh grades onwards in order to help reveal talents and guide students towards a profession.
Gifted and talented students will be provided with special education opportunities.
It will be ensured that high achieving secondary school students continue their university education without exams and with state scholarships according to their interests, wishes and abilities.

Individuals in need of special education will be identified, classified, special education institutions will be expanded and supervised, and education programs will be re-evaluated according to the needs of the day.
Special education services will be expanded to cover pre-school education, primary education, secondary education, higher education and adults.
Importance will be given to training special education teachers and auxiliary personnel.
Vocational education will be emphasized.

In order to train the intermediate manpower needed by the economy, emphasis will be given to formal and non-formal vocational-technical education and skill-building education, and education programs will be reorganized based on occupational standards.
The share of vocational education that increases employability in secondary education will be increased.
Program integrity will be ensured between vocational and technical secondary education institutions and vocational schools.
Relationship, communication and interaction between business life and vocational and technical education will be improved.
Higher education will be brought to a level that can compete with world universities.

It will be essential to transform universities into educational institutions that train the manpower our country needs, produce science and technology through research, lead social development, find solutions to problems with scientific methods, and compete with world universities.
Specialization of universities in line with the potentials of the regions where they are located will be ensured.
Private university establishment will be encouraged by establishing an effective quality assessment and supervision system.

In order to train university lecturers and scientists domestically, universities will be specialized in master's and doctoral programs and the necessary technical and academic infrastructure will be established.
OUR MAIN OBJECTIVES AND VIEWS: Unconscious migration will be prevented: To develop projects that will stop the phenomenon of unconscious and uncontrolled migration and encourage living in place.

Medium-sized provinces with potential in the fields of industry and services will be identified and the infrastructure needs of these provinces, which are functional regional centers, such as drinking water, sewerage, housing and transportation will be met rapidly and a suitable investment environment will be created for the private sector.
Migration from rural areas to big cities will be kept in these centers and on-site employment will be provided.
In order to prevent urban agglomeration and unplanned construction due to industrialization and migration, the relationship between urbanization rate and land supply will be established.
Security problems arising from unhealthy structures and urbanization caused by migration will be eliminated.

Although globalization is said to offer opportunities in terms of spreading and developing democracy, ensuring the rule of law, and securing fundamental rights and freedoms on the grounds of establishing the common welfare and happiness of humanity, this process has become associated with problems such as international terrorism, migration, ethnic conflicts, civil unrest, regional conflicts, double standards contrary to international law, hunger and impoverishment, the growing gap between rich and poor countries, and environmental disasters.
The salaries of village and neighborhood mukhtars will be raised to at least the minimum wage, taking into account criteria such as the administrative structure and population of the settlement.
The increase in the minimum wage based on the minimum standard of living will be reflected in the amount of family insurance benefit.

A social welfare order will be established By establishing a stable economic growth and a strong production economy, a social welfare order will be established that produces, creates employment and ensures that all segments involved in this process receive a fair share of the value produced in proportion to their contribution, and that the needy who are not involved in the production process are supported by social protection programs and are lifted out of poverty.

For this purpose, a favorable investment climate will be created in which private enterprise can take long-term investment decisions, small and medium-sized enterprises will be supported, and investments by foreign direct capital to create added value and employment will be encouraged.

The essence of our social welfare policy will primarily consist of permanently lifting poor people out of poverty, leaving no citizen below the poverty line, and improving the quality of life of citizens by raising the welfare level of society.
Economic and social policies will be implemented in harmony in a way to support those on low and fixed incomes and a balanced distribution of income will be ensured.
Public-private sector cooperation will be developed to reduce regional development disparities and mobilize local production potential.
In the fight against poverty, it will be essential to bring the poor into a productive position.
The fight against poverty will be aimed at preventing the formation of a charity economy and a culture of poverty, and ensuring that the poor become producers and live off their own earnings.

Income-generating projects will be supported by diversifying economic activities for the poor, and entrepreneurs who will start their own businesses will be provided with financing, consultancy and marketing support.
Those who are employed but poor or at risk of impoverishment will also benefit from social support payments.
The rent economy, which provides easy profits and does not provide employment, will be put an end to and resources will be used in a way that encourages production.

The tax base will be broadened, the tax burden of the poor will be eased, and transfer policies will be implemented to ensure that the poor and those at risk of impoverishment receive a larger share of national income.
Supportive arrangements will be made to increase social welfare.

In order to lift out of poverty those who are most affected by poverty, those with low level of education, engaged in agriculture and forestry, working as self-employed and casual workers, will be provided with the opportunity to be employed in non-agricultural sectors through vocational training and skill acquisition programs.
Basic needs, education, health and social services will be made accessible and available to the poor.
